<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/10251> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A graphic representation of a city area or other densely populated region, portraying the location of groups or select types of people in their environment through various geographic techniques."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/10256> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Unified, combined and coordinated management of environmental problems which correlates relevant organisations, groups, individuals and disciplines by bringing the parts together for a complete approach."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/10274> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "An organized, systematic effort through various communications media to alert the general population of a given area to anything of significant interest or concern."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1028> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any of the suborder Heteroctera, having piercing and sucking mouthparts, specialized as a beak."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1039> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The art and technique of building houses."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1041> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Area of land suitable for building on."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1042> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any material used in construction, such as steel, concrete, brick, masonry, glass, wood, etc."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/10444> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Horned ruminant mammals raised in many breeds for wool, edible flesh, or skin."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1046> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The activity of designing, organizing or preparing for future construction or reconstruction of edifices and facilities."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/10495> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Cover or protection, as from weather or danger; place of refuge."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/10510> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Line corridors (roads, paths, and hedgerows) which lack interior habitat but may serve as movement groups for organisms. Corridors may also provide an efficient migratory pathway for animals. The presence or absence of breaks in a corridor may be a very important factor in determining the effectiveness of its conduit and barrier functions."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/10511> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Harm caused to the environment by animals as, for instance, in the case of overgrazing, trampling, etc. Overgrazing damage is reduced by properly located watering facilities to decrease daily travel by livestock. Rotation of grazing areas allows time for recovery of grass. Some land can be easily restored if grazing is allowed only during one season. Animals may cause damage to crops when agriculture land borders on virgin territory or game reserves. In addition wild animals may bring disease in valuable domestic herds. Cattle overstocking has caused serious degradation of habitat, and cattle raising is thus, to some extent, counterproductive."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/10512> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The habit of many animal species of moving inside their habitats or of travelling, during migrations, to different biotopes, often considerable distances apart; in aquatic environments displacements can occur horizontally or vertically while in terrestrial environments animal populations that breed in the alpine or subalpine zones in summer, move to lower levels in winter; animal displacements usually follow circadian rhythms and are related to the necessity of finding breeding, resting and feeding areas."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/10539> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A group of animals inhabiting a given area."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/10548> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any of various processes, either sexual or asexual, by which an animal produces one or more individuals similar to itself."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/10554> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The act or fact of surviving or condition of having survived."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/10562> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Species native to, and restricted to, a particular geographical region."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/10568> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Deciduous tree which has wide leaves, as opposed to the needles on conifers."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/10617> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Plant with elongated, planar, green leaves which measure up to 1,5 m. The flowers come out in the autumn but not every year. The fruits are dark balls, which one often finds washed up on beaches after storms. The same happens with the leaves which wilt and separate from the plant at the end of summer. It grows on sandy substrates, and has a rhizome from which several plants grow. The compact form of its growths retains the sediments pulled by the currents along the sea bed. Neptunegrass forms extensive prairies, always on the continental shelf. The plant's presence, apart from constituting an excellent refuge and food reserve for many species, gives an indication of the maturity and good condition of the whole marine ecosystem."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1061> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Collection of open and/or closed drains, together with structures and pumps used to collect and dispose of excess surface or subsurface water."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/10633> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The number of plants in an area."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/10640> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Collection of trees from different parts of the world, grown for scientific study."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/10651> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Areas for the conservation of rare or endangered animal species."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/10652> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Gardens for the conservation of rare species of plants."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/10667> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The sum of the earth's or a particular region's herb, vegetable, shrub and tree life viewed as the inheritance of the present generation, especially plant species deemed worthy of preservation and protection from extinction."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/10671> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Attempts made to prevent the extinction of threatened species and populations by reintroducing them in their natural habitat. The reintroduction of species in a region requires a preliminary study to establish the reasons of their disappearance and the modifications that might have occurred in the biotopes."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/10692> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Forests have been exploited over the centuries as a source of wood and for obtaining land for agricultural use. The mismanagement of forest lands and forest resources has led to a situation where the forest is now in rapid retreat. The main aspects of the situation are: serious shortages in the supply of industrial wood; the catastrophic erosion and floods accompanying the stripping of forests from mountainous land; the acute shortages of fuel wood in much of the developing world; the spread of desert conditions at an alarming rate in the arid and semi-arid regions of the world; and the many environmental effects of the destruction of tropical rainforests."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/10693> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "An extensive area of woodland that is found at natural elevations usually higher than 2000 feet."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/10695> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Type of forest found in the Mediterranean area comprising mainly xerophilous evergreen trees."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/10698> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Forest whose trees are all in the adult stage and have reached the reproductive period."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/10699> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A low evergreen shrub formation, usually found on siliceous soils in the Mediterranean lands where winter rainfall and summer drought are the characteristic climate features. It consists of a profusion of aromatic species, such as lavender, myrtle, oleander and rosemary and often includes abundant spiny shrubs. It has been suggested that the maquis is a secondary vegetation, occupying the lands cleared of their natural evergreen oak forests by human activity."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/10706> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Branch of forestry concerned with the prevention and control of damage to forests arising from the action of people or livestock, of pests and abiotic agents."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/10711> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A traditional system of woodland management whereby timber trees are grown above a coppiced woodland. It is used in particular as a method of exploiting oakwoods, in which all the trees except a rather open network of tall, well-formed oaks - the standards at about fifty per hectare - are felled, leaving plenty of space for hazels and other underwood to grow and be coppiced at intervals of ten to fifteen years."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/10726> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Large wild animals that weigh typically more than 30 lb when fully grown, hunted for food, sport or profit."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/10744> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Raising of shellfish in inland waters, estuaries or coastal waters, for commercial purposes. All commercial shellfish beds producing bivalve molluscs must be monitored for microbial contamination. Samples of water and shellfish flesh must be tested for the presence of algal toxins. Periodic monitoring of fish and shellfish must be carried out to check for the presence of contaminants."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1075> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The multiplication of or concentration of power in administrators and administrative offices in an organization, usually resulting in an extension into and regimentation of certain areas of social life."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/10773> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A test given to a candidate for a certificate or a position and concerned typically with problems to be solved, skills to be demonstrated, or tasks to be performed."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/10780> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any education, instruction or discipline occurring at the beginning of an activity, task, occupation or life span."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1082> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A large, long-bodied motor vehicle equipped with seating for passengers, usually operating as part of a scheduled service."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/10837> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The coordination or structuring of work practices and production processes in order to influence the way jobs are designed and performed in the workplace."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/10847> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A building containing a swimming pool and a large room or other places where you can play sports."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1084> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The activity, position or site associated with commerce or the earning of a livelihood."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/10884> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "An established or selected course for travel consisting, typically, of secondary roads with significant scenic, cultural, historic, geological or natural features and including vistas, rest areas, and interpretive sites matching the scenic characteristics of the course."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/10890> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A private, non-profit facility where plants and animals can be viewed in a natural outdoor setting."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/10898> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Provision of accommodation for rest or for residence in a room or rooms or in a dwelling place."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/10904> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The community or people in general or a part or section of the community grouped because of a common interest or activity."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/10906> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A route or track running along the coast."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/10907> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A guided trail, designed to explain to children a piece of countryside, the type of soil, flora, fauna, etc. Such trails may be self-guiding, using either explanatory notices set up at intervals or numbered boards referring to a printed leaflet: in other cases parties may be led by a demonstrator or warden."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/10911> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Resort where sports held in the open air on snow or ice, especially skiing are practiced."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/10925> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The act of assigning various hours of one's day, week or year to particular activities, especially those falling within the categories of work and leisure."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1092> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A tiny, circular battery made for a watch or for other microelectric applications."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/10933> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "External conditions or surroundings in which people live or work."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/10935> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A product life cycle includes the following phases: acquisition of raw materials, production, packaging, distribution, use, recyling, and disposal."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/10936> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A mark, seal or written identification attached or affixed to products that provides specific ecological information allowing consumers to make comparisons with other similar products, or instructions on how to safely use or properly recycle or dispose of both products and packaging."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/10971> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Study of the effects of social structure on cognition and behavior, of processes of face-to-face interaction, and of the negotiation of social order."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/10972> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A system of values, ideas and practices established to orient individuals in their community and culture and to provide them with naming, classification and communication codes."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/10980> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The legal right of access to administrative documents or the opportunity to avail oneself of the same."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/10988> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The skill, knowledge, qualification, capacity or authority associated with the chief of an administrative department or other high ranking official selected by the head of state."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1098> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Strands of insulated electrical conductors laid together, usually around a central core, and wrapped in a heavy insulation."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11016> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A design, scheme or project pertaining to the production, distribution and use of income, wealth and commodities."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11031> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Economic, military, technical or financial aid or support given to nations or countries in need, often from other governments or international or intergovernmental organizations."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11034> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Organised method of recording all business transactions in the national economy."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11035> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A separate financial record or statement that discloses financial activity in a particular area and supplements existing financial records."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11044> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Monetary resources set aside for some purpose."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11046> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "An international organization established in 1944, affiliated with the United Nations that acts as an international bank facilitating the exchange of national currencies and providing loans to member nations. It also evaluates the performance of the economies of the world's countries."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11057> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The periodic or continuous verification of the accounts, assets and liabilities of a company or other organization, often to confirm compliance with legal and professional standards."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11061> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Evaluation of the natural structures, resources and landscapes to ensure their careful management and preservation."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11063> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The value or the amount of money exchanged for the production and sustained supply of water."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11069> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A type of leadership and management style attempting to gain the loyalty and support of subordinates by excessively providing for their needs and interests."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11070> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Securities held for the production of income in the form of interest and dividends with the aim of controlling or reducing pollution or substances in the environment deemed harmful to human health and natural resources."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11073> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A prize or bonus given as an inducement or reward for efforts to reduce the presence of pollution or substances in the environment deemed harmful to human health or natural resources."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11082> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Applying a monetary rate or value at which water can be bought or sold."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11095> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A stage of growth or advancement in any aspect of a community that is defined by or restricted to a particular and usually small district or area."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11097> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The gathering and studying of data to determine the projection of demand for an item or service."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11100> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Trade which is unimpeded by tariffs, import and export quotas and other measures which obstruct the free movement of goods and services between states."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11103> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "One of the world's poorest nations, typically small in area and population, with low per capita incomes, literacy levels and medical standards, subsistence agriculture and a lack of exploitable minerals and competitive industries."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11106> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The connections, associations or involvement of developed nations, found predominantly in the Northern Hemisphere, with developing nations, found predominantly in the Southern Hemisphere."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1111> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A malleable silvery-white metallic element of the alkaline hearth group; the fifth most abundant element in the earth crust, occurring especially as forms of calcium carbonate. It is an essential constituent of bones and teeth and is used as a deoxidizer in steel."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11124> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A list of record surrogates arranged in order of some attribute expressible in machine-orderable form."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11127> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "An ordered sequence of data samples in numerical form used to predict or demonstrate trends through time and space."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1112> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Amount of calcium contained in a solution."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11130> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The amount of change in some quantity during a time interval divided by the length of the time interval."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11134> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "An organized group of persons elected or appointed to discuss scientific matters."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11146> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Research directed toward using knowledge gained by basic research to make things or to create situations that will serve a practical or utilitarian purpose."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11148> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Systematic investigation to establish facts or principles concerning a specific scientific subject."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11159> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any course destined to promote economic growth, modernization, increase in agricultural production and the creation of a framework in which to fulfill primary needs, such as education, health and supply of water in the rural areas. The attainment of such objectives depends in general on the type of administrative systems proposed for the various programmes and on the national political situation as regards, for instance land tenure, agrarian reform, the disbursement of assistance and food policy."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11178> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The business of growing fruit and vegetables on a commercial scale."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11187> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Removal of heavy metals from water by the employment of plants or treatment by which plant organisms act to degrade hazardous organic contaminants or transform hazardous inorganic contaminants to environmentally safe levels in soils, subsurface materials, water, sludges, and residues."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11199> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The seasonal migration of livestock to suitable grazing grounds."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11204> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The removal of water from a marshy area by artificial means, e.g. the introduction of drains."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11211> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Fertilizer compound or mixture containing available (soluble) phosphate; examples are phosphate rock (phosphorite), superphosphates or triple superphosphates, nitrophosphate, potassium phosphate, or N-P-K mixtures."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1121> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Guarded area equipped with sanitary facilities where holiday-makers may pitch a tent and camp by paying a daily rate."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11224> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The removal of water or any soluble constituents from the soil. Leaching often occurs with soil constituents such as nitrate fertilizers with the result that nitrates end up in potable waters."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11234> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The monetary or material worth at which buyers and sellers agree to do business for agricultural goods and services."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11243> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The activity or process of overseeing and preparing for the future physical arrangement and condition of any agricultural or pastoral area, which may involve protecting and developing natural and human resources that affect an area's economic vitality."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11244> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The administration, promotion, organization and planning for the business or industry of providing information, transportation, entertainment, accommodations and other services to travelers or visitors."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11246> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any entity or group of individuals involved with the creation, management and conservation of an extensive area of woodland, often to produce products and benefits such as timber, clean water, biodiversity and recreation."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11248> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A formulated or systematic method for the supply of material necessities such as tools, gear, provisions or furnishings."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11269> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A place along a route or line at which a train stops to pick up or let off passengers or goods, especially with ancillary buildings and services."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11289> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The science or art of conducting ships or aircraft from one place to another, esp. the method of determining position, course, and distance travelled over the surface of the earth by the principles of geometry and astronomy and by reference to devices (as radar beacons or instruments) designed as aids."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11294> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Transportation of persons and goods by means of ships travelling along fixed navigation routes."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/112> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Generally, any formal official imposition of penalty or fine; destruction, taking, seizure, or withholding of property; assessment of damages, reimbursement, restitution, compensation, costs, charges or fees; requirement, revocation or suspension of license; and taking other compulsory or restrictive action by organization, agency or its representative."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1130> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any malignant cellular tumour including carcinoma and sarcoma. It encompasses a group of neoplastic diseases in which there is a transformation of normal body cells into malignant ones, probably involving some change in the genetic material of the cells, possibly as a result of faulty repair of damage to the cell caused by carcinogenic agents or ionizing radiation."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11312> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "An unattached dwelling unit inhabited by an adult person plus one or more related persons."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11322> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The activity or process of preparing for the future arrangement and condition of an urban center, particularly the development of its physical lay-out, which would include the construction, reconstruction, conversion, alteration or enlargement of buildings and other structures, and the extension or use of undeveloped land."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11333> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Areas that are subject to the pre-emption right which is a privilege accorded by the government to the actual settler upon a certain limited portion of the public domain, to purchase such tract at a fixed price to the exclusion of all other applicants."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11359> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Branch of engineering dealing with the form and functions of urban areas."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11375> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The accurate reestablishment of the form and details of a building, its artifacts, and the site on which it is located, usually as it appeared at a particular time."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11427> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A declaration made in a prescribed form before a justice of the peace, notary public, or other person authorized to administer an oath."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11472> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Rules concerning the movement of goods or persons by sea, railway or road."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11478> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The moral, legal or ethical claims of posterity on present people, based on the recognition that the young and unborn are vulnerable to contemporary decision-making, especially decisions having long-term effect on the societies and environment they inherit."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11479> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Rights recognized and protected by law, pertaining to the members of a state."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11489> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Factual information, advice or a written warning communicated to a person by an authorized source, often conveyed because of a legal or administrative rule requiring transmission of such information to all concerned parties."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1148> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A four-wheeled motor vehicle used for land transport, usually propelled by a gasoline or diesel internal combustion engine."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11498> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The education, instruction, or discipline pertaining to or connected with the mechanical or industrial arts and the applied sciences."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11508> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The form in which proposed statutes, resolutions or special acts are introduced into a legislative body, before they are enacted or passed."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11524> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Generally, land and water owned by individuals or corporations as opposed to the state; in French civil law, any government property capable of being owned by non-public entities, which cannot be seized and which is restricted to the stipulated ownership and use."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11526> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "eas or ocean areas owned by the state as opposed to individuals or corporations."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11531> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "An investigation, especially a formal one conducted into a matter of public utility by a body constituted for that purpose by a government, local authority, or other organization."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11535> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The power or authority of a government to regulate or command industry, organizations, programs, initiatives and individuals."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11536> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The rights of use over the property of another; a burden on a piece of land causing the owner to suffer access by another."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11583> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The correct application of law as opposed to arbitrariness."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11587> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A judicial examination and determination of issues between parties to action; whether they need issues of law or of fact. A judicial examination, in accordance with law of the land, of a cause, either civil or criminal, of the issues between the parties, whether of law or fact, before a court that has proper jurisdiction."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11594> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "An organ of the government, belonging to the judicial department, whose function is the application of the laws to controversies brought before it and the public administration of justice. The presence of a sufficient number of the members of such a body regularly convened in an authorized place at an appointed time, engaged in the full and regular performance of its functions. A body in the government to which the administration of justice is delegated. A body organized to administer justice, and including both judge and jury. An incorporeal, political being, composed of one or more judges, who sit at fixed times and places, attended by proper officers, pursuant to lawful authority, for the administration of justice. An organized body with defined powers, meeting at certain times and places for the hearing and decision of causes and other matters brought before it, and aided in this, its proper business, by its proper officers, attorneys and counsel to present and manage the business, clerks to record and attest its acts and decisions, and ministerial officers to execute its commands, and secure due order in its proceedings."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1159> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any of the group of organic compounds composed of carbon, hydrogen and oxygen, including sugars, starches and celluloses."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1160> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A nonmetallic element existing in the three crystalline forms: graphite, diamond and buckminsterfullerene: occurring in carbon dioxide, coal, oil and all organic compounds."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11611> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any agreement which gives rise to relationship of landlord and tenant (real property) or lessor and lessee (real or personal property). Contract for exclusive possession of lands or tenements for determinate period. Contract for possession and profits of lands and tenements either for life, or for certain period of time, or during the pleasure of the parties."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11618> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The approval given by the judge of certain acts and agreements for the purpose of rendering them more binding and executory."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11623> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The right of first refusal to purchase land in the event that the grantor of the right should decide to sell."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11635> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The sea and the atmosphere are fluids in contact with one another, but in different energy states - the liquid and the gaseous. The free surface boundary between them inhibits, but by no means totally prevents, exchange of mass and energy between the two. Almost all interchanges across this boundary occur most effectively when turbulent conditions prevail. A roughened sea surface, large differences in properties between the water and the air, or an unstable air column that facilitates the transport of air volumes from sea surface to high in the atmosphere. Both heat and water (vapor) tend to migrate across the boundary in the direction from sea to air. Heat is exchanged by three processes: radiation, conduction, and evaporation. The largest net exchange is through evaporation, the process of transferring water from sea to air by vaporization of the water."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11636> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Uncontrolled movement, caused by percolation or other processes, of liquid or gaseous polluting materials from an original source area into other parts of an ecosystem."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11639> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Contamination of water, soil and air with pathogen bacteria."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11644> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Pollution caused by animal or plant material derived from living and dead organisms that may contain pathogenic bacteria and negatively influences the environment."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11647> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Pollution by toxic substances that produce a harmful effect on living organisms by physical contact, ingestion, or inhalation."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11649> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The discharge, dumping or emission of wastes below the surface of the soil."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1164> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The cycle of carbon in the biosphere, in which plants convert carbon dioxide to organic compounds that are consumed by plants and animals, and the carbon is returned to the biosphere in inorganic form by processes of respiration and decay."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11661> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Measures taken in advance to prevent the occurrence of disasters or similar emergencies."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11662> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any precautionary action, procedure or installation conceived or undertaken to guard or defend from harm persons, property or the environment."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11671> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "High degree of ionization of an acid in water solution."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11675> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The presence in the environment of living organisms or agents derived by viruses, bacteria, fungi, and mammal and bird antigens that can cause many health effects."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11676> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The addition or presence of chemicals to, or in, another substance to such a degree as to render it unfit for its intended purpose. Also refers to the result(s) of such an addition or presence."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11692> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any tiny or very small mass of material that has a definite volume and shape and resists forces that would alter its volume or shape."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11713> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Herbicide belonging to the triazine group, widely employed and particularly in maize crops. It is highly toxic for phytoplancton and freshwater algae and, being highly soluble in water, it easily contaminates aquifers."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11734> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A gas at ordinary temperatures; produces an orange-red deposit when cooled to temperatures of liquid air; prepared by passing an electric discharge through a mixture of sulfur vapor and sulfur dioxide at low temperature."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11745> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Chemical compound belonging to the polychlorinated biphenyls family, used in the production of electrical equipment which requires dielectric fluid such as power transformers and capacitors, as well as in hydraulic machinery, vacuum pumps, compressors and heat-exchanger fluids."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11779> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The amount of carbon covalently bound in organic compounds in a water sample."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11782> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Tests, examinations or evaluations performed in a laboratory."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11788> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The amount of oxygen dissolved in a stream, river or lake is an indication of the degree of health of the stream and its ability to support a balanced aquatic ecosystem. The oxygen comes from the atmosphere by solution and from photosynthesis of water plants. The maximum amount of oxygen that can be held in solution in a stream is termed the saturation concentration and, as it is a function of temperature, the greater the temperature, the less the saturation amount. The discharge of an organic waste to a stream imposes an oxygen demand on the stream. If there is an excessive amount of organic matter, the oxidation of waste by microorganisms will consume oxygen more rapidly than it can be replenished. When this happens, the dissolved oxygen is depleted and results in the death of the higher forms of life."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11789> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The capability of being decomposed by prolonged exposure to light."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11791> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Substance incapable of forming a solution, especially in water."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11792> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Substance that is not capable of changing from a solid or liquid form to a vapour."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11794> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A substance capable of readily changing from a solid or liquid form to a vapour; having a high vapour pressure and a low boiling point."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11809> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "1) The determination of the different grain size in a granular material.\n2) The proportion by weight of particles of different sizes in granular material."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11813> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A substance characterized by definite molecular composition."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11814> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Material having the ability to generate a sufficient concentration of combustible vapors to produce a flame, if ignited."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1181> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Test for assessing if a chemical or physical agent increases the risk of cancer. The three major ways of testing for carcinogens are animals tests, epidemiological studies and bacterial tests."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11836> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Those structures, including the heart and blood vessels, which provide channels for the flow of blood."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1190> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A geographical region bordered on the south by South America and Panama, and on the west by Central America, and consisting of the West Indian, and nearby, islands and the Caribbean Sea, a part of the western Atlantic Ocean."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11912> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A motion, usually unintentional and often undesirable, of parts of machines and structures."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/11> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Physical, chemical and other non-living environmental factors. They are essential for living plants and animals of an ecosystem, providing the essential elements and nutrients that are necessary for growth. The abiotic elements also include the climatic and pedologic components of the ecosystem."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/12008> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Particulate matter suspended in the air. The particulate matter may be in the form of dusts, fumes, or mist. Aerosols in the atmosphere are the form in which pollutants such as smoke are dispersed."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/12013> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Reduction of tree population in forests caused by acidic precipitation, forest fires, air pollution, deforestation, pests and diseases of trees, wildlife, etc."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/12017> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A colorless liquid, miscible with water, used as a reagent and solvent. Also known as alcohol; ethyl alcohol; grain alcohol."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/12045> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The study of paleoclimates throughout geologic time, and of the causes of their variations, on either a local or a worldwide basis. It involves the interpretation of glacial deposits, fossils and sedimentologic and other types of data."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/12062> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Climate characterized by constant temperatures, abundant rainfall and a very short dry season."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/12063> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A type of climate characterized by hot, dry, sunny summers and a winter rainy season; basically, this is the opposite of a monsoon climate. Also known as etesian climate."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/12067> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A climate which is typical of equatorial and tropical regions, that is, one with continually high temperatures and with considerable precipitation, at least during part of the year."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/12082> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A temperature inversion in the atmosphere in which the temperature, instead of falling, increases with height above the ground. With the colder and heavier air below, there is no tendency to form upward currents and turbulence is suppressed. Inversions are often formed in the late afternoon when the radiation emitted from the ground exceeds that received from the sinking sun. Inversions are also caused by katabatic winds, that is cold winds flowing down the hillside into a valley, and by anticyclones. In inversion layers, both vertical and horizontal diffusion is inhibited and pollutants become trapped, sometimes for long periods. Low-level discharges of pollutants are more readily trapped by inversions than high level dischargers, hence the case for high stacks. Furthermore, high level discharges into an inversion tend to remain at a high level because of the absence of vertical mixing."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/12096> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The process of extracting underground water from a source."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/12098> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The movement of surface water into soil or rock through cracks and pores."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/120> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The physical or chemical bonding of molecules of gas, liquid or a dissolved substance to the external surface of a solid or the internal surface, if the material is porous, in a very thin layer."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/12104> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Water that occupies pores, cavities, cracks and other spaces in the crustal rocks. It includes water precipitated from the atmosphere which has percolated through the soil, water that has risen from deep magmatic sources liberated during igneous activity and fossil water retained in sedimentary rocks since their formation. The presence of groundwater is necessary for virtually all weathering processes to operate. Phreatic water is synonymous with groundwater and is the most important source of any water supply."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/12107> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Precautionary actions, procedures or installations undertaken to prevent or reduce harm to the environmental integrity of drainage areas used to catch water, such as reservoirs or basins."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/12108> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Water table is inherently susceptible to contamination from landuse activities. Remediation is very expensive and often impractical. Prevention of contamination is therefore critical in effective groundwater management."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1210> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A substance whose presence alters the rate at which a chemical reaction proceeds, but whose own composition remains unchanged by the reaction. Catalysts are usually employed to accelerate reactions(positive catalyst), but retarding (negative) catalysts are also used."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/12122> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The total quantity of water flowing from the catchment during the period of the flood."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/12123> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The filling or partial filling with silt of a reservoir that receives fine-grained sediment brought in by streams and surface runoff."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/12145> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "1) The drainage basin of a stream. \n2) An area occupied by a lake and its drainage basin."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/12152> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A body of water that is owned and maintained by a national governmental body or agency."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/12153> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A body of water that is owned and maintained by an individual or entity other than the national government."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/12165> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any mechanical procedure or process where some or all of the salt is removed from water."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/12171> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The utilization of the ocean for its food resources, mineral resources, and energy and water sources."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/12183> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Contamination of the generally broad portion of a stream near its outlet which is influenced by the tide of the water body into which it flows. Many estuaries have become badly contaminated by wastes that have been generated from heavily populated areas."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1220> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The yield obtained from a given fishery; fishery catches should be strictly controlled so that the fish population can have a sufficient breeding mass and thus give a sustained yield for future generations."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/12213> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The drawing of water from a reservoir by means of draining pipes located at the bottom of the basin and controlled by a system of sluices which ensure, if necessary, the emptying of the basin in a given period of time in respect of downstream conditions."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/12216> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Taste in water can be caused by foreign matter, such as organic compounds, inorganic salts or dissolved gases. These materials may come from domestic, agricultural or natural sources. Some substances found naturally in groundwater, while not necessarily harmful, may impart a disagreeable taste or undesirable property to the water. Magnesium sulphate, sodium sulphate, and sodium chloride are but a few of these. Acceptable waters should be free from any objectionable taste at point of use."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/12219> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A proliferation of a marine green plankton toxic and often fatal to fish, perhaps stimulated by the addition of nutrients."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1221> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Those of the planet's flora and fauna which are threatened with extinction. Hunting and poaching to fuel the trade in ivory, horn, skins, fur and feathers have long been a threat to already endangered species. Pollution, agricultural expansion, loss of wetlands, deforestation and other erosion of habitats have been added to the hazards. Human activity was responsible for most of the animals and plants known to have been lost in the past two centuries."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/12220> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Matter suspended in a fluid by the upward components of turbulent currents or by colloidal suspension."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/12226> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The degree of dissolved salts in water measured by weight in parts per thousand."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/12231> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A structure in which water is collected."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/12240> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A stream of water that is forced up into the air through a small hole, especially for decorative effect or the structure in a lake or pool from which this flows."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/12248> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Artificial or natural area of water, used for storing water for domestic or industrial use."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1225> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Domesticated bovine animals, including cows, steers and bulls, raised and bred on a ranch or farm."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/12277> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Addition of air to sewage or water so as to raise its dissolved oxygen level."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/12289> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The process in which sunlight, bacterial action and oxygen cause self-purification in waste water, Usually taking place in a shallow pond, or system of such ponds."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1229> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Principle connected with the precautionary principle: it means that, if there are strong reasons for expecting serious or irreversible damage to the environment following a given project, lack of full scientific certainty should not be used as a reason for postponing cost-effective measures to prevent environmental degradation. Critics of this approach are concerned about large commitments of resources to deal with vaguely defined problems."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/12321> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Area where waste material, especially metal, is dumped."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/12325> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Industry for the transformation of solid waste into useful products."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/12349> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The process of removing dirt, litter or other unsightly materials from shore line property or surrounding areas."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/12357> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Large items of waste material, such as appliances, furniture, large auto parts, trees, branches, stumps, etc."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/12377> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Wastes resulting from the operations of pollutant removal from industries, cleaning processes, etc."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/12382> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Metal material discarded during manufacturing or processing operations which cannot be directly fed back into the operation; Worn or discarded metal materials removed from service at the end of its useful life."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/12394> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Oil which derives from petroleum and is made up of hydrocarbons."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/12395> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The watery liquid that separates from the curd when the milk is clotted, as in making cheese."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/12417> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A manner of waste disposal in which refuse or unwanted material is dumped or submerged beneath the surface of a body of water."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1242> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The basic building block of a battery. It is an electrochemical device consisting of an anode and a cathode in a common electrolyte kept apart with a separator. This assembly may be used in its own container as a single cell battery or be combined and interconnected with other cells in a container to form a multicelled battery."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/12431> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any material, solid or semisolid, left after processing in a device designed to reduce waste volume by combustion."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/12444> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any process beyond gravity sedimentation that increases the concentration of solids in sludge with or without the use of chemical flocculants."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1244> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The main polysaccharide in living plants, forming the skeletal structure of the plant cell wall; a polymer of beta-D-glucose linked together with the elimination of water to form chains of 2000-4000 units."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/12450> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Operations, functions and processes involved in industrial production."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/12456> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Area of land which is no longer usable for cultivation or for any other purpose after having been the site of an industrial plant."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/12471> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The act of dismembering the carcass of an animal with the production of organic waste which if improperly disposed cause problems of pollution and fawl smells."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/12485> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A container or a reservoir for the storage of hydrocarbons."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/12587> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The process of deriving methane from any source, including livestock manure, landfills, coal mines, etc."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1259> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A system in which a governing or administrative body has a certain degree of power or authority to prevail in the management of local, national and international matters."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/12600> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Breakdown of organic material without the presence of oxygen, a treatment which permanently removes the unpleasant odour of many organic wastes so that they can be used on agricultural land."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/12601> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Process that uses microorganisms to decompose organic wastes either into water, carbon dioxide, and simple inorganic substances, or into simpler organic substances, such as aldehydes and acids. The purpose of a biological treatment system is to control the environment for microorganisms so that their growth and activity are enhanced, and provide a means for maintaining high concentration of the microorganisms in contact with the wastes."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/12605> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any processing of wastewater, toxic substances or other materials involving a combination of physical and chemical methods, such as physical processes including air-stripping or filtration and chemical processes including coagulation, chlorination or ozonation."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/12606> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Processes that separate components of a waste stream or change the physical form of the waste without altering the chemical structure of the constituent materials. Physical treatment techniques are often used to separate the materials within the waste stream so that they can be reused or detoxified by chemical or biological treatment or destroyed by high-temperature incineration."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/12607> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Removal of floating solids and suspended solids, both fine and coarse, from raw sewage."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1266> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The art and techniques of producing articles of clay, porcelain, etc."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/12687> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Precautionary measures, equipment or structures implemented to guard or defend people, property and lands from an unusual accumulation of water above the ground."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/12711> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Measures adopted to control erosion and degradation phenomena in the mountain regions caused by the loss of forest cover due to acid rain, uncontrolled forest cutting, winter skiing resorts construction, etc."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/12763> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Actions and measures undertaken, often at a local level, to ensure that citizens of a community are secure from harm, injury, danger or risk."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/12807> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Installations whose functioning involves the possibility of major hazards such as chemical plants, nuclear, coal and oil power production plants, etc."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/12808> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Installations whose functioning involves the possibility of major hazards such as chemical plants, nuclear, coal and oil power production plants, etc."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1280> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The administration, organization and planning for the flow of materials or merchandise through various stages of production and distribution, involving a network of vendors, suppliers, manufacturers, distributors, retailers and other trading partners."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/12889> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A commercial agreement which provides protection against the risks, or a particular risk, associated with pollution, toxic waste disposal or related concerns."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/12905> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Equivalent in money or other form for a loss sustained for an injury, for property taken, etc."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1290> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A porous solid product containing 85-98% carbon and produced by heating carbonaceous materials such as cellulose, wood or peat at 500-600 C° in the absence of air."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/12912> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Institution for the management of public issues."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1292> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A map, generally designed for navigation or other particular purposes, in which essential map information is combined with various other data critical to the intended use."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/12985> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "An address or form of oral communication in which a speaker makes his thoughts and emotions known before an audience, often for a given purpose."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/129> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The creation and dissemination of paid announcements or public notices to draw attention to goods, services or events offered by some entity, usually for purchase."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/13002> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A work systematically describing the flora of a particular region, listed by species and considered as a whole."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/13025> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A document or a portion thereof expressing an official enactment of a legislative body, with emphasis on the document's precise wording or language."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/13053> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Factual data, knowledge or instructions relating to scientific research or the development, testing, evaluation, production, use or maintenance of equipment."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/13060> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A system of interrelated persons and/or devices linked to permit the exchange of data or knowledge."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1307> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Fertilizer manufactured from chemicals; excessive use of them can cause pollution, when all the chemicals are not taken up by the plants and the excess is leached out of the soil into rivers and may cause algal bloom."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/13088> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A way of proceeding or doing something, especially a systematic or regular one."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/13098> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Sector of the metallurgical industry dealing with the production of cast iron, steel and iron alloys. Emissions from these industries tend to settle quickly from the atmosphere and can lead to rising concentrations in the soil. The main raw material input to the production process is iron ore. Also recycled scrap is used."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/13100> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The resulting effects and interrelationships of human population concentrations, the built environment, and the biophysical environment."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1310> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Industry related with the production of chemical compounds. The chemical processing industry has a variety of special pollution problems due to the vast number of products manufactured. The treatment processes combine processing, concentration, separation, extraction, by-product recovery, destruction, and reduction in concentration. The wastes may originate from solvent extraction, acid and caustic wastes, overflows, spills, mechanical loss, etc."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/13111> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The entire sequence of events involved in the development of an individual organism."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/13117> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any relatively unobstructed field of cultivated and mown grass, especially near a house or in a park."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/13118> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A series of transformations or biological events which follow one after the other one, reaching at the end of the cycle the initial conditions, as in the life cycle of many animal and plant organisms."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/13120> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any of the conditions in which people live. Also all human settlements in villages, towns or major cities, which require environmental management to provide water, public spaces, remove public wastes, etc."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/13121> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A process in which an increasing proportion of a country's population is concentrated in urban areas."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/13122> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A plot of cultivated ground adjacent to a dwelling and usually devoted in whole or in part to the growing of herbs, fruits, flowers, or vegetables for household use."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/13123> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The process of forming visible images directly or indirectly by the action of light or other forms of radiation on sensitive surfaces."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/13127> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Waste pieces or disused articles of wrought iron (wrought-iron scrap) suitable for reworking for rolling or forging."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
