<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1737> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Manufactured products intended primarily for personal use by individuals or families and classified as either durables or non-durables, depending on length of use."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1738> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A collection of persons united to address concerns regarding the purchase and use of specific commodities or services."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1739> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Factual, circumstantial and, often, comparative knowledge concerning various goods, services or events, their quality and the entities producing them."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1759> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The amount or quantity of polluting material found in a transporting agent that flows at a steady rate, in contrast to a sudden or dramatic influx."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1761> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The performing of cultivations along lines connecting points of equal elevation so reducing the loss of top soil by erosion, increasing the capacity of the soil to retain water and reducing the pollution of water by soil."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1763> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A commercial service provider, usually bound by a written agreement, responsible for the removal of dirt, litter or other unsightly materials from any property."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1781> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Setting aside a highly radioactive material until the radioactivity has diminished to a desired level."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1782> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Oil used as a cooling agent, either with forced circulation or with natural circulation."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1786> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Water used to make something less hot, such as the irradiated elements from a nuclear reactor or the engine of a machine."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1792> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A chemical element; one of the most important nonferrous metals; a ductile and malleable metal found in various ores and used in industry, engineering, and the arts in both pure and alloyed form."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1794> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The skeleton of certain solitary and colonial anthozoan coelenterates; composed chiefly of calcium carbonate."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1800> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The thick light porous outer bark of the cork oak, used widely as an insulator and for stoppers for bottles, casks, etc."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1807> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A physical linkage, connecting two areas of habitat and differing from the habitat on either side. Corridors are used by organisms to move around without having to leave the preferred habitat."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1808> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A process in which a solid, especially a metal, is eaten away and changed by a chemical action."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1817> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Relation between costs of a certain activity and its benefits to a certain community."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1818> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The attempt to assess, compare and frequently justify the total price or loss represented by a certain activity or expenditure with the advantage or service it provides."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1824> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "In economics, the value of the factors of production used by a firm in producing or distributing goods and services or engaging in both activities."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/183> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "An agreement, convention, or promise of two or more parties, by deed in writing, signed, and delivered, by which either of the parties pledges himself to the other that something is either done, or shall be done, or shall not be done, or stipulates for the truth of certain facts."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1850> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "An occupation or trade requiring manual dexterity or skilled artistry."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1860> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A violation of the law, punishable by the State in criminal proceedings."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1864> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "General term referring to the concentration limit beyond which a substance can cause dangerous effects to living organisms."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1865> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The maximum load that a given system can tolerate before failing."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1874> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The problem of crop protection has changed dramatically since 1945. There is now a whole arsenal of chemicals with which to combat agricultural pests and diseases, but this development has itself many drawbacks. Such sophisticated techniques are available only to a minority of farmers; in most parts of the world the standard of crop protection remains abysmally low. In addition, modern crop protection methods have been criticized for relying too heavily on chemical control. Biological controls, both natural and contrived, have been neglected. In some cases involving misuse of agricultural chemicals, crops must be protected from the very measures intended for their protection. Meanwhile previously localized pests and diseases continue to spread worldwide."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1880> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A place, often shown by markings, lights, or poles, where a street, railway, etc. may be crossed."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1881> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Bridges and tunnels provided for animals for crossing roads and railways. Railway and road infrastructures represent an hindrance to wildlife migration."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1885> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A comparatively volatile liquid bitumen composed principally of hydrocarbon, with traces of sulphur, nitrogen or oxygen compounds; can be removed from the earth in a liquid state."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1888> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Travelling by sea in a liner for pleasure, usually calling at a number of ports."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1890> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A large group of plants, comprising the Thallophyta, Bryophyta and Pteridophyta, the last of which are cryptogams."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1902> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any procedure or approach used to prepare land or soil for the growth of new crops, or to promote or improve the growth of existing crops."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1909> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The process whereby the capabilities or possibilities inherent in a people's beliefs, customs, artistic activity and knowledge are brought out or made more effective."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1921> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The body of customary beliefs, social forms, and material traits constituting a distinct complex of tradition of a racial or social group."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1926> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The aggregate of courses of study provided in a particular school, college, university, adult education program, technical institution or some other educational program."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1945> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A branch of the biological sciences which deals with the structure, behaviour, growth, and reproduction of cells and the functions and chemistry of cell components."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1951> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Production of food made from milk or milk products."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1952> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Products derived from milk, such as butter, cheese, lactose, etc."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1958> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Injury or harm resulting from the planned movement of armed forces or from the tactical exercises simulating war operations that is carried out for training and evaluation purposes."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/195> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A discipline concerned with developing and improving the means for providing food and fiber for mankind's needs."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1968> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Transporting substances capable of producing adverse health effects, fires or explosions to other countries or areas for the conduct of foreign trade."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1969> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Goods or products that are full of hazards or risks when used, transported, etc."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1974> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The act of collecting and gathering individual facts, statistics or other items of information."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1979> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A computerized compilation of data, facts and records that is organized for convenient access, management and updating."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/197> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Machines utilized for tillage, planting, cultivation, and harvesting of crops."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1986> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any operation or combination of operations on data, including everything that happens to data from the time they are observed or collected to the time they are destroyed."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1988> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Policies, procedures or devices designed to maintain the integrity or security of informational elements in storage or in transmission."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/1996> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A persistent organochlorine insecticide, also known as dichlorodiphenyltrichloroethane, that was introduced in the 1940s and used widely because of its persistence (meaning repeated applications were unnecessary), its low toxicity to mammals and its simplicity and cheapness of manufacture. It became dispersed all over the world and, with other organochlorines, had a disruptive effect on species high in food chains, especially on the breeding success of certain predatory birds. DDT is very stable, relatively insoluble in water, but highly soluble in fats. Health effects on humans are not clear, but it is less toxic than related compounds. It is poisonous to other vertebrates, especially fish, and is stored in the fatty tissue of animals as sublethal amounts of the less toxic DDE. Because of its effects on wildlife its use in most countries is now forbidden or strictly limited."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2002> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The mechanical dewatering of a wet solid by pouring off the liquid without disturbing the underlying sediment or precipitate."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2003> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Basic organizational leadership concept and process of shifting and delegating power and authority from a higher level to subordinate levels within the administrative/managerial hierarchy in order to promote independence, responsibility, and quicker decision-making in applying or interpreting policies and procedures to the needs of these levels."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2014> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The more or less permanent breakdown of a molecule into simpler molecules or atoms."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/202> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Land used primarily for the production of plant or animal crops, including arable agriculture, dairying, pasturage, apiaries, horticulture, floriculture, viticulture, animal husbandry and the necessary lands and structures needed for packing, processing, treating, or storing the produce."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2031> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The act or process of protecting citizens or any geographical area by preparing for or by using military means to resist the attack of an enemy."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2042> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Those chemicals resulting from partial decomposition or chemical breakdown of substances."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2053> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The desire, ability and willingness of an individual to purchase a good or service. The consumer must have the funds or the ability to obtain funds in order to convert the desire into demand. The demand of a buyer for a certain good is a schedule of the quantities of that good which the individual would buy at possible alternative prices at a given moment in time."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2056> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The gradual pattern of change in the growth of human populations in a particular region or country, from a rapid increase in the birth and death rates to a leveling off in the growth rate due to reduced fertility and other factors."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2060> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The statistical study of human vital statistics and population dynamics."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2062> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The activity of reducing buildings or other structures to rubble."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2064> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Masonry or rubble wastes arising from the demolition of buildings or other civil engineering structures."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2071> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "1) The loss of nitrogen from soil by biological or chemical means. It is a gaseous loss, unrelated to loss by physical processes such as through leachates. \n2) The breakdown of nitrates by soil bacteria, resulting in the release of free nitrogen. This process takes place under anaerobic conditions, such as are found in water-logged soil, and it reduces soil fertility."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/208> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The administration or handling of soil, crops and livestock."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2099> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "1) Plants for the extraction of fresh water from saltwater by the removal of salts, usually by distilling.\n2) Parts of the world with severe water shortages are looking to desalination plants to solve their problems. Desalination of water is still nearly four times more expensive than obtaining water from conventional sources. However technology is improving and costs are likely to decrease slightly in the future. There is now more interest in building distillation plants beside electric installations so that the waste heat from power generation can be used to drive the desalination process."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/20> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Level of risk judged to be outweighed by corresponding benefits or one that is of such a degree that it is considered to pose minimal potential for adverse effects."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2103> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A wide, open, comparatively barren tract of land with few forms of life and little rainfall."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2119> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The process of removing a sorbed substance by the reverse of adsorption or absorption."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2124> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The removal of sulphur, as from molten metals or petroleum oil. Sulphur residues in fuels end up as sulphur dioxide when the fuel is burned causing acid rain."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/212> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Insects and mites that damage crops, weeds that compete with field crops for nutrients and water, plants that choke irrigation channels or drainage systems, rodents that eat young plants and grain, and birds that eat seedlings or stored foodstuffs."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2131> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A surface-active agent used for removing dirt and grease from a variety of surfaces and materials. Early detergents contained alkyl sulphonates, which proved resistant to bacterial decomposition, causing foaming in rivers and difficulties in sewage treatment plants. These hard detergents were replaced during the 1960s with soft biodegradable detergents. Apprehension continues to be expressed about the use of phosphates in detergents, helping to promote the process of eutrophication. No satisfactory substitute has yet emerged."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2139> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Method employed in the assessment or in the evaluation of a quantity, a quality, a fact, an event, etc."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2147> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A nation possessing a relatively high degree of industrialization, infrastructure and other capital investment, sophisticated technology, widespread literacy and advanced living standards among its populations as a whole."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2156> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Area which has been given special help from a government to encourage business and factories to be set up there."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/215> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A course of action adopted by government or some other organization that determines how to deal with matters involving the cultivation of land; raising crops; feeding, breeding and raising livestock or poultry; and other farming issues."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2160> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The act or process of formulating a course of action that promotes the economic advancement of a region or people, particularly in countries known to have low levels of economic productivity and technological sophistication."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2182> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The development of cells so that they are capable of performing specialized functions in the organs and tissues of the organisms to which they belong."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2186> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The spontaneous movement and scattering of particles (atoms and molecules), of liquid, gases, and solids."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2195> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A representation of a surface's topography stored in a numerical format. Each pixel has been assigned coordinates and an altitude."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2207> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A by-product formed during the preparation of the herbicide 2, 4, 5-T, and sometimes produced by the incineration of chlorinated organic compounds. It may also occur naturally and is distributed widely in the environment, except locally in extremely low concentrations. Substantial amounts were released by the industrial accident of Seveso in 1976."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2212> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The second rank of administrative acts (inferior to regulations, superior to decisions) made by the council or commission of the European Communities on order to carry out their tasks in accordance with the Treaties. They must be addressed to states, not individuals, but many create rights for individuals or allow the directive to be pleaded before municipal court."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2213> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Person lacking one or more physical power, such as the ability to walk or to coordinate one's movements, as from the effects of a disease or accident, or through mental impairment."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2216> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A course or procedure of activity designed to clear the debris or remove harmful substances left by an ecological calamity, natural or human in origin, in a given area."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2218> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "An anticipatory emergency plan to be followed in an expected or eventual disaster, based on risk assessment, availability of human and material resources, community preparedness, local and international response capability, etc."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2222> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Money, food or other assistance provided for those surviving a sudden, calamitous event causing loss of life, damage or hardship."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2227> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The rate of flow of a river at a particular moment in time, related to its volume and its velocity."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2232> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A definite pathological process having a characteristic set of signs and symptoms which are detrimental to the well-being of the individual."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2237> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "An agent, such as heat, radiation, or a chemical, that disinfects by destroying, neutralizing, or inhibiting the growth of disease-carrying microorganisms."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2245> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A distribution of finely divided particles in a medium."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2262> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A sector of the economy in which an aggregate of commercial enterprises is engaged in the manufacture and marketing of alcoholic beverages made by a distillation process of vaporization and condensation, such as vodka, rum, whiskey and other related beverages."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2275> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Military site where all activity has ceased. Such areas, being extremely well sheltered against outside disturbances and in many ways less affected by human landuse than many other open landscapes, can contain significant natural habitats and rare or endangered wildlife. Abandoned military territories constitute an important source of natural landscapes to be managed and restored in an environmentally sound way."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2276> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A long, narrow excavation artificially dug in the ground; especially an open and usually unpaved waterway, channel, or trench for conveying water for drainage or irrigation, and usually smaller than a canal. Some ditches may be natural watercourses."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2282> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Material of any kind, regardless of physical form, which furnishes information, evidence or ideas, including items such as contracts, bills of sale, letters, audio and video recordings, and machine readable data files."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2284> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The process of accumulating, classifying and disseminating information, often to support the claim or data given in a book or article."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2287> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A common four-legged animal, especially kept by people as a pet or to hunt or guard things."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2291> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "1) Wild animal which has been trained to live near a house and not be frightened of human beings; 2) species which was formerly wild, now selectively bred to fill human needs."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2294> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Liquid petroleum product used in domestic heaters."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2298> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Noise caused by domestic facilities and activities."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/229> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Unusable materials, liquid or solid, that result from agricultural practices, such as fertilizers, pesticides, crop residue (such as orchard prunings) and cattle manure."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/22> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any street or narrow stretch of paved surface that leads to a specific destination, such as a main highway."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2308> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The amount of test substance administered. Dose is expressed as weight of test substance (g, mg) per unit weight of test animal (e.g., mg/kg), or as weight of food or drinking water."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2309> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The relation between the quantity of a given substance and a measurable or observable effect."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2316> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any of the insects composing six families of the suborder Anisoptera and having four large, membranous wings and compound eyes that provide keen vision."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2323> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Incidental surface waters from diverse sources such as rainfall, snow melt or permafrost melt."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2332> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The use of fishing nets of great length and depth, aptly described as \"walls of death\" because of the huge numbers of marine mammals, birds, and turtles that became ensnared in them. The Tarawa Declaration of 1989 formulated at the 20th South Pacific Forum, aimed at banning drift netting in the South Pacific. In June 1992 the UN banned drift netting in all the world's oceans."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2354> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A chemical substance used internally or externally as a medicine for the prevention, diagnosis, treatment or cure of disease, for the relief of pain or to control or enhance physical or mental well-being."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2358> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "To clean fabrics etc. with a solvent other than water."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/235> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A formulated or systematic method for the management of soil, crops and livestock."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2360> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A system of extensive agriculture allowing the production of crops without irrigation in areas of limited rainfall. Dry farming involves conserving soil moisture through mulching, frequent fallowing, maintenance of a fine tilth by cross-ploughing, repeated working of the soil after rainfall and removal of any weeds that would take up some of the moisture."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2361> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The process of partially or totally removing water or other liquids from a solid."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2364> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "An economy based upon two separate/distinct economic systems which co-exist in the same geographical space. Dualism is characteristic of many developing countries in which some parts of a country resemble advanced economies while other parts resemble traditional economies, i.e. there are circuits of production and exchange."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2365> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "To reduce the quantity of packaging waste, and thereby of overall MSW, Germany introduced a far-reaching legislation to reduce waste, based on the producer's responsibility principle. Industry was given the option to set up a third party organization which would carry out the collection and sorting of sales packaging for care of manufacturers and retailers. Thus, Some 600 companies created \"Duales System Deutschland\" in 1990 (\"Dual\" because it meant creating a second collection system in parallel to the existing waste collection system of the local authorities). Duales System Deutschland (DSD), now has overall responsibility for the separate collection and recycling of packaging. At present, the Dual System is the only nationwide system for the collection and sorting of sales packaging. Packaging participating in this collection system is marked with the Green Dot."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2372> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The discharge, deposit or injection of any waste onto or into the soil or other land surfaces."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2377> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A low mound, ridge, bank, or hill of loose, windblown granular material (generally sand, sometimes volcanic ash), either bare or covered with vegetation, capable of movement from place but always retaining its characteristic shape."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2380> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Period of the day during which the sun is shining."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2394> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The addition of material to strengthen the structure of the dykes."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/23> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The ability, right and permission to approach and use, or the general availability of resources that transmit the beliefs, customs, artistic activity and knowledge of a people."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2405> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The science that deals with the earth or any part thereof; includes the disciplines of geology, geography, oceanography and meteorology, among others."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2406> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The Earth depends on the sun for its existence as a planet hospitable to life, and solar energy is the major factor determining the climate. Hence, conditions on the sun and conditions on Earth are inextricably linked. Although the sun's rays may appear unchanging, its radiation does vary. Many scientists suspect that sunspot activity has a greater influence on climatic change than variations attributed to the greenhouse effect."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2412> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A geographic region of the Asian continent bordered by the Pacific Ocean in the east that includes China, Japan, Korea, Macao, Taiwan and Siberia."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2413> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A geographic region of the European continent west of Asia and east of Germany and the Adriatic Sea, traditionally consisting of countries that were formerly part of the Soviet Union, such as Poland, the Czech Republic, Slovakia, Hungary, Romania, Serbia, Croatia and Bulgaria."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2419> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The organ of the EU that is primarily concerned with the formulation of policy and the adoption of Community legislation. The Council consists of one member of government of each of the member states of the Community, and its presidency is held by each state in turn for periods of six months."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2422> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A type of legislation issued by the European Union which is binding on Member States in terms of the results to be achieved but which leaves to Member States the choice of methods."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2424> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "EC Directive proposed on 15 July 1992 aiming at harmonizing national measures concerning the management of packaging and packaging waste; the directive covers all packaging placed on the market."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2435> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The European Community's initiative to encourage the promotion of environmentally friendly products. The scheme came into operation in late 1992 and was designed to identify products which are less harmful to the environment than equivalent brands. It was hoped that by buying labelled goods, consumers would be able to put pressure on manufacturers and retailers both to make and to stock \"greener\" products. This includes the effects they have on the environment at all stages. The labels are awarded on environmental criteria set by the EC."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2437> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Number of individual specimens of an animal or plant seen over a certain period of time in a certain place."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2441> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The condition of equilibrium among the components of a natural community such that their relative numbers remain fairly constant and their ecosystem is stable. Gradual readjustments to the composition of a balanced community take place continually in response to natural ecological succession and to alterations in climatic and other influences."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2442> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The systematic accounting or recordkeeping of a company's impact on the environment or its progress towards environmentally sound business practices."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2450> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "An environmental factor that, under some definite conditions, can exert appreciable influence on organisms or their communities, causing the increase or decrease in the number of organisms and/or changes in the communities."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2456> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "1) The space occupied by a species, which includes both the physical space as well as the functional role of the species.\n2) Ecological niche refers to the characteristics of an environment that provides all the essential food and protection for the continued survival of a particular species of flora or fauna. In addition to food and shelter, there is no long-term threat to existence in that place from potential predators, parasites and competitors. The concept of the ecological niche goes a long way beyond the idea of the species habitat."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2469> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Grouping of individuals and organizations dedicated to the protection of the environment."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2477> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The competency in performance in business matters involving the relation between financial and environmental principles."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2478> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The quantitative and qualitative identification, study, and evaluation of the nature of an economy or a system of organization or operation."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2484> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The state of nations and the historical processes of change experienced by them, the extent to which the resources of a nation are brought into productive use; the concept of development subsumes associated social, cultural and political changes as well as welfare measures."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2494> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A tool or method used by any organization in the management of developmental processes used in the production of, or in the regulation of, material resources."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2498> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A definite course of action adopted and pursued by a government, political party or enterprise pertaining to the production, distribution and use of income, wealth and commodities."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2501> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The social study of the production, distribution, and consumption of wealth."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/250> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A system or process for controlling the temperature and sometimes the humidity and purity of the air in a house, etc."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2510> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The study of relationships in the economy. Its purpose is to analyze and explain the behaviour of the various economic elements. The body of economic theory can be divided into two broad categories, positive theory and welfare theory. Positive theory is an attempt to analyze the operation of the economy without considering the desirability of its results in terms of ultimate goals. Welfare theory is concerned primarily with an evaluation of the economic system in terms of ethical goals which are not themselves derived from economic analysis."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2511> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Changes of variables and parameters of an economic system, analysed in statistical calculations."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2517> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Branch of medical science concerning the study and the therapy of children diseases caused by environmental factors."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2518> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The study of biophysical, biochemical and physiological processes used by animals to cope with factors of their physical environment, or employed during ecological interactions with other organisms."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2527> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Excursions to relatively untouched lands, which for the tourist promise the chance to observe unusual wildlife and indigenous inhabitants. The travel industry, in an attempt to market adventure and authenticity to those travellers weary of \"civilisation\" promote travel to environments free of modern technology. Ecotourism's inherent contradiction is the promotion of untouched lands, which immediately become touched by the hands of tourism."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2528> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Quality of some substances or preparations which present or may present immediate or delayed risks for one or more sectors of the environment."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2531> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Species that has special characteristics which allow it to live in a certain habitat."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2539> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The study of the relationships between soil and organisms, including the use made of land by mankind."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2547> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The act or process of imparting or acquiring knowledge or skills."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2566> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Resultant of natural or manmade perturbations of the physical, chemical or biological components making up the environment."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2569> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Parameter or rule for assessing the competency in performance of production relative to the input of resources."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2570> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The ratio of output to input, usually given as a percentage."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2578> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Council Directive of 27 June 1985 on the assessment of the effects of certain public and private projects on the environment (85/337/EEC). The Directive applies to projects which are likely to have significant effects on the environment by virtue of their nature, size or location."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2584> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Someone who has reached the later stage of life or who has attained a specified age within that stage."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2586> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Engineering that deals with practical applications of electricity; generally restricted to applications involving current flow through conductors, as in motors and generators."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2587> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Industry for the production of electric energy."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2593> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Company which is responsible for the supply and distribution of electric energy to a given area."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2595> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The act or process of transforming other forms of energy into electric energy."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2596> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The value or amount of money exchanged for the production and sustained supply of charged ion current used as a power source."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2597> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Industry for the supply and distribution of electric power."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2599> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Wires conducting electric power from one location to another; also known as electric power line."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2606> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A stationary plant containing apparatus for large-scale conversion of some form of energy (such as hydraulic, steam, chemical, or nuclear energy) into electrical energy."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2617> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The study of the motion of electric charges, especially of steady currents in electric circuits, and of the motion of electrified particles in electric or magnetic fields."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2618> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The production of a chemical reaction by passing an electric current through an electrolyte. In electrolysis, positive ions migrate to the cathode and negative ions to the anode."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2624> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Study, control, and application of the conduction of electricity through gases or vacuum or through semiconducting or conducting materials."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2626> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Government or management prescribed rule for the disposal and recycling of electric parts, circuits and systems, especially computer devices."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2638> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Group III consists of two subgroups: group IIIb and group IIIa. Group IIIa consists of scandium, yttrium, and lanthanium, which is generally considered with the lanthanoids, and actinium, which is classified with the actinoids. Group IIIb, the main group, comprises boron, aluminium, gallium, indium, and thallium."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2640> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Group V consists of two subgroups: group Vb, the main group, and group Va. Group Va consists of vanadium, niobium, and tantalum, which are generally considered with the transition elements. The main group consists of nitrogen, phosphorus, arsenic, antimony, and bismuth."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2654> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The formation and development of an embryo from an egg."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2656> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Program of procedures to be undertaken in the event of a sudden, urgent and usually unexpected occurrence requiring immediate action, especially an incident of potential harm to human life, property or the environment."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2657> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Money, food or other assistance provided for those surviving a sudden and usually unexpected occurrence requiring immediate action, especially an incident of potential harm to human life, property or the environment."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2661> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Shelter given to persons who are deprived of the essential needs of life following a disaster."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2667> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The relationship between the amount of pollutants produced to the amount of raw materials processed, or fuel consumed, in any polluting process."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2668> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The final step in a clean air plan is to predict future air quality to demonstrate that we can (if we can) meet the health standards by implementing the measures proposed in the plan. This is done by first projecting the emission inventory into the future, taking into account changes in population, housing, employment in specific business sectors, and vehicle miles traveled. These data are obtained from various sources and the resulting emissions are adjusted to account for regulations and control measures scheduled for implementation during the same time period. Additional adjustments are made to reflect large facilities that are expected to start up, modify, or shut down. The resulting inventory is an emission forecast, and is usually expressed in tons per day of particular pollutants for a given year. Additional steps may be required to determine how the forecasted quantities of air pollution will affect the overall air quality. One way to accomplish this is through computer modeling. A computer model simulates how pollutants disperse, react, and move in the air. The inputs to such a computer model are complex. They include weather patterns, terrain, and the chemical nature of air pollutants."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2672> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A listing, by source, of the amounts of air pollutants discharged in the atmosphere of a community daily."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2674> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A chemical process, building, furnace, plant or other entity responsible for the discharge of pollutants or contaminants into the environment."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2677> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The maximum amount of discharge legally allowed from a single source, mobile or stationary."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2683> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The work or occupation in which a person is employed."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2684> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Issues or initiatives pertaining to the inter-relationship between ecological concerns and the economics of employment, including sustained, environmentally safe development; the effect of environmental activism on jobs; and the creation of environmental occupations."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2693> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The enclosure of any polluting product with a material that prevents its release in the environment."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2700> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The plants threatened with extinction by human or natural changes in the environment."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2704> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Threat to the quality and quantity of groundwater by activities related to the use of land. As some activities (e.g. landfill) present a particular risk of pollution, the closer an activity is to a well or borehole, the greater the risk of the pumped water being polluted. The type of soil, the geology, the rainfall and the amount of water pumped out of the ground must all be taken into consideration."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2707> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "An approach to pollution control which concentrates upon effluent treatment or filtration prior to discharge into the environment, as opposed to making changes in the process giving rise to the wastes."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2712> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The capacity to do work; involving thermal energy (heat), radiant energy (light), kinetic energy (motion) or chemical energy; measured in joules."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2714> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The strategy for reducing energy requirements per unit of industrial output or individual well-being without affecting the progress of socio-economic development or causing disruption in life style. In temperate developed countries most energy is used in heating and lighting industrial and domestic buildings. Industrial processes, transport and agriculture are the other main users. During the 1970s it was demonstrated that substantial savings could be achieved through appropriate building technologies and the use of energy-efficient equipment for heating, air-conditioning and lighting. Most goods could and should be both manufactured and made to work more efficiently."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2715> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Amount of energy consumed by a person or an apparatus shown as a unit."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2716> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The process of changing energy from one form to another."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2720> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any loss of energy, generally by conversion into heat."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2724> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Refers to actions to save fuels by better building design, the modification of production processes, better selection of road vehicles and transport policies, the adoption of district heating schemes in conjunction with electrical power generation, and the use of domestic insulation and double glazing in homes."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/272> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The measurement of ambient air-pollution concentrations in order to determine whether there is a problem in a given region."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2730> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The administration or handling of power derived from sources such as fossil fuel, electricity and solar radiation."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2738> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Potential supplies of energy which have not yet been used (such as coal lying in the ground, solar heat, wind power, geothermal power, etc.)."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2742> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Sources from which energy can be obtained to provide heat, light, and power. Energy resources, including fossil and nuclear fuels as well as solar, water, tidal and geothermal energy, may be captured or recovered and converted into other energy forms for a variety of household, commercial, transportation, and industrial applications."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2744> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Amount of energy reserves; often refers to the stocks of non-renewable fuel, such as oil, which a nation, for example, possesses."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2746> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The provision and storage of energy (the capacity to do work or produce a change), or the amount of energy stored, for the use of a municipality, or other energy user."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2754> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A machine in which power is applied to do work by the conversion of various forms of energy into mechanical force and motion."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2759> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The process of increasing the abundance of a specified isotope in a mixture of isotopes. It is usually applied to an increase in the proportion of U-235, or the addition of Pu-239 to natural uranium for use in a nuclear reactor or weapon."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2760> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A quantity of nutriments that meets fundamental nutritional requirements and is provided to a person, group or community on a continuing basis."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2772> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Environmentally friendly architecture is based on the following five principles: 1) healthful interior environment; 2) energy efficiency; 3) ecologically benign materials; 4) environmental form; 5) good design."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2778> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The growth and development of awareness, understanding and consciousness toward the biophysical environment and its problems, including human interactions and effects. Thinking \"ecologically\" or in terms of an ecological consciousness."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2779> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Final part of the environmental impact study and assessment which compares environmental costs and benefits on the basis of homogeneous criteria."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/277> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any measure, technique or design intended to reduce the risk of harm posed by either moving vehicles or projectiles above the earth's surface or pollutants to the earth's atmosphere."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2790> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Efforts and activities to maintain and sustain those attributes in natural and urban environments which are essential both to human physical and mental health and to enjoyment of life."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2797> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Unlawful acts against the environment, such as water contamination, hazardous waste disposal, air contamination, unpermitted installation of plants, oil spills, etc."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/279> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The activity of organizing or preparing for transportation through the atmosphere above earth's surface."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2801> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The total of learned behavior, attitudes, practices and knowledge that a society has with respect to maintaining or protecting its natural resources, the ecosystem and all other external conditions affecting human life."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2805> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The growth, progress or advancement in matters of ecological concern."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2811> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A recognized field of specialization in the discipline of Economics that embraces the issues of pollution control and environment protection, in which costs and benefits are difficult or impossible to estimate, much of the subject matter falling outside the competitive market system. Yet, it is an area in which immense common property resources need to be allocated sensibly to the overall public good. The subject is also very much concerned with ways and means to achieve this sensible allocation such as emission and effluent charges, user charges for the treatment or disposal of waste, environmental taxes, product charges, deposit refunds, tradeable pollution rights, performance bonds, natural resource accounting, and the economic implications of sustainable development."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2814> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The educational process that deals with the human interrelationships with the environment and that utilizes an interdisciplinary problem-solving approach with value clarification. Concerned with education progress of knowledge, understanding, attitudes, skills, and commitment for environmental problems and considerations. The need for environmental education is continuous, because each new generation needs to learn conservation for itself."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2821> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Financial resources set aside for measures involving ecological maintenance or the protection, defense, or shelter of natural resources."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2823> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A physical or chemical agent capable of causing harm to the ecosystem or natural resources."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2824> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The art and science of the protection of good health, the prevention of disease and injury through the control of positive environmental factors, and the reduction of potential physical, biological, chemical and radiological hazards."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2828> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A systematic and chronological account of past events and conditions relating to the ecosystem, its natural resources or, more generally, the external factors surrounding and affecting human life."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2831> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Agricultural activities have significant impacts on water quality, including increases in stream sedimentation from erosion, and increases in nutrients, pesticides, and salt concentrations in runoff. In certain regions, the misuse of pesticides has led to the development of pesticide-resistant strains of pests, destroyed natural predators, killed local wildlife, and contaminated human water supplies. Improper application of fertilizers has changed the types of vegetation and fish types inhabiting nearby waterways and rivers."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2833> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Energy and environmental problems are closely related, since it is nearly impossible to produce, transport, or consume energy without significant environmental impact. The environmental problems directly related to energy production and consumption include air pollution, water pollution, thermal pollution, and solid waste disposal. The emission of air pollutants from fossil fuel combustion is the major cause of urban air pollution. Diverse water pollution problems are associated with energy usage. One major problem is oil spills. In all petroleum-handling operations, there is a finite probability of spilling oil either on the earth or in a body of water. Coal mining can also pollute water. Changes in groundwater flow produced by mining operations often bring otherwise unpolluted waters into contact with certain mineral materials which are leached from the soil and produce an acid mine drainage. Solid waste is also a by-product of some forms of energy usage. Coal mining requires the removal of large quantities of earth as well as coal. In general, environmental problems increase with energy use and this combined with the limited energy resource base is the crux of the energy crisis. An energy impact assessment should compare these costs with the benefits to be derived from energy use."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2847> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A measurement, statistic or value that provides a proximate gauge or evidence of the effects of environmental management programs or of the state or condition of the environment."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2850> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Science and techniques of data elaboration and of computer processing of information concerning ecosystems and ecology."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2856> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Securities held for the production of income in the form of interest and dividends with the aim of benefitting the environment."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2862> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Branch of law relating to pollution control; national parks, wildlife, fauna and flora, wilderness and biodiversity; environmental and occupational health; environmental planning; heritage conservation and a large number of international conventions relating to the environment."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2869> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Substance that causes undesirable change in the physical, chemical, or biological characteristics of the air, water, or land that can harmfully affect the health, survival, or activities of human or other living organisms."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2872> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Adoption of integrated and preventative management practices aiming at reducing the impacts of industrial and trade activities on the environment; these practices include, among others, life-cycle analysis in the product development cycle, the introduction of clean process technology and measures of waste minimisation."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2876> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Firms that do not comply with environmental regulations for the disposal of noxious wastes generated during the production cycle."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2889> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The identification of desirable objectives for the physical environment, including social and economic objectives, and the creation of administrative procedures and programmes to meet those objectives."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2890> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A formulated or systematic method for the protection of natural or ecological resources."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2895> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The introduction by man into the environment of substances or energy liable to cause hazards to human health, harm to living resources and ecological systems, damage to structure or amenity, or interference with legitimate uses of the environment."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2900> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Measures and controls to prevent damage and degradation of the environment, including the sustainability of its living resources."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2902> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Associations whose object resides in the protection of natural environment."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2908> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A government agency, committee or group that is responsible for preserving and safeguarding ecological or natural resources."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/290> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The physical processes at the air-water interface: momentum, heat and mass transfer across the air-water interface, mixing of surface water by wind stress and wave breaking, directional wave spectra and wave forces on offshore structures. The air-water interaction is measured by the turbulence and gas exchanges resulting from the mixing of the water column by wind."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2910> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Technologies that meet environmental objectives by incorporating pollution prevention concepts in their design. Environmental control strategies introduced in the early design stages of a process, rather than an end-of-pipe control option introduced in the later stages, improve the technical and economic performance of a process."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2912> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Properties and characteristics of the environment, either generalized or local, as they impinge on human beings and other organisms. Environmental quality is a general term which can refer to: varied characteristics such as air and water purity or pollution, noise, access to open space, and the visual effects of buildings, and the potential effects which such characteristics may have on physical and mental health."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2917> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "An account or statement, usually in writing, describing in detail events, situations or conditions pertaining to the ecosystem, its natural resources or any of the external factors surrounding and affecting human life."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2918> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The study of the environment and its modifications caused by human activities."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2920> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Qualitative and quantitative evaluation of the risk posed to the environment by the actual or potential presence and/or use of specific pollutants."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2922> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The interdisciplinary study of environmental problems, within the framework of established physical and biological principles, i.e. oriented toward a scientific approach."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2923> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Measures taken or policies instituted to protect and promote the safety of external conditions affecting the life, development and survival of an organism."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2925> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Assessment made by a company or organization of the financial benefits and disadvantages to be derived from adopting a more environmentally sound policy."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2938> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The assessment, evaluation, or appraisal of business performance in matters involving ecology and finances."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2945> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any of a group of catalytic proteins that are produced by living cells and that mediate and promote the chemical processes of life without themselves being altered or destroyed."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2947> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A sudden increase in the incidence rate of a disease to a value above normal, affecting large numbers of people and spread over a wide area."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2955> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Animals belonging to the family of Equidae."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2956> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any collection of materials, supplies or apparatuses stored, furnished or provided for an undertaking or activity."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2969> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The scientific study or the characteristic life processes of living organisms found in a semi-enclosed coastal body of water which has a free connection with the open sea and within which sea water is measurably diluted with freshwater."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2974> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Area at the mouth of a river where it broadens into the sea, and where fresh and sea water intermingle to produce brackish water. The estuarine environment is very rich in wildlife, particularly aquatic, but it is very vulnerable to damage as a result of the actions of humans."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2979> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A colorless liquid, slightly soluble in water; used as a reagent, intermediate, anesthetic, and solvent."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2980> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The philosophical study of the moral value of human conduct and of the rules and principles that ought to govern it."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/2982> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The science that deals with the study of the origin, distribution, and relations of races or ethnic groups of mankind."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/298> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A group of organic chemical compounds composed of carbon, hydrogen, and oxygen. The molecules in the series vary in chain length and are composed of a hydrocarbon plus a hydroxyl group. Alcohol includes methanol and ethanol."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
