<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3007> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "enrichment of water by nutrients, especially compounds of nitrogen and/or phosphorus, causing an accelerated growth of algae and higher forms of plant life that produce an undesirable disturbance to the balance of organisms present in the water and to the quality of the water concerned"@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3007> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "økt konsentrasjon av næringsstoffer i vann, særlig nitrogen- og/eller fosforforbindelser, som skaper økt algevekst og høyere former for planteliv som medfører uønskede forstyrrelser i balansen mellom organismene i vannforekomsten eller i vannkvaliteten"@no <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3012> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A standard, norm, value or measurement by which the quantity or quality of a process, object or person's work performance is ascertained through an analysis and judgment of the relevant information in context and in view of established goals, objectives and standards."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3022> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Discharge of water from the earth's surface to the atmosphere by evaporation from lakes, streams and soil surfaces and by transpiration from plants. Also known as fly-off."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3026> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The biological theory or process whereby species of plants and animals change with the passage of time so that their descendants differ from their ancestors, i.e. development from earlier forms by hereditary transmission of slight variations in successive generations."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3027> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Mathematics and other sciences based on calculation."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3028> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A pit, cavity, or other uncovered cutting produced by excavation."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3032> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The location chosen for an excavation, meaning the act or process of removing soil and/or rock materials by digging, blasting, breaking, loading either at the surface or underground."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/303> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Excessive and rapid growth of algae and other aquatic plants when they are stimulated to grow too quickly by pollution. It takes place when there are too many nutrients in the water and is aggravated when accompanied by a rise in temperature. Although the algae grow quickly they soon die because they have swallowed up all the water's nutrients. As they decompose they tend to rise to the surface and form a green slime. Algal bloom have increased because higher levels of nitrogen and phosphates from agricultural areas have leached from the fields into water courses."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3040> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "An order or regulation issued by the president or some administrative authority under his direction for the purpose of interpreting, implementing or giving administrative effect to a provision of the constitution or of some law or treaty."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3044> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "1) A duct or pipe through which waste material is emitted.\n2) A combination of components which provides for enclosed flow of exhaust gas from engine parts to the atmosphere."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3048> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Plants, animals or microorganisms which are introduced by humans into areas where they are not native. Exotics are often associated with negative ecological consequences for native species and the ecosystems."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3049> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Spending by consumers, investors, or government for goods or services."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3050> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A test under controlled conditions that is made to demonstrate a known truth, examine the validity of a hypothesis, or determine the efficacy of something previously untried."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3054> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A computer configuration of hardware and software that simulates the judgment and behavior of a human or an organization with extensive knowledge in a particular field, often by giving answers, solutions or diagnoses."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3057> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The search for economic deposits of minerals, ore, gas, oil, or coal by geological surveys, geophysical prospecting, boreholes and trial pits, or surface or underground headings, drifts, or tunnels."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3058> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A violent, sudden release of energy resulting from powders or gases undergoing instantaneous ignition or from some other means of detonation, often accompanied by a force producing great amounts of heat, major structural damages, shock waves and flying shrapnel."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3071> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "To deprive an owner of property, especially by taking it for public use."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3079> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Discrepancies between private costs and social costs or private advantages and social advantages; the basic concept of externality is interdependence without compensation."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3084> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Animal or plant species which have completely disappeared from the planet."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/308> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any substance composed of two or more unlike atoms held together by chemical bonds characterized by straight-chained, branched or cyclic properties."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/30> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The cause or origin of an unexpected occurrence, failure or loss with the potential for harming human life, property or the environment."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3113> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Land area normally used for crop production but left unsown for one or more growing seasons."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3115> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Arable land not under rotation that is set at rest for a period of time ranging from one to five years before it is cultivated again, or land usually under permanent crops, meadows or pastures, which is not being used for that purpose for a period of at least one year. Arable land which is normally used for the cultivation of temporary crops but which is temporarily used for grazing is included."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3117> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A group comprising parents, offsprings and others closely related or associated with them."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/311> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any organic compound of hydrogen and carbon characterized by a straight chain of the carbon atoms."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3120> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A severe shortage of food, as through crop failure or over population. It may be due to poor harvests following drought, floods, earthquake, war, social conflict, etc."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3123> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The dwelling on a farm as distinguished from utility buildings as a barn, corncrib, milk house."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3138> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The entire animal life of a given region, habitat or geological stratum."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3147> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A binding rule or body of rules established by a government that has been constituted as a union of independent political units or states."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3151> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The act and effect of supplying animals with food."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3154> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Waterlogged, spongy ground containing alkaline decaying vegetation, characterized by reeds, that may develop into peat. It sometimes occurs in the sinkholes of karst region."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3159> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any enzymatic transformation of organic substrates, especially carbohydrates, generally accompanied by the evolution of gas; a physiological counterpart of oxidation, permitting certain organisms to live and grow in the absence of air; used in various industrial processes for the manufacture of products, such as alcohols, acids, and cheese by the action of yeasts, molds, and bacteria; alcoholic fermentation is the best-known example. Also known as zymosis."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3162> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any of a large number of vascular plants composing the division Polypodiophyta, without flowers and fruits."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3169> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Substance added to soil for the purpose of promoting plant life, usually containing nitrogen, potassium and phosphorus, e.g. manure, guano, rock phosphates."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3175> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A material made from small fibres of glass twisted together, which is used for keeping buildings warm, or a plastic strengthened by these fibres and used for making structures such as the outsides of cars and boats."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3177> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A decline in the productivity of an area of land or in its ability to support natural ecosystems or types of agriculture. Degradation may be caused by a variety of factors, including inappropriate land management techniques, soil erosion, salinity, flooding, clearing, pests, pollution, climatic factors, or progressive urbanization."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3179> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Scientific study made in the open air to collect information that can not be obtained in a laboratory."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3181> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any substance used to fill the holes and irregularities in planed or sanded surfaces so as to decrease the porosity of the surface for finish coatings."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3184> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A porous material for separating suspended particulate matter from liquids by passing the liquid through the pores in the filter and sieving out the solids."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3190> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Separation of suspended particles from a liquid, gas, etc., by the action of a filter."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3192> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A system where inert materials, which are not to be mobilized by natural processes even for long time periods, are confined by three barriers: the natural impermeable surroundings, an artificial barrier (such as liner) which can be controlled and, most important, the inert material itself. The concept of final storage includes the possibility to mine the materials in the future if such materials are sufficiently \"clean\" (mono-landfills) and if it becomes economic to mine such ores."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3195> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Help and support provided on matters concerning money."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3197> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Something given, including any form of income or price support; individual investor's monetary offering or contribution to common fund or stock; government agency's or lending aid agency's subsidy, grant, or other contribution to help bolster an economy."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3205> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Procurement of monetary resources or credit to operate a business or acquire assets."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3207> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A pecuniary punishment or penalty imposed by lawful tribunal upon person convicted of crime or misdemeanor."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3209> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Air-borne solid particles, originating from human activity and natural sources, such as wind-blown soil and fires, that eventually settle through the force of gravity, and can cause injury to human and other animal respiratory systems through excessive inhalation."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3219> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A chemical used as a coating for or a component of a combustible material to reduce or eliminate a tendency to burn; used with textiles, plastics, rubbers, paints, and other materials."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3220> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "All necessary precautions to see that fire is not initiated, by ensuring that all necessary fire fighting apparatus is in good order and available for use if fire should break out, and by ensuring that personnel are properly trained and drilled in fighting fire."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3225> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Rules to be followed and safety systems to be adopted for preventing or fighting fire."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3226> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Technical organisation with trained personnel for dealing with fires and other incidents and for co-operating in their prevention."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3232> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A commercial partnership of two or more persons, especially when incorporated."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3237> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The industry of catching, processing and selling fish."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3243> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The production, distribution, and consumption of fish and seafood and all financial aspects of the fishing and seafood industry."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3254> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Raising of fish in inland waters, estuaries or coastal waters."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3260> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Industry for the handling, processing, and packing of fish or shellfish for market or shipment."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3261> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Rules concerning fishing activities; in international law the matter is ruled by the 1958 Geneva Convention."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3282> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "1) Flares use open flames during normal and/or emergency operations to combust hazardous gaseous. The system has no special features to control temperature or time of combustion; however, supplemental fuel may be required to sustain the combustion. Historically, flares have been used to dispose of waste gases in the oil and gas industry and at wastewater treatment plants having anaerobic digestors. Regulation for thermal destruction of hazardous wastes limit the practical use of flaring to combustion of relatively simple hydrocarbons, such as methane from digesters or landfill gas collection systems. \n2) A control device that burns hazardous materials to prevent their release into the environment; may operate continuously or intermittently, usually on top a stack."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3283> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Tests performed in the medical field whose results are available very quickly."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3287> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A substance, such as an extract or a spice, that imparts flavor."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3291> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Plans, referred to in various rules as emissions averaging, or flexible compliance plans, allow facilities to undercontrol some emission points that are too costly to control to mandated levels as long as these units are balanced by overcontrolling other emission units that are more cost-effective to control."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3295> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A process of contact and adhesion whereby the particles of a dispersed substance form large clusters or the aggregation of particles in a colloid to form small lumps, which then settle out."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3298> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "An unusual accumulation of water above the ground caused by high tide, heavy rain, melting snow or rapid runoff from paved areas."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3301> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A general and temporary condition of partial or complete inundation of normally dry land areas from the overflow of inland and/or tidal waters, and/or the unusual and rapid accumulation or runoff of surface waters from any source. A great flow along a watercourse or a flow causing inundation of lands not normally covered by water."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3311> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The forward continuous movement of a fluid through closed or open channels or conduits."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3325> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "1) A system for burning solid carbonaceous fuel efficiently and at a relatively low temperature, thus minimizing the emission of pollutants. The fuel is crushed to very small particles or a powder and mixed with particles of an inert material. The mixture is fed into a bed through which air is pumped vertically upwards, agitating the particles so they behave like a fluid. The forced circulation of air and the small size and separation of fuel particles ensures efficient burning.\n2) A bed of finely divided solid through which air or a gas is blown in a controlled manner so that it behaves as a liquid."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3328> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The addition of the fluorine ion to municipal water supplies in a final concentration of 0.8-1.6 ppm (parts per million) to help prevent dental caries in children."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/332> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A condition of abnormal sensitivity in certain individuals to contact with substances such as proteins, pollens, bacteria, and certain foods. This contact may result in exaggerated physiologic responses such as hay fever, asthma, and in severe enough situations, anaphylactic shock."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3334> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A gaseous or liquid chemical element; a member of the halide family, it is the most electronegative element and the most chemically energetic of the nonmetallic elements; highly toxic, corrosive, and flammable; used in rocket fuels and as a chemical intermediate."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3345> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Bulk feed for livestock, especially hay, straw, etc."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3354> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A material that can be ingested and utilized by the organism as a source of nutrition and energy."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3372> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Potentially harmful substances in any food consumed by humans, or other animals, including inorganic and organic chemicals, viruses and bacteria."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3376> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A commercial establishment in which food is manufactured or packaged for human consumption."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3388> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A substance that can be used or prepared for use as food."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3405> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Trade between countries and firms belonging to different countries."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3406> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A vegetation community dominated by trees and other woody shrubs, growing close enough together that the tree tops touch or overlap, creating various degrees of shade on the forest floor. It may produce benefits such as timber, recreation, wildlife habitat, etc."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3416> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any forest environment, in which plants and animals interact with the chemical and physical features of the environment, in which they live."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/341> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "An overflowing; an inundation or flood, especially when the water is charged with much suspended material."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3423> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A sector of the economy in which an aggregate of establishments is engaged in the management of an extensive area of woodland, often to produce products and benefits such as timber, wildlife habitat, clean water, biodiversity and recreation."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3425> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Planning of forest utilization for wood production, conservation purposes, fauna and flora protection, recreation and water supply."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3430> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A course of action adopted and pursued by government or some other organization, which seeks to preserve or protect an extensive area of woodland, often to produce products and benefits such as timber, wildlife habitat, clean water, biodiversity and recreation."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3438> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Forest resources consist of two separate but closely related parts: the forest land and the trees (timber) on that land."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3440> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The production, distribution, and consumption of goods and services from the industry involved with the process of establishing and managing forests."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3442> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A binding rule or body of rules prescribed by a government to regulate the use and conservation of wooded areas, most often those owned by the government itself."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3465> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The adhesion of different marine organisms to the underwater parts of ships, causing the ships to loose speed."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3483> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Trade name for a group of polyhalogenated hydrocarbons containing fluorine and chlorine; an example is trichlorofluoromethane."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3489> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The living organisms and nonliving materials of an inland aquatic environment."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3495> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any insectivorous anuran amphibian of the family Ranidae, such as Rana temporaria of Europe, having a short squat tailless body with a moist smooth skin and very long hind legs specialized for hopping."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3496> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A deposit of interlocking ice crystals formed by direct sublimation on objects."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3518> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Solids in the air that have been generated by the condensation of vapors, chemical reactions or sublimation (a direct change from solid to gas). Often metallic oxides or metals, these particles are less than 1 micrometer in diameter and may be toxic."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/351> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Technology that, as an alternative to resource-intensive and wasteful industry, aims to utilize resources sparingly, with minimum damage to the environment, at affordable cost and with a possible degree of control over the processes."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3522> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A substance from the point of view of its function or purpose, for example a painting agent or a preserving substance."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3524> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The main soil function is participation in the material transformation and migrating processes occurring in the natural environment on which the functioning of ecosystems depends. The most active participants in the occurring processes are microorganisms and invertebrates, whose activity, different variety, complex structure, and abundance accurately reflect the soil type and its characteristics: so they are important indicators of ecological stability. The variety of soil organisms determine its self-regulatory and self-cleaning capacity."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/352> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A natural or synthetic oxide of aluminum widely distributed in nature, often found as a constituent part of clays, feldspars, micas and other minerals, and as a major component of bauxite."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3533> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The hair-covered, dressed pelt of such a mammal, used in the making of garments and as trimming or decoration."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3536> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A colourless flammable toxic liquid heterocyclic compound, used in the synthesis of nylon."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3542> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The business or trade of dressed furs and garments made from the coats of certain animals."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/354> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A can or box made of aluminium in which material is held or carried."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3553> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Wild animals, including birds and fish, hunted for sport, food or profit."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/356> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A sector of the economy in which an aggregate of commercial enterprises is engaged in the mining and processing of aluminum."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3570> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Company charged with the production and distribution of gas for domestic use."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3581> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "1) Any chemical or heat process used to convert a substance to a gas. \n2) The production of gaseous fuels by reacting hot carbonaceous materials with air, steam or oxygen. The process takes place at high temperature. The gasification product is a mixture of combustible gases and tar compounds, together with particles and water vapour. Depending on the gasification method, the proportion of components varies, but common to all the processes is that the gas has to be purified before it can be used directly in a gas engine or a gas turbine."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3582> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Conversion of a gas to the liquid phase by cooling or compression."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3586> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Interconnected system of pipes for the distribution and supply of gas."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3591> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A long pipe, especially underground, used to transport gas over long distances."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3595> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Gas feedback device: while refuelling gasoline vapors are sucked off and led back again into the storage tank."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3599> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The provision and storage of any fuel gas, or the amount of any fuel gas stored, for the use of a municipality, or other fuel gas user."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3600> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any mollusc of the class Gastropoda, typically having a flattened muscular foot for locomotion and a head that bears stalked eyes."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3604> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Place where gas, especially coal gas, is made."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/360> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A tiny, thin-walled, capillary-rich sac in the lungs where the exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide takes place. Also called air sac."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3615> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The study of the elements and the compounds they form."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3624> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "1) The complex of techniques for the production of new genes and the alteration of the structure of the chromosomes to produce effects beneficial to man, in agriculture and medicine.\n2) The intentional production of new genes and alteration of genomes by the substitution or addition of new genetic material."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3640> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Geogenic factors are those which originate in the soil, as opposed to those of anthropic origin (anthropogenic)."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3646> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The study of the natural features of the earth's surface, comprising topography, climate, soil, vegetation, etc. and man's response to them."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3647> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Disasters caused by movements and deformation of the earth's crust."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3652> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The physical and chemical interactions between the Earth's surface and the natural forces acting upon it to produce landforms. The processes are determined by such natural environmental variables as geology, climate, vegetation and baselevel, to say nothing of human interference. The nature of the process and the rate at which it operates will be influenced by a change in any of these variables."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3654> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The study of the classification, description, nature, origin, and development of present landforms and their relationships to underlying structures, and of the history of geologic changes as recorded by these surface features."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3657> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The application of scientific methods and engineering techniques to the exploitation and use of natural resources."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3658> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "An energy produced by tapping the earth's internal heat. At present, the only available technologies to do this are those that extract heat from hydrothermal convection systems, where water or steam transfer the heat from the deeper part of the earth to the areas where the energy can be tapped. The amount of pollutants found in geothermal vary from area to area but may contain arsenic, boron, selenium, lead, cadmium, and fluorides. They also may contain hydrogen sulphide, mercury, ammonia, radon, carbon dioxide, and methane."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3661> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "1) A pathogenic micro-organism.\n2) Living substance capable of developing into an organ, part, or organism as a whole; a primordium."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3663> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The beginning or the process of development of a spore or seed."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3673> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Slow moving masses of ice which have accumulated either on mountains or in polar regions. They are found where warm, moist air or warm water meets cold air or water. They move, influenced by the force of gravity and the pressure of the ice, above the underlying slush layers and slide downhill, eventually melting at lower levels to form rivers or reaching sea-level, where they form ice shelves or fall into the water as icebergs."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3676> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "1) The study of all aspects of snow and ice; the science that treats quantitatively the whole range of processes associated with all forms of solid existing water. \n2) The study of existing glaciers and ice sheets, and of their physical properties."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3678> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A hard, amorphous, inorganic, usually transparent, brittle substance made by fusing silicates, sometimes borates and phosphates, with certain basic oxides and then rapidly cooling to prevent crystallization."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3687> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A worldwide assembly of national, political party or organizational delegates, or the pact or the agreement that arises from such an assembly that forms, often, the preliminary to an international treaty."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3690> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Models concerning different aspects of reality which can be applied at global level."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3692> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Changes in the surface-air temperature, referred to as the global temperature, brought about by the greenhouse effect which is induced by emission of greenhouse gases into the air."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3715> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A body of top government officials appointed to advise the President or the chief executive officer of a country, usually consisting of the heads of government departments or agencies."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3718> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any course of action adopted and pursued by a ruling political authority or system, which determines the affairs for a nation, state or region."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3721> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Edible, starchy seeds of the grass family (Graminae) usable as food by man and his livestock."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3734> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The interacting system of the biological communities located in biomes characterized by the dominance of indigenous grasses, grasslike plants and forbs, and their non-living environmental surroundings."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3739> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Obtaining a mixture of coarse sand and small water- worn or pounded stones, (used for paths and roads and as an aggregate) from the earth."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3748> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The vegetation on pastures that is available for livestock to feed upon."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3754> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "1) An area of land, not necessarily continuous, near to and sometimes surrounding a large built-up area. The area is kept open by permanent and severe restriction on building. 
2) An irrigated, landscaped, and regularly maintained fuelbreak, usually put to some additional use, such as a golf course, park, or playground. 
3) A planning designation that mandates the setting aside of otherwise developable lands for the purpose of creating natural or semi-natural open spaces. Greenbelts are usually linear parkways, tracts, or belts of land running through or around urban conurbations.
4) An area or zone of open, semi-rural, low-density land surrounding existing major urban areas, but not necessarily continuous. The zone is to be kept open by permanent and severe restrictions on new development."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/375> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A colorless gaseous alkaline compound that is very soluble in water, has a characteristic pungent odour, is lighter than air, and is formed as a result of the decomposition of most nitrogenous organic material."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3760> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Cultivation of plants, especially of out-of-season plants, in glass-enclosed, climate-controlled structures."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3761> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The warming of the Earth's atmosphere caused by the increasing concentration of atmospheric gases, such as water vapour and carbon dioxide. These gases absorb radiation emitted by the Earth, thus slowing down the loss of radiant energy from the Earth back to space."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3763> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A collective expression for those components of the atmosphere that influence the greenhouse effect, namely carbon dioxide, methane, nitrous oxides, ozone, CFCs and water vapour."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3770> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A plot of vegetated land separating or surrounding areas of intensive residential or industrial use and devoted to recreation or park uses."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3774> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "To reduce to powder or small fragments."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3780> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Water that occupies pores and crevices in rock and soil, below the surface and above a layer of impermeable material. It is free to move gravitationally, either downwards towards the impermeable layer or by following a gradient."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3781> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The process, deliberate or inadvertent, of extracting ground water from a source at a rate so in excess of the replenishment that the ground water level declines persistently, threatening exhaustion of the supply or at least a decline of pumping levels to uneconomic depths."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3784> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Contamination of any water found under the earth's surface by any leaching pollutants, such as inorganic compounds (chlorides, nitrates, heavy metals, etc.), synthetic organic chemicals (pesticides, fertilizers, etc.) and pathogens (bacteria, parasites, etc.)."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3788> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "An observable pattern of activity displayed by persons in and as an aggregate."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3805> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any seed-bearing plant of the division Gymnospermae, in which the ovules are borne naked on the surface of the mega sporophylls, which are often arranged in cones."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3806> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A colourless or white mineral used in the building industry and in the manufacture of cement, rubber, paper and plaster of Paris."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3815> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The time required for one-half the atoms of a given amount of radioactive material to undergo radioactive decay."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3822> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "An organic compound bonded with one of the five halogen elements (astatine, bromine, chlorine, fluorine, and iodine). Several of these compounds contribute to reductions in the concentration of ozone in the stratosphere."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3830> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A particular skill performed with the hands."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3847> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The process by which two or more states, sometimes under the auspices of an interstate or international organization, change their legislation relevant to some area of common concern to conform their statutes and to facilitate compliance and enforcement across borders."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3849> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The amount or measure of the crop gathered in a season."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3854> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any material that poses a threat to human health and/or the environment. Typical hazardous substances are toxic, corrosive, ignitable, explosive, or chemically reactive."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3858> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any waste or combination of wastes with the potential to damage human health, living organisms or the environment. Hazardous wastes usually require special handling and disposal procedures which are regulated by national and international laws."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3874> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Laws, ordinances, or codes prescribing sanitary, clean air, etc., standards and regulations, designed to promote and preserve the health of the community and working conditions of businesses."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3885> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any prescribed course or mode of action governing the preliminary examination by a magistrate of basic evidence and charges to determine whether criminal proceedings, a trial or other judicial actions are justified."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/388> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "An open-air entertainment area consisting of stalls, side shows etc."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3892> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "An apparatus that heats or provides heat."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3893> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "An area with poor acid soil, typically dominated by ling (Calluna) or heaths (Erica)."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3904> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A device which transfers heat from a cooler reservoir to a hotter one, expending mechanical energy in the process, especially when the main purpose is to heat the hot reservoir rather than refrigerate the cold one."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3911> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Traffic of large motor vehicles designed to carry heavy loads."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3915> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A metal whose specific gravity is approximately 5.0 or higher."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3917> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A line of closely planted bushes or shrubs, marking the boundaries of a field. The type of hedge varies between parts of the country, and its age can be dated from the number of species of tree and shrub present. Over the last thirty years hedge-row removal has had a marked visual effect on lowland agricultural landscapes. From the farmer's point of view, in areas of predominant arable or intensively managed grazing, there is little or no economic justification for retaining hedges."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3935> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "An animal that feeds on grass and other plants."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3958> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The level of water when the tide is at its highest level."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3971> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The process by which small but cumulative changes in the learned, nonrandom, systematic behavior and knowledge of a people occur from generation to generation."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3974> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Monument built in memory of an historical event."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3977> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Place where significant historical events occurred and which is important to an indigenous culture or a community."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3983> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A systematic written account comprising a chronological record of events (as affecting a city, state, nation, institution, science, or art) and usually including a philosophical explanation of the cause and origin of such events."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3995> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A large animal with four legs which people ride on or use for carrying things or pulling vehicles."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/3999> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A place where people who are ill or injured are treated and taken care of by doctors and nurses."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/399> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The branch of chemistry dealing with techniques which yield any type of information about chemical systems."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4032> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A binding rule or body of rules prescribed by a government to regulate the buying, selling, leasing, construction or maintenance of dwelling places."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4046> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "An interruption, cessation or disorder of human bodily functions, systems or organs resulting from genetic or developmental errors, infection, nutritional deficiency, toxicity, illness or unfavorable environmental factors."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4055> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A branch of biological sciences that studies the functions of organs and tissues in human beings."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4062> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Cities, towns, villages, and other concentrations of human populations which inhabit a given segment or area of the environment. Human settlements are associated with numerous and complex environmental, pollution, and living condition problems for planning and management."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4070> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The more or less decomposed organic matter in the soil. Besides being the source of most of the mineral salts needed by plants, humus improves the texture of the soil and holds water, so reducing the loss of nutrients by leaching."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4077> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A tropical cyclone of great intensity; any wind reaching a speed of more than 73 miles per hour (117 kilometers per hour) is said to have hurricane force."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4107> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Flammable, poisonous gas with characteristic odour of rotten eggs, perceptible in air in a dilution of 0.002 mg/l. It is used as a reagent in chemical analysis; extremely hazardous; collapse, coma and death from respiratory failure may come within a few seconds after one or two inspirations; low concentrations produce irritation of conjunctiva and mucous membranes. Headache, dizziness, nausea, lassitude may appear after exposure."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4126> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The science that deals with the principles and practices of good health."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4131> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The dense substance formed by the freezing of water to the solid state; it commonly occurs in the form of hexagonal crystals."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4136> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The determination of the specific substance or substances that are causing pollution."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4140> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The process of converting 'raw' remotely sensed data into a usable form through the application of various transformations such as supervised and unsupervised classification schemes."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4141> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Codes published by Intergovernmental Maritime Consultative Organisation (IMCO) relating to international shipping, particularly regarding safety and marine pollution."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4144> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "One of the possible consequences of the introduction of plant species in an area where they are not indigenous."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4146> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The reception of material, such as pollutants, by the environment and from any source."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4149> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Damage caused by pollution from a distinct source of emission."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4150> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The prediction of immissions is calculated on the basis of the pollutant load, the source height, the wind speed and the dispersion coefficient."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4151> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Maximum levels of selected pollutants which would lead to unacceptable air quality."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4158> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A branch of biological science concerned with the native or acquired resistance of higher animal forms and humans to infection with microorganisms."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/415> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Behaviour of animals in their normal environment, including all the processes, both internal and external, by which they respond to changes in their environment."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4160> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Actions, procedures or installations undertaken to reduce the extent or degree of negative effects on human health and the ecosystem introduced by human design or interaction with the environment."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4161> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Instrument which samples atmospheric suspensoids by impaction; such instruments consist of a housing which constrains the air flow past a sensitized sampling plate."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4162> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Precautionary measures, actions or installations implemented to avert negative effects on the environment."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4163> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Elements of an action which cause damage to the surrounding environment."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4177> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Sudden immission in considerable amount of one or more pollutants in the atmosphere, in a water body or in the soil."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4178> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Noise characterized by transient short-duration disturbances distributed essentially uniformly over the useful passband of a transmission system."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4187> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The gain derived from capital, from labour or effort, or both combined, including profit or gain through sale or conversion of capital."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/419> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Excrement from animals that may be dried and burned to generate energy or converted to liquid or gaseous fuels, such as methane, through chemical processes."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4205> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Technologies employed by the native inhabitants of a country and which constitute an important part of its cultural heritage and should therefore be protected against exploitation by industrialized countries; the problem of indigenous knowledge has been discussed during the Rio Conference but it does not receive much protection under the Biodiversity Convention. Article 8 mandates that parties \"respect, preserve and maintain knowledge, innovations and practices of indigenous and local communities embodying traditional life styles... and promote their wider application with the approval and involvement of holders of such knowledge, innovations and practices and encourage the equitable sharing of benefits arising from them\"."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/421> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Investigation carried out in animals for research purposes."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4227> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The disposal of any waste generated by a manufacturing or processing process by the agency or body which produced it."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4229> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Materials generally discarded from industrial operations or derived from manufacturing processes."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4233> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The guiding procedure, philosophy or course of action for the protection of natural resources from pollution generated by manufacturing or business enterprises."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4247> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A binding rule or body of rules prescribed by a government to regulate working conditions or the acquisition, processing and disposal of materials by the aggregate of factories, companies and enterprises in one or more manufacturing or technically productive fields."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4253> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The process of making arrangements or preparations to facilitate the manufacturing, producing and processing of goods or merchandise."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4256> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Pollution as a result of industrial processes and manufacturing."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4258> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any process of converting or transforming raw materials and other resources into goods or services which have value."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4273> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Waste materials discarded from industrial operations, or derived from manufacturing processes; may be solid, sludge (wet solids) or liquid wastes and may or may not be considered hazardous."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4278> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A system of land use planning that forms zones or boundaries to be used only by manufacturing or business enterprises."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4282> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The process of waste inertisation includes solidification and stabilisation; stabilisation is the process used for reduction of hazard potential of the waste by converting the contaminants into their least soluble, least immobile, or least toxic form. Solidification physically binds or encapsulates the waste in a monolithic solid of high structural integrity. Thus solidification may be used for powders, liquids or gases."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4283> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Wastes that do not undergo any significant physical, chemical, or biological transformations when deposited in a landfill."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4289> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Invasion of crop by parasites. Among vertebrate animals, many crop pests are mammals, especially in the order of rodents and birds. Among invertebrates, certain species of gastropods and a large number of roundworms from the class of nematodes harm crops. The most varied and numerous species of crop pests are arthropods-insects, arachnids and some species of millipedes and crustaceans. Diseases vary from viral, bacterial, and nutritional to fungal, environmental and non-specific. The FAO has estimated that annual worldwide losses done by plant pests and diseases amount to approximately 20-25% of the potential worldwide yield of food crops."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4291> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Movement of water through the soil surface into the ground."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/429> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A branch of agriculture concerned with the breeding and feeding of domestic animals."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/42> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A type of pollution which washes out of the atmosphere as dilute sulphuric and nitric acids. It tends to be a regional rather than a global phenomenon, linked to particular industrial activities and meteorological conditions. It includes rain, more than normally acidic snow, mist, sleet, fog, gas and dry particles. It upsets the balance of nature, disrupting ecosystems, and destroys forests and woodlands, plants and crops; kills aquatic life by altering the chemical balance of lakes and rivers and corrodes building materials and fabrics. The pollutants are caused principally by discharges from power station chimneys of sulphur dioxide and nitrogen oxides released by burning fossil fuels, coal and oil."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4309> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "An organized system of providing assistance or aid to individuals who are seeking information, such as by using databases and other information sources to communicate or supply knowledge or factual data."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4311> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any coordinated assemblage of persons, devices and institutions used for communicating or exchanging knowledge or data, such as by simple verbal communication, or by completely computerized methods of storing, searching and retrieving information."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4317> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Electron magnetic radiation whose wavelengths lie in the range from 0.75 or 0.8 micrometer to 1000 micrometers."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4321> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The basic network or foundation of capital facilities or community investments which are necessary to support economic and community activities."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4325> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A stress upon an organism that disrupts the structure or function and results in a pathological process."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4326> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A dispersion of a pigment or a solution of a dye in a carrier vehicle, yielding a fluid, paste, or powder to be applied to and dried on a substrate; writing, marking, drawing, and printing inks are applied by several methods to paper, metal, plastic, wood, glass, fabric, or other substrate."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4333> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A lake, river, or other body of water wholly within the boundaries of a state."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/434> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Noise caused by animals such as dogs kept in kennels or in private homes as pets."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4358> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A class of the Arthropoda typically having a segmented body with an external, chitinous covering, a pair of compound eyes, a pair of antennae, three pairs of mouthparts, and two pairs of wings."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4376> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The protection provided against risks or a risk, often as specified by the type of protection or the item being protected."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4398> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A transference of binary coded information items between two or more computers across any communications channel capable of carrying electromagnetic signals."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4401> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A sum paid or charged for the use of money or for borrowing money over a given time period."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4402> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A group of people who share common traits, attitudes, beliefs or objectives and who have formed a formal organization to serve specific concerns of the membership."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4417> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Cooperation in international efforts to support global environmental goals. Solutions to environmental problems such as trans-boundary airborne and waterborne pollution, ozone depletion and climate change require action by all responsible countries."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4427> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The political or diplomatic interaction or dealings between independent nations that pertain to ecological concerns."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4438> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The political or diplomatic interaction or dealings between independent nations."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4441> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Freedom from danger or the quality of averting risk of harm to persons, property or the environment shared across one or more national boundaries; consequently, the combined efforts of more than one nation to achieve or preserve that state."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4448> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Portions of a geographical area which constitutes a hydrogeological unit as the catchment area for a single river which are under the jurisdiction of two or more countries."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4451> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Method employed in the assessment of the meaning and significance of data, results, facts, etc."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4454> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "1) The area between land and sea which is regularly exposed to the air by the tidal movement of the sea. Marine organisms that inhabit the intertidal zones have to adapt to periods of exposure to air and to the waves created by wind, which makes it the most physically demanding of the marine habitats. \n2) The shore zone between the highest and lowest tides."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4473> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A reversal in the usual direction of a process, as in the change of density of water at 4° C."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4474> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The atmosphere layer through which an inversion occurs."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4475> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any animal lacking a backbone, including all species not classified as vertebrates."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4478> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any item of value purchased for profitable return, as income, interest or capital appreciation."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4483> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A nonmetallic halogen element; the poisonous, corrosive dark plates or granules are readily sublimed; insoluble in water, soluble in common solvents; used as germicide and antiseptic, in dyes, tinctures, and pharmaceuticals, in engraving lithography, and as a catalyst and analytical reagent."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4485> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The process in which ions are exchanged between a solution and an insoluble solid, usually a resin."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4492> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A region of the earth's atmosphere, extending from about 60 to 1000 kilometers above the earth's surface, in which there is a high concentration of free electrons formed as a result of ionizing radiation entering the atmosphere from space."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4505> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "1) To supply land with water so that crops and plants will grow or grow stronger."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4507> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A permanent irrigation conduit constructed to convey water from the source of supply to one or more farms."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4509> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Farming based on the artificial distribution and application of water to arable land to initiate and maintain plant growth."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/450> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any living organism characterized by voluntary movement, the possession of cells with noncellulose cell walls and specialized sense organs enabling rapid response to stimuli, and the ingestion of complex organic substances such as plants and other animals."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4524> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The fine-grained creamy-white dentine forming the tusks of elephants, and the teeth or tusks of certain other large animals such as the walrus; it has long been esteemed for a wide variety of ornamental articles."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4530> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Persons united in a joint liability or indebtedness. Two or more persons jointly liable for the same debt."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4541> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The power of a court to hear and decide a case or make a certain order."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4550> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A thin oil distilled from petroleum or shale oil, used as a fuel for heating and cooking, in lamps, and as a denaturant for alcohol."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4567> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A room or building with scientific equipment for doing scientific tests or for teaching science, or a place where chemicals or medicines are produced."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4571> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Tests or investigations carried out in a laboratory."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4575> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Discarded materials produced by analytical and research activities in a laboratory."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4584> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The dynamics or general state of the association between management and non-management employees in an enterprise, industry or nation, with special attention to the maintenance of agreements, collective bargaining and the status of unions."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4586> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A material which contains a substantial quantity of a cellulose derivative, most commonly nitrocellulose but sometimes a cellulose ester, such as cellulose acetate or cellulose butyrate, or a cellulose ether such as ethyl cellulose; used to give a glossy finish, especially on brass and other bright metals."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4589> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A body of water cut off from the open sea by coral reefs or sand bars."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/458> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The situation in which two chemicals upon interaction interfere in such a way that the action of one partially or completely inhibits the effects of the other."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
