<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4590> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "1) The depression in the Earth's surface occupied or formerly occupied by a lake and containing its shore features. \n2) The area from which a lake receives drainage."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4593> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The direct or indirect human alteration of the biological, physical, chemical or radiological integrity of lake water, or a lake ecosystem."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4600> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The permission or freedom to use, enter, approach or pass to and from a tract of land, which often consists of real estate property."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4603> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The system of registering certain legal estates or interests in land. It describes the land and any additional rights incidental to it, such as rights of way over adjoining land."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4607> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The maximum extent to which ground or soil area may be exploited without degradation or depletion."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4609> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Removal of trees, undergrowth, etc. in preparation for ploughing, building, etc."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4610> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The care, preservation and re-use of solid areas of the earth's surface, especially soil regions valued as a natural resource or utilized as an agricultural resource."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4612> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Land cover is the physical state of the land surface. It is the combination of vegetation, soil, rock, water and human-made structures, which make up the earth's landscape. The land cover is the interface between the earth's crust and the atmosphere, influencing the exchange of energy and matter in the climatic system and biogeochemical cycles."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4621> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The oldest method of waste disposal for the solid matter discarded in the domestic dustbin, along with the packaging material and paper from high street shops and offices. Landfill sites are usually disused quarries and gravel pits. When they were filled, previous practice was to cover them up with soil and forget about them. Housing estates have been built, often with disastrous consequences, on old landfill dumps. Waste burial has now become a serious technology and a potential source of energy. Landfill sites can be designed to be bioreactors, which deliberately produce methane, gas as a source of biofuel or alternative energy. Traditionally, waste tips remained exposed to air and aerobic microbes - those which thrive in air - in order to turn some of the waste into compost. However, open tips also encourage vermin, smell in hot weather and disfigure the landscape. In the 1960s, as a tidier and safer option, landfill operators began to seal each day's waste in a clay cell. While excluding vermin, the clay also excluded air. Decomposition relied on anaerobic microbes, which die in air. However, the process produced methane (natural gas), which was a safety hazard. The methane is now extracted by sinking a network of perforated pipes into the site."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4624> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Landfill gas is highly dangerous as methane is highly explosive; therefore it must be controlled at all operational landfill sites, whether by active or passive ventilation or both especially in the case of deep sites. There exist venting systems for shallow and deep sites respectively."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4626> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Liquid that has seeped through solid waste in a landfill and has extracted soluble dissolved or suspended materials in the process."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4633> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The use, settlement or possession of solid areas of the earth's surface."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4635> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The activity of designing, organizing or preparing for the future use of solid areas of the earth's surface, especially regions valued for natural resources, utilized as agricultural resources or considered for human settlement."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4644> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A register or survey of land, containing information on the surface of properties, tenants' names, commencing with the earliest owners through successive ownership and partitions, and such like."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4646> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The treatment of any unusable land usually by filling with refuse or levelling until the land can be brought into productive use."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4648> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The traits, patterns, and structure of a specific geographic area, including its biological composition, its physical environment, and its anthropogenic or social patterns. An area where interacting ecosystems are grouped and repeated in similar form."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/464> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The waters, including ice shelves, that surround the continent of Antarctica, which comprise the southernmost parts of the Pacific, Atlantic and Indian oceans, and also the Ross, Amundsen, Bellingshausen and Weddell seas."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4650> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Landscapes might change through time as a result of human activities or natural processes such as fires or natural disasters. Changes in landscape structure can be documented by using data from aerial photographs or satellite images, and new technologies, such as remote sensing and geographic information systems."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4653> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The safeguarding, for public enjoyment, of landscape and of opportunities for outdoor recreation, tourism and similar activities; the concept includes the preservation and enhancement not only of what has been inherited but the provision of new amenities and facilities."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4659> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The aspect of the land use planning process that deals with physical, biological, aesthetic, cultural, and historical values and with the relationships and planning between these values, land uses, and the environment."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/465> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "An area within the Antarctic Circle that includes the fifth largest continent and its surrounding waters, consisting mostly of thick ice shelves."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4660> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Elaboration and implementation of strategies and measures for the conservation, preservation, suitable use, and renewal of natural resources and nature or man-made components of landscape, in particular wildlife and natural systems of various standing."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4661> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Area where landscape is protected for its particular features in order to maintain its role in contributing to the wider enjoyment of the countryside."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4662> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Using parts of landscape in a way that heavily modifies its features."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4682> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The interdisciplinary process of evaluating, organising, and controlling the present and the future development and use of lands and their resources in terms of their suitability on sustained yield basis. Includes an overall ecological evaluation in terms of specific kinds of uses as well as evaluations of social, economic, and physical contexts to the land concerned."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4684> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Type of management and utilization of the soil."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/468> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Action resulting from or influenced by human activity or intervention."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4691> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any sizable building which relies on machinery that converts energy released from the rapid burning of a fuel-air mixture into mechanical energy."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4702> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The act of washing and ironing clothes, linen, etc."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4710> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any variety of activities associated with promoting compliance and obedience to the binding rules of a state, especially the prevention, investigation, apprehension or detention of individuals suspected or convicted of violating those rules."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4719> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Complex of rules fixed by law or custom which regulate social relations."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4722> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "1) The process of separating a liquid from a solid (as in waste liquid by percolation into the surrounding soil. \n2) Extraction of soluble components of a solid mixture by percolating a solvent through it.\n3) To lose or cause to lose soluble substances by the action of a percolating liquid."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4724> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Lead compounds are present as gasoline additives, in paint, ceramic products, roofing, caulking, electrical applications, tubes, or containers. Lead exposure may be due to air, water, food, or soil. Lead in the air is primarily due to lead-based fuels and the combustion of solid waste, coal, oils, and emissions from alkyl lead manufacturers, wind blown dust volcanoes, the burning of lead-painted surfaces, and cigarette smoke. Lead in drinking water comes from leaching from lead pipes, connectors, and solder in both the distribution system and household plumbing."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4727> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A binding rule or body of rules prescribed by a government to reduce or eliminate the lead content in petroleum fuels used in vehicular and other engines that pollute the air with lead-carrying exhaust."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4728> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A measure of the amount of lead or lead salts absorbed by the body as a possible sign of acute or chronic lead poisoning, which can affect the nervous, digestive or muscular systems."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4730> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The main organ of photosynthesis and transpiration in higher plants, usually consisting of a flat green blade attached to the stem directly or by a stalk."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4739> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The fundamental law or judicial precedent that warrants or supports a subsequent decision or action by any governmental, corporate or private entity."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/473> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A chemical substance, produced by microorganisms and synthetically, that has the capacity to inhibit the growth of, and even to destroy, bacteria and other microorganisms."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4743> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any order or rule issued by a government stipulating its procedures for the creation, execution or adjudication of laws."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4744> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The means by which a right is enforced or the violation of a right is prevented, redressed, or compensated."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4746> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The exact wording or language of a law or other document in conformity with the law or having the authority of law."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4752> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Rules concerning the limits of pollutant emissions."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4759> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The power of a deliberative assembly of persons or delegates to bring a bill, resolution or special act to an official, legally binding status."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4760> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The skill, knowledge, qualification, capacity or authority to make, give or enact rules with binding force upon a population or jurisdiction."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4762> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Knowledge or a service providing knowledge concerning actual and proposed laws, including approval status, the history and content of deliberative proceedings and the specific language of those laws."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4764> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The department, assembly, or body of persons that makes statutory laws for a state or nation."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4767> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Sports and recreational activities carried out in the time free from work or other duties."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4777> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A large order of scaly-winged insects, including the butterflies, skippers, and moths; adults are characterized by two pairs of membranous wings and sucking mouthparts, featuring a prominent, coiled proboscis."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4782> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A progressive, malignant disease of the blood forming organs; a distorted proliferation and development of leukocytes and their precursors in the blood and bone marrow."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4788> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Subjection to a legal obligation, such as financial recompense or ecological reparations, for any harm or damage inflicted on persons, property or the environment in the course of commercial or recreational activity in, on or near a sea."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/478> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Agent that inhibits the growth of barnacles and other marine organisms on a ship's bottom (an antifouling paint or other coating). Organo-tin compounds have been the most often used agents in this application since they are effective against both soft and hard fouling organisms. However, in spite of their performance, they have a negative impact on the marine environment and their long half life in the environment, has prompted marine paint manufacturers to look for a nonpersistent alternative."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4793> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Place where books and other literary materials are kept."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4797> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Procedures performed by administrative agencies in conjunction with issuance of various types of licences."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4799> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Composite organisms formed by the symbiosis between species of fungi and an algae. They are either crusty patches or bushy growths on tree trunks, stone walls, roofs or garden paths. Because they have no actual roots they get their sustenance from the atmosphere and rainwater. Lichens play an important role in the detection and monitoring of pollution, especially sulphur dioxide, as they are highly sensitive to pollution and different species disappear if pollution reaches specific levels."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4802> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The phases, changes, or stages through which an organism passes throughout its lifetime."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4808> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The particular attitudes, habits or behaviour associated with an individual or group."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4819> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Extraction of brown coal from natural deposits; lignite is a brownish-black solid fuel in the second stage in the development of coal. It has a little over half the heating value of bituminous or anthracite coal."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4830> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The study of bodies of fresh water with reference to their plant and animal life, physical properties, geographical features, etc."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4832> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Point noise sources placed one after the other one as, for instance, in a row of cars moving on a road."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4834> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A layer of synthetic or natural materials, on the sides of or beneath a landfill, landfill cell or surface impoundment, that restricts the downward or lateral escape of liquids carrying leachate into the surrounding environment."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4840> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A gaseous compound or mixture converted to the liquid phase by cooling or compression; examples are liquefied petroleum gas (LPG), liquefied natural gas (LNG), liquid oxygen, and liquid ammonia."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4843> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any fertilizer substance with a moisture content of over ninety percent, usually consisting of animal excrement with water added."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4844> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A state of matter intermediate between that of crystalline substances and gases in which a substance has the capacity to flow under extremely small shear stresses and conforms to the shape of a confining vessel, but is relatively incompressible, lacks the capacity to expand without limit, and can posses a free surface."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4845> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Fluid wastes, consisting of sewage and domestic wastewater, or processed water, or other liquids, produced by industrial activity, particularly by such industries as pulp and paper production, food processing, and the manufacture of chemicals."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4850> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Written material such as poetry, novels, essays, especially works of imagination characterized by excellence of style and expression and by themes of general or enduring interest."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4853> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The identification, description, analysis and classification of books and other materials used or consulted in the preparation of a work."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4857> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Straw, hay or similar material used as bedding by animals."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4862> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Cattle, horses, and similar animals kept for domestic use especially on a farm."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4864> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Breeding of cattle, horses and similar animals."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4866> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "An element or characteristic of a habitation considered in light of its ability to sustain and promote the health and general well-being of occupants."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4871> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any reptile of the suborder Lacertilia, especially those of the family Lacertidae, typically having an elongated body, four limbs, and a small tail: includes the gechos, iguanas, chameleons, monitors, and slow worms."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4879> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The power of a government agency or its administrators to administer and implement laws and government policies for a city, town or small district."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4884> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The theory and practice of all public money matters pertaining to city, town or small district governments."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4886> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The supply of heat, either in the form of steam or hot water, from a central source to a group of buildings."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4891> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Traffic moving within a city, town, or area and subject to frequent stops, as distinguished from long distance traffic."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4897> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A self -propelled engine driven by steam, electricity or diesel power and used for drawing trains along railway tracks."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4902> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Traffic moving over extended areas, great distances and usually not subject to frequent stops."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4909> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The act or process of predicting and calculating the likely conditions or occurrences for an extended and future point in time, often involving the study and analysis of pertinent data."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4911> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The prevailing tendency or general direction expected for some observed value over a lengthy and extended period of time, often determined by studying and analyzing statistical data."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4914> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The result of a business operation where overhead costs are greater than the receipts or income."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4916> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Destruction of biotopes produced by environmental degradation which in turn is caused by air- or water-borne pollution."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4917> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The magnitude of the physiological sensation produced by a sound, which varies directly with the physical intensity of sound but also depends on frequency of sound and waveform."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4931> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any relatively unsophisticated technical equipment or method with an amplitude or functionality below what is available in a similar or comparable system."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4934> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A substance used to reduce friction between parts or objects in relative motion."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4956> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "An aim or objective pertaining to the production, distribution and use of income, wealth and commodities in a country, region or other large area, typically concerned with governmental fiscal and monetary policy as it affects employment, consumption, investment and growth levels."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4965> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A class of physical phenomena associated with moving electricity, including the mutual mechanical forces among magnets and electric currents."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4967> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A series of addresses or e-mail addresses to which solicited or unsolicited mass mailings can be sent."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/496> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Science whose results are employed in technical applications."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4982> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any animal of the Mammalia, a large class of warm-blooded vertebrates having mammary glands in the female, a thoracic diaphragm, and a four-chambered heart. The class includes the whales, carnivores, rodents, bats, primates, etc."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4985> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Government, control, superintendence, physical or manual handling or guidance; act of managing by direction or regulation, or administration, as management of family, or of household, etc."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4988> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Planned use of natural resources, in particular of non-renewable resources, in accordance with principles that assure their optimum long-term economic and social benefits."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/498> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "1) A flexible and participatory approach to developing economically viable, regionally applicable and sustainable technology.\n2) Technology designed to be used in developing countries. Typical requirements are that it should: be easy to use by the unskilled; have no difficult-to-get parts; be easily repaired on the spot. Typical example: a simple windmill to pump water rather than a diesel-driven pump. The terms `alternative', `intermediate' and `appropriate' are often used interchangeably."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4998> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Plant communities and trees that inhabit tidal swamps, muddy silt, and sand banks at the mouths of rivers and other low-lying areas which are regularly inundated by the sea, but which are protected from strong waves and currents. Mangroves are the only woody species that will grow where the land is periodically flooded with sea water; individual species have adapted themselves to different tidal levels, to various degrees of salinity, and to the nature of the mud or soil. Mangrove swamps and thickets support hundreds of terrestrial, marine, and amphibian species; have a special role in supporting estuarine fisheries; provide shelter, refuge and food for many forms of wildlife."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/4999> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A wet, spongy area of land in tropical climates and along coastal regions that is dominated by mangrove trees and shrubs, particularly red mangroves (Rhizophora), black mangroves (Avicennia) and white mangroves (Laguncularia)."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5006> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The process or act of exchanging, buying or selling any manufactured product, or the raw materials for any manufacturing process."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/500> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Authorization or permission for setting up or making adjustments to a building or to a mechanical or electrical system or apparatus."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/501> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "1) The cultivation and harvest of freshwater or marine animals and plants, in ponds, tanks, cages or on protected beds. This is usually done in inland waters, estuaries or coastal waters. It is estimated that commercial fish farming accounts for more than 10% of the world's fish needs. Fish farming usually concentrates on molluscs, including oysters, mussels and clams, because they are usually immobile and fetch high prices. Shrimps and salmon are also farmed, but the stock have to be caught in the wild first, so that they can be brought up to commercial standards in pens. Aquaculture in not new. In Asia freshwater fish have been farmed for some 4.000 years, usually on small farms. \n2) The use of artificial means to increase the production of aquatic organisms in fresh or salt water."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5027> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A branch of biology that deals with those living organisms which inhabit the sea."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5033> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Marine environments include estuaries, coastal marine and nearshore zones, and open-ocean-deep-sea regions."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5035> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The harvest of animals and plants from the ocean to provide food and recreation for people, food for animals, and a variety of organic materials for industry."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5042> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The assessment of marine pollution by an integrated chemical, ecological and toxicological survey."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5044> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any detrimental alteration of the marine environment caused by the intentional or accidental release of dangerous or toxic substances, such as industrial, commercial and urban waste water."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5051> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "That system of law which particularly relates to marine commerce and navigation, to business transacted at sea or relating to navigation, to ships and shipping, to seamen, to the transportation of persons and property by sea, and to marine affairs generally."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5052> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Travelling on the sea by means of boats, ships, etc."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5058> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Place of commercial activity in which articles are bought and sold. Also purchase and sale. In a limited sense market is the range of bid and asked prices reported by brokers making the market in over-the-counter securities. Also the demand for any particular article."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/505> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any watery environment, from small to large, from pond to ocean, in which plants and animals interact with the chemical and physical features of the environment."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5080> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A pastime, diversion, exercise or other means of enjoyment and relaxation that is shared with or performed by a large number of people."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5086> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The substance of which a product is made or composed."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5093> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The study of the nature, behaviour, and use of materials applied to science and technology."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5097> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The branch of mathematics most explicitly concerned with the limit process or the concept of convergence; includes the theories of differentiation, integration and measure, infinite series, and analytic functions."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5107> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The maximum exposure to a physical or chemical agent allowed in an 8-hour work day to prevent disease or injury."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5110> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Strictly a term for a field of permanent grass used for hay, but also applied to rich, waterside grazing areas that are not suitable for arable cultivation."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5128> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The branch of engineering concerned with the design, construction, and operation of machines."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5135> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The science and art of treating and healing."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5144> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The science and art of treating and healing."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5147> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A plant formation found in the Mediterranean area comprising mainly lowgrowing, xerophilous evergreen trees and shrubs. It results mainly from the deterioration of the original vegetation by grazing and burning."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5148> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A change of the state of a substance from the solid phase to the liquid phase. Also known as fusion."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/514> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Plants adapted for a partially or completely submerged life."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5150> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A thin tissue that encloses or lines biological cells, organs, or other structures. It consists of a double layer of lipids with protein molecules between the two layers. Membranes are permeable to water and fat-soluble substances but not to such polar molecules as sugars."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5161> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "All the chemical reactions that take place in a living organism, comprising both anabolism and catabolism. Basal metabolism is the energy exchange of an animal at rest. Catabolism is the synthesis of complex molecules from simpler ones. Catabolism is the breaking down by organisms of complex molecules into simpler ones with the liberation of energy."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5169> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A process in which a chemical or some other substance is applied to metals as a way to clean, protect, alter or modify appearance or physical properties, especially surface properties."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5186> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A metallurgical process in which ore mixtures are heated above melting point to extract or yield a crude metal."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/518> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Layers of rock, sand or gravel that can absorb water and allow it to flow. An aquifer acts as a groundwater reservoir when the underlying rock is impermeable. This may be tapped by wells for domestic, agricultural or industrial use. A serious environmental problem arises when the aquifer is contaminated by the seepage of sewage or toxins from waste dumps. If the groundwater in coastal areas is over-used salt water can seep into the aquifer."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5197> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The science concerned with the atmosphere and its phenomena."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5199> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A colourless, odourless, and tasteless gas, lighter than air and reacting violently with chlorine and bromine in sunlight, a chief component of natural gas; used as a source of methanol, acetylene, and carbon monoxide. Also known as methyl hydride."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5210> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A term applied loosely to any large city, but specifically to that city in a country which is the seat of government, of ecclesiastical authority, or of commercial activity."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5219> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The local, rather uniform climate of a specific place or habitat, compared with the climate of the entire area of which it is a part."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/521> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Growing crops as opposed to dairy farming, cattle farming, etc."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5226> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The separation or removal from a liquid of particulates and microorganisms in the size range of 0.1 to 0.2 microns in diameter."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5229> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Pollutant which exists in very small traces in water."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5230> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The interpretative application of microscope magnification to the study of materials that cannot be properly seen by the unaided eye."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5231> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "An electromagnetic wave which has a wavelength between about 0.3 and 30 centimeters, corresponding to frequencies of 1-100 gigahertz; however there are no sharp boundaries between microwaves and infrared and radio waves."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5262> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Filling of disused mines with soil, crushed stone, or waste materials in order to restore the geological, agricultural and landscape features of the concerned area."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5267> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A fiber manufactured from glass, rock, or slag generally for use in fabricating heat insulation."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/527> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The planting and care of woody plants, especially trees."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5282> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The process of making arrangements or preparations to facilitate the production of goods or services at an output that would require the lowest possible expenditure of money, time or labor."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5286> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A district where mineral exploitation is performed."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5295> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Mining is an intensive type of land use with potential for environmental impact over a limited area. When closure occurs, it should address both environmental and safety aspects. Mine reclamation is an ongoing program designed to restore to an acceptable state the physical, chemical and biological quality or potential of air, land and water regimes disturbed by mining. The objective of mine reclamation is to prevent or minimize adverse long-term environmental impacts, and create a self-sustaining ecosystem as near as practicable to what existed before the mining activity."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5303> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A group that is different racially, politically, etc. from a larger group of which it is a part."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5307> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The tendency or capacity of two or more liquids to form a uniform blend, that is, to dissolve in each other; degrees are total miscibility, partial miscibility, and immiscibility."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/530> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The scientific study of the material remains of the cultures of historical or prehistorical peoples."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5311> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any procedure or action undertaken to reduce the adverse impacts that a project or activity may have on the environment."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5316> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A forest composed of several tree species."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5317> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Use of land for more than one purpose; e.g. grazing of livestock, watershed and wildlife protection, recreation, and timber production."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5318> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The intermingling of different materials to produce a homogeneous mixture."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5322> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Living quarters mounted on wheels and capable of being towed by a motor vehicle."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5327> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "An investigative technique using a mathematical or physical representation of a system or theory that accounts for all or some its known properties. Models are often used to test the effect of changes of system components on the overall performance of the system."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5332> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "1) The water vapour content of the atmosphere, or the total water substances (gaseous, liquid and solid) present in a given volume of air. \n2) Water that is dispersed through a gas in the form of water vapour or small droplets, dispersed through a solid, or condensed on the surface of a solid."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5343> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Financial determination, adjustment, estimation, or appraisal for purposes of levying a tax, charge or fine."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5350> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Interconnected group of monitoring stations for the surveillance of pollution."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5352> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Station where the presence, effect, or level of any polluting substance in air or water, noise and blasting, radiation, transport movements, land subsidence, or change in the character of vegetation are measured quantitatively or qualitatively."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5357> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The market condition where a particular commodity or service has only one seller, either because the seller has exclusive possession of an essential input or because large economies of scale inhibit the entrance of a competitor into the market."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5360> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "An object, especially large and made of stone, built to remember and show respect to a person or group of people, or a special place made for this purpose."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5369> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The branch of biology concerned with the form and structure of organisms."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5371> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The number of deaths occurring in a given population for a given period of time."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5388> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any gaseous or liquid flammable fuel that burns in an internal combustion engine."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/538> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The art and science of designing and building structures, or large groups of structures, in keeping with aesthetic and functional criteria."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5392> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Gases vented to the atmosphere by internal-combustion-engine driven vehicles."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5405> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Area characterized by conspicuous peaks, ridges, or mountain ranges."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5419> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Multilateralism stands for a long-held but rarely achieved ideal, namely the voluntary co-operation of nations for peace and development. Multilateral initiatives are undermined or diluted by ultra-nationalist, bilateral and regional initiatives. Multilateralism may be undercut by the uncoordinated decisions of those contributing to it. Multilateralism constitutes the democracy of international society. An enlightened multilateralism enhances the specific interests of states while advancing their common cause."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5424> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "1) Coordinated management for the most judicious and harmonious use of the land on a long term basis under the concept of combining two or more uses and/or purposes with attention to sustainability and nonimpairment of the natural resources and land area.\n2) Use of land for more than one purpose; e.g. grazing of livestock, watershed and wildlife protection, recreation, and timber production."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5428> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The aggregation of services offered by a town or city in which streets and other public areas are kept clean, such as through trash pick-ups, street sweeping and decontamination of water, soil and other natural resources."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5430> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The guiding procedure, philosophy or course of action regarding the protection of natural resources in local settings, cities or towns."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5431> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A town, city, or other district having powers of local self-government."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5432> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Broadly, a law or body of laws that pertains solely to the citizens and inhabitants of a state; narrowly, a law or body of laws pertaining to towns, cities, villages and their local governments."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5433> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The jurisdiction, position or status of city, town or local government."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5439> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any publicly or privately organized setup in which water is processed at a central plant and delivered to homes and businesses via water pipes."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5440> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Municipal water management deals with aspects of water supply and water technology concerning planning, processing, building and producing. It also concerns the problems of waste water collection, sewage disposal, waste water treatment in rural areas, water economising measures, water body quality management."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5452> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A large, diverse family of low-slung, long-bodied carnivorous mammals including minks, weasels, and badgers; distinguished by having only one molar in each upper jaw, and two at the most in the lower jaw."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5462> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A change in the chemical constitution of the DNA in the chromosomes of an organism: the changes are normally restricted to individual genes, but occasionally involve serious alteration to whole chromosomes. When a mutation occurs in gametes or gametocytes an inherited change may be produced in the characteristics of the organisms that develop from them. Mutation is one of the ways in which genetic variation is produced in organisms. A somatic mutation is one that occurs to a body cell, and is consequently past on to all the cells derived from it by mitosis. Natural mutations, at this stage of biological evolution, when they occur in the cells of higher animals, almost always produce deleterious characteristics. Both natural and artificial mutations can be brought about by ionizing radiation (hence the genetic and carcinogenic dangers of nuclear weapons) and by certain chemical substances called mutagens."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5463> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The branch of botany concerned with the study of fungi."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5465> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The symbiotic association of the root of a higher plant with a fungus. In an ectotrophic mycorrhiza (e.g., heath, pine trees) the fungal mycelium covers the outside of the roots; in an endotrophic mycorrhiza (e.g. orchids) the fungus grows inside the cells of the root cortex."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5475> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A nation's financial resources and its financial management, with a view towards its productivity."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5476> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The collection and processing of financial information regarding the costs for ecological challenges or opportunities for nations or countries."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5479> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The transfer of ownership of a private business or other private property to a national government, either through uncompensated seizure (expropriation) or through forced sale at a government-determined price."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5482> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A binding rule or body of rules prescribed by the government of a sovereign state that holds force throughout the regions and territories within the government's dominion."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5496> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Violent, sudden and destructive change in the environment without cause from human activity, due to phenomena such as floods, earthquakes, fire and hurricanes."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5502> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A forest area that has developed free from the influence of humans and remains largely unaffected by their activities. The natural forest may include, but is not necessarily equivalent to, an old-growth forest."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5503> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A natural fuel containing methane and hydrocarbons that occurs in certain geologic formations."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5507> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Generally, the world's natural resources as handed down to the present generation, and specifically, the earth's outstanding physical, biological and geological formations, and habitats of threatened species of animals and plants and areas with scientific, conservation or aesthetic value."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/551> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The interacting system of a biological community and its non-living environmental surroundings in a climatic region where the annual precipitation averages less than 10 inches per year."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5524> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The branches of science dealing with objectively measurable phenomena pertaining to the transformation and relationships of energy and matter; includes biology, physics, and chemistry."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/552> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Lands characterized by low annual rainfall of less than 250 mm, by evaporation exceeding precipitation and a sparse vegetation."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5537> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Active management of the earth's natural resources and environment to ensure their quality is maintained and that they are wisely used."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5538> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A binding rule or body of rules prescribed by a government to protect, preserve or renew an area's natural habitats or ecosystem."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5544> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Precautionary actions, procedures or installations undertaken to prevent or reduce harm to the elements of the material world that exist independently of human activity."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5555> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The fact or an instance of feeling the lack of something."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5565> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A group of unsegmented worms which have been variously recognized as an order, class, and phylum."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5580> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A sociopolitical, religious, occupational or other group of common characteristics and interests formed as an alternative to social, and often residential, options currently available."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5589> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A malleable ductile silvery-white metallic element that is strong and corrosion-resistant, occurring principally in pentlandite and niccolite: used in alloys, especially in toughening steel, in electroplating, and as a catalyst in organic synthesis."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/558> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The military units of a state, typically divided by their differing contexts of operations, such as the army, navy, air force and marines."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5601> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A salt or ester of nitric acid, included in compounds such as potassium nitrite, sodium nitrite and butyl nitrite."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5604> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any one of a class of usually organic compounds that contain the monovalent group, -NO2 (nitro group or radical) linked to a carbon atom."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5608> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A reddish-brown gas; it exists in varying degrees of concentration in equilibrium with other nitrogen oxides; used to produce nitric acid."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5612> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A colourless gas, soluble in water, ethanol and ether. It is formed in many reactions involving the reduction of nitric acid, but more convenient reactions for the preparation of reasonably pure NO are reactions of sodium nitrite, sulphuric acid, etc."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5613> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Oxides formed and released in all common types of combustion; they are formed by the oxidation of atmospheric nitrogen at high temperatures. Introduced into the atmosphere from car exhausts, furnace stacks, incinerators, power stations and similar sources, the oxides include nitrous oxide, nitric oxide, nitrogen dioxide, nitrogen pentoxide and nitric acid. The oxides of nitrogen undergo many reactions in the atmosphere to form photochemical smog."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/562> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Hydrocarbons having an unsaturated ring containing alternating double and single bonds, especially containing a benzene ring."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5637> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A mandatory sum of money levied by government upon producers of disturbing, harmful or unwanted sounds, frequently in the transportation or construction industries, to encourage reduction of sound levels."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5638> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Sound is radiated both as air-borne and as structure-borne; most sources produce both, thus various noise attenuation principles must be employed. Measures include: the replacement of components with quieter parts and material; the enclosure of particularly noisy components; the selection of quieter types of fan; the replacement of noisy compressed-air nozzles with quieter types; the choice of quieter transmission and cooling systems."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5643> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Legislation introduced by many governments to prevent or restrict the emission of noise from industrial, commercial and domestic premises; from motor vehicles and aircraft; and from consumer appliances and equipment."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5650> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Noise in the environment which can be harmful to human beings, animals and plants."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5651> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Harmful or unwanted sounds in the environment, which in specific locals, can be measured and averaged over a period of time."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5662> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "1) A member of a people or tribe who move from place to place to find pasture and food.\n2) Nomads include gypsies, desert tribes such as the Bedouin and the many primitive tribes in the Americas, Asia and Australia. Herding survives as a way of life around the Sahara, in the Middle East, in Asia as far east as western India, and in the Asian parts of the USSR. The end of pastoral nomadism would be regrettable not merely on account of the independence and distinctiveness of this way of life but because this type of economy may be a more rational means of raising large numbers of animals under arid conditions than is capital-intensive ranching."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5668> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Energy that is renewable and ecologically safe, such as tidal power, wind power, etc."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5671> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Private, voluntary, non-profit organisations, acting as pressure groups. Throughout the world there are more than 5.000 international NGOs which are concerned with the environment and development, with millions of supporters."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5676> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A nonmetallic element, such as arsenic or silicon, that has some of the properties of a metal."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5677> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Energy that is ecologically safe and renewable. The most widely used source is hydroelectric power, which currently supplies some 6.6% of the world's energy needs. Other non-polluting sources are solar energy, tidal energy, wave energy and wind energy. Most non-polluting energy sources require a high capital investment but have low running costs."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5684> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Non-renewable resources have been built up or evolved over a geological time-span and cannot be used without depleting the stock and raising questions of ultimate exhaustibility, since their rate of formation is so slow as to be meaningless in terms of the human life-span."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5686> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Area which provides commercial, industrial, and public facilities."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5689> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A plant or animal other than the one against which the pesticide is applied."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/568> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The creation of works of beauty or other special significance."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5692> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A geographic region of the African continent south of Europe and the Mediterranean Sea, and north of Africa's tropical rain forest, including Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia, Libya and the Egyptian region west of the Suez Canal, and also the Sahara Desert and Atlas Mountains."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5694> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The northern part of the Atlantic Ocean, extending northward from the equator to the Arctic Ocean."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5695> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "An ocean north of the equator between the eastern coast of Asia and the western coasts of the Americas, extending northward to the arctic region, with principal arms including the Gulf of Alaska, the Sea of Okhotsk, the Sea of Japan and the Bering, Yellow, East China, South China and Philippine seas, and islands including the Aleutian, Midway, Marshall and Hawaiian islands, the Japanese island arc and the Malay Archipelago."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5708> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "An event occurring in a nuclear power plant or anywhere that radioactive materials are used, stored, or transported and involving the release of potentially dangerous levels of radioactive materials into the environment."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5718> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "An unintentional release of energy from a rapid reaction of atomic nuclei yielding high temperatures and radiation potentially harmful to human health and the environment."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5721> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A place, including buildings, where all the activities relating to nuclear research are performed."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/572> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Animals characterized by the repetition of similar segments (metameres), exhibited especially by arthropods, annelids, and vertebrates in early embryonic stages and in certain specialized adult structures."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5734> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The ongoing, public discussion and dispute over the uses of energy."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5741> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A reaction involving a change in an atomic nucleus, such as fission, fusion, neutron capture, or radioactive decay, as distinct from a chemical reaction, which is limited to changes in the electron structure surrounding the nucleus."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5742> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Device which creates heat and energy by starting and controlling atomic fission."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5745> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A facility in which scientists and other researchers study the behavior and characteristics of atomic nuclei through testing and other forms of experimentation, often to invent new technology with scientific, medical and industrial purposes."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5746> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Measures and techniques implemented to reduce the possibility of incidence and the potential harm posed by radioactive substances used as an energy source, a test material or in weaponry."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5750> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any bomb, warhead, or projectile using active nuclear material to cause a chain reaction upon detonation."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5751> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any of several organic acids combined with proteins (DNA or RNA) which exist in the nucleus and protoplasm of all cells."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5757> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Condition in which there is equilibrium between intake and excretion of nutrients."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5759> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A biogeochemical cycle, in which inorganic nutrients move through the soil, living organisms, air and water or through some of these."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5761> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Elimination of nutrients as, for example, from sewage in order to prevent eutrophication of water in reservoirs."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5769> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The measure of the quantity or availability of nutrients found in materials ingested and utilized by humans or animals as a source of nutrition and energy."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5776> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The act of a party who objects to some matter or proceeding in the course of a trial or an argument or reason urged by him in support of his contention that the matter or proceeding objected to is improper or illegal."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5778> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The legal responsibility or duty compelling manufacturers to affix certain marks or other written identification to their products, as is directed by laws, regulations or government standards."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5781> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A functional or organic disease caused by factors arising from the operations or materials of an individual's industry, trade, or occupation."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5783> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A collection of people who earn their living by similar or identical means of work."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5788> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Law enacted to reduce the incidence among workers of personal injuries, illnesses, and deaths resulting from employment."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5789> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The mass of water occupying all of the Earth's surface not occupied by land, but excluding all lakes and inland seas."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5793> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The process by which pollutants, including sewage, industrial waste, consumer waste, and agricultural and urban runoff are discharged into the world's oceans. These pollutants arise from a myriad of sources."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5799> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A measure, referenced to a standard value, of the heat or coldness in a body of oceanic water."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/57> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Physical quantity of sound measured, usually expressed in decibels."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5809> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Unlawful acts against the environment, such as water contamination, hazardous waste disposal, air contamination, unpermitted installation of plants, oil spills, etc."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5810> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any room, set of rooms or building used for the administration of government service, business transactions or other work related activities."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5816> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Relating to travelling outside rush-hours to avoid overcrowding in public means of transport."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5820> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Policy whereby emissions from a proposed new or modified stationary source are balanced by reductions from existing sources to stabilise total emissions."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5825> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Activities taking place or located away from the site."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5830> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A floating device used to contain oil on a body of water. Once the boom has been inflated, it is towed downwind of the oil slick and formed into a U-shape; under the influence of wind, the oil becomes trapped within the boom. Skimming equipment travels into the boom enclosure and the oil is pumped into containers."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5837> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Contamination of any ecosystem, but usually of freshwater or marine ecosystems, by oil or other petroleum products."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5838> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "There are various systems for the abatement of oil pollution at sea: the \"Load-on-top\" system involves passing the washing from tank cleaning operations and residue from discharge of the original ballast water to an empty cargo tank nominated as the \"slop\" tank. Fresh oil cargo is loaded on top of the final residue left after further discharges of water, the resulting mixture being acceptable to refineries despite some additional cost in removing the salt and water. Under the International Convention for the Prevention of Pollution from Ships, 1973, all oil-carrying ships will be required to be capable of operating with this method of retention, or alternatively to discharge to reception facilities. Another method consists in spraying on the oil dispersives and/or blasting straw and sawdust, functioning as \"blotting paper\", onto water, beaches, rocks and docks. The Vikoma System for the containment of oil spills at sea, developed by British Petroleum, a seaboom of about 500 metres in length, is inflated and towed downwind of the oil slick and formed into a U-shape; under the influence of wind, the oil becomes trapped within the boom. Skimming equipment travels into the boom enclosure and the oil is pumped into containers."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5839> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Boats used for recovering oil spilled at sea from oil tankers. The recommended procedure is to contain and physically recover the spill with or without the use of adsorbents. This approach entails three processes: a) confinement of the spill by spill booms; b) recovery of the spill by sorbing agents; c) physical removal of the contained oil by oil pick-up devices."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5840> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "System of process units used to convert crude petroleum into fuels, lubricants, and other petroleum-derived products."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
