<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5841> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The separation of petroleum mixtures into their component parts."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5848> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The mass of oil that floats on a surface of water, which is discharged accidentally, naturally or by design, and can be moved by currents, tides and the wind."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5852> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The accidental release of oil, or other petroleum products usually into freshwater or marine ecosystems, and usually in large quantities. It can be controlled by chemical dispersion, combustion, mechanical containment, and absorption."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5856> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Landfill that has been filled and covered with topsoil and seeded. The most common end use for landfills is open spaces with no active recreation taking place over the completed landfill. The obvious reason for this use is that the completed surface is steeply sloped to provide rapid runoff. Also, no irrigation of the cover grasses should be allowed. It is very unlikely to think that commercial or industrial buildings will be constructed on a completed landfill. If the end use is such that the public will be walking on the site, it is important that all manholes be properly secured, leachate lagoons fenced, and other potential hazards eliminated."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5857> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any place that has been made unclean or unsafe by the discharge of high concentrations of hazardous or detrimental substances into its water, soil or atmosphere."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5858> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Old installation that do not respond to new rules for the prevention of environmental pollution and whose redevelopment requires investments for adopting technologies related to the protection of waterways, waste management, noise reduction and emission control."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5863> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The testing and measurement of the sensitivity of the sense of smell."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5870> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The study of the causes, development, characteristics, and treatment of tumors."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5875> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Fishing in the deepest parts of the sea."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5877> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Data referring to the practical carrying-out of a process."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/587> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any man-made object placed in a near-periodic orbit in which it moves mainly under the gravitational influence of one celestial body, such as the earth, sun, another planet, or a planet's moon."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5885> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Adjustments made to a building or to a mechanical or electrical system or apparatus in order to maximize its functionality and efficiency."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5892> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Carbon which comes from an animal or plant."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5897> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Farming without the use of industrially made fertilizers or pesticides."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5913> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Waste containing carbon compounds; derived from animal and plant materials."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5914> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "An individual constituted to carry out all life functions."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/591> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Generic name for a group of fibrous mineral silicates. It includes blue asbestos (crocidolite), white asbestos (chrysotile) and brown asbestos (amosite). After they are mined the asbestos fibres are separated from the rock and are spun into a cloth. When inhaled the fibres penetrate the lungs and the tissues of the bronchial tubes, resulting in asbestosis, a crippling lung disease. Asbestos also causes cancer of the lung and the gastro-intestinal tract, and mesothelioma, a malignant cancer of the inner lining of the chest. However, because it is a poor conductor of electricity and highly resistant to heat it has been widely used over the years in fire-fighting suits, and building and insulating materials. The fibrous form of several silicate minerals, at one time widely used for electrical and thermal insulation; the use of all forms of asbestos is now either banned or strictly controlled in many countries since it causes cancer."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5927> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Molecules containing carbon-metal linkage; a compound containing an alkyl or aryl radical bonded to a metal."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5931> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Pesticides that contain phosphorous; short-lived, but some can be toxic when first applied."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5944> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A rarely used word referring to the study of mountain systems and the depiction of their relief."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5949> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The passage of a solvent through a semipermeable membrane separating two solutions of different concentrations. A semipermeable membrane is one through which the molecules of a solvent can pass but the molecules of most solutes cannot. There is a thermodynamic tendency for solutions separated by such a membrane to become equal in concentration, the water (or other solvent) flowing from the weaker to the stronger solution. Osmosis will stop when the two solutions reach equal concentration, and can also be stopped by applying a pressure to the liquid on the stronger-solution side of the membrane. The pressure required to stop the flow from a pure solvent into a solution is a characteristic of the solution, and is called the osmotic pressure. Osmotic pressure depends only on the concentration of particles in the solution, not on their nature."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/594> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A hardened mixture of asbestos fibers, Portland cement and water used in relatively thin slabs for shingles, wallboard and siding."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5953> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A pastime, diversion, exercise or other means of enjoyment and relaxation that is carried out in a particular city, town or small district."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5959> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Putting too much fertilizer on land; the runoff from overfertilisation can cause water pollution."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5960> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Taking out of the sea more than natural population growth can sustain. Overfishing has a number of causes, the most ruthless being \"chronic over capacity\" of modern fishing fleets to effectively take far more fish than can be replaced."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5967> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The circulation, especially in the fall and spring, of the layers of water in a lake or sea, whereby surface water sinks and mixes with bottom water; it is caused by changes in density differences due to changes in temperature, and is especially common wherever lakes are icebound in winter."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5978> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Binary chemical compound in which oxygen is combined with a metal or nonmetal."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5982> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A gaseous chemical element; an essential element in cellular respiration and in combustion processes; the most abundant element in the earth's crust and about 20% of the air by volume."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5986> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Amount of oxygen contained in a solution."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5991> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "An allotropic form of oxygen containing three atoms in the molecule. It is a bluish gas, very active chemically, and a powerful oxidizing agent. Ozone is formed when oxygen or air is subjected to a silent electric discharge. It occurs in ordinary air in very small amounts only."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5992> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A factor that reflects the ozone depletion potential of a substance, on a mass per kilogram basis, as compared to chlorofluorocarbon-11 (CFC-11). Such factor shall be based upon the substance's atmospheric life time, the molecular weight of bromine and chlorine, and the substance's ability to be photolytically disassociated, and upon other factors determined to be an accurate measure of relative ozone depletion potential."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/5999> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "All products made of any materials of any nature to be used for the containment, protection, handling, delivery and presentation of goods, from raw materials to processed goods, from the producer to the user or the consumer."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/59> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The characteristics found within a structure that determine the quality of sound in its relevance to hearing."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6013> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The study of life in past geologic time, based on fossil plants and animals and including phylogeny, their relationship to existing plants, animals, and environments, and the chronology of the Earth's history."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6035> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Organism which lives and obtains food at the expense of another organism, the host."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6038> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A branch of biology which deals with those organisms, plant or animal, which have become dependent on other living creatures."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6047> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Area where a vehicle can be left for a period of time."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6052> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "1) Any very small part of matter, such as a molecule, atom, or electron. \n2) Any relatively small subdivision of matter, ranging in diameter from a few angstroms to a few millimeters."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/607> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A body of persons associated for the regulation of a common economic activity by means of a special organization."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6094> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "That shell or layer of the Earth in which soil-forming processes occur."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6103> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "1) A punishment for a crime.\n2) A sum specified in a contract as payable on its breach but not constituting a genuine estimate of the likely loss."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6123> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "An exposure limit that is set for exposure to an hazardous substance or harmful agent and enforced by OSHA (Occupational Safety and Health Act) as a legal standard. It is based on time-weighted average concentrations for a normal 8-hour work day and 40 hour work week."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6124> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The license, formal consent or authorization to act on some matter, frequently validating the action as lawful or procedurally correct."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6138> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any organism that damages crops, injures or irritates livestock or man, or reduces the fertility of land."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6139> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Keeping down the number of pests by killing them or preventing them from attacking."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6144> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The specific or known route or vector of any chemical substance released into the environment to prevent, destroy or mitigate any pest that is directly or indirectly detrimental to harvest crops and other human interests."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6146> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A pesticide remaining in the environment for a fairly long time, continuing to be effective for days, weeks, and months."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6154> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The production of materials derived from petroleum or natural gas."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6163> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The branch of economic geology that relates to the origin, migration and accumulation of oil and gas, and to the discovery of commercial deposits. Its practice involves the application of geochemistry, geophysics, paleontology, structural geology and stratigraphy to the problems of finding hydrocarbons."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6169> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Controlled utilization, protection and development of  exploited and potentially exploitable sources of crude oil to meet current demand and ensure future requirements."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6177> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Concerted activity concerned with manufacturing pharmaceutical goods."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6179> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Discarded medicinal drugs and related products from pharmacies, hospitals, clinics, pharmaceutical manufacturers, etc."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/617> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The gaseous envelope surrounding the Earth in a several kilometers-thick layer."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6187> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The academic discipline concerned with making explicit the nature and significance of ordinary and scientific beliefs and investigating the intelligibility of concepts by means of rational argument concerning their presuppositions, implications, and interrelationships; in particular, the rational investigation of the nature and structure of reality (metaphysics), the resources and limits of knowledge (epistemology), the principles and import of moral judgment (ethics), and the relationship between language and reality (semantics)."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6189> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "1) Generic term for any compound containing a phosphate group.\n2) Any salt or ester of any phosphoric acid, especially a salt of orthophosphoric acid."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6198> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The result or consequence of a chemical reaction caused by light or ultraviolet radiation."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6202> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A combination of fog and chemicals that come from automobile and factory emissions and is acted upon by the action of the sun. Nitrogen dioxide, in the presence of the sun and some hydrocarbons, is turned into nitric oxide and atomic oxygen. The atomic oxygen reacts with the oxygen molecules and other constituents of automobile exhaust fumes to form a variety of products including ozone. The ozone is harmful in itself and is also implicated in a highly complex series of continuing reactions. As long as there is ozone or nitrogen dioxide and sunlight present, other undesirable reactions will occur."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6204> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The process of making measurements from photographs, used especially in the construction of maps from aerial photographs and also in military intelligence, medical and industrial research, etc."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6211> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The process by which plants transform carbon dioxide and water into carbohydrates and other compounds, using energy from the sun captured by chlorophyll in the plant. Oxygen is a by-product of the process. Photosynthesis is the essence of all plant life (autotrophic production) and hence of all animal life (heterotrophic production) on the planet Earth. The rate of photosynthesis depends on climate, intensity and duration of sunlight, available leaf area, soil nutrient availability, temperature, carbon dioxide concentration, and soil moisture regimes."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6224> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The study of the physical aspects of the ocean, the movements of the sea, and the variability of these factors in relationship to the atmosphere and the ocean bottom."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6225> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A form of urban land use planning which attempts to achieve an optimal spatial coordination of different human activities for the enhancement of the quality of life."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/622> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The general movement and circulation of air, which transfers energy between different levels of the atmosphere. The mechanisms of circulation are very complicated. They involve the transfer of energy between the oceans and the atmosphere, the land and the atmosphere, as well as the different levels of the atmosphere."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6235> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The study of those aspects of nature which can be understood in a fundamental way in terms of elementary principles and laws."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/623> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The Earth's atmosphere consists by volume of nitrogen (79,1%), oxygen (20,9%), carbon dioxide (about 0,03%) and traces of the noble gases (argon, krypton, xenon, helium) plus water vapour, traces of ammonia, organic matter, ozone, various salts and suspended solid particles."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6240> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The biological study of the functions of living organisms and their parts."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/624> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The chemical abundance in the earth's atmosphere of its constituents including nitrogen, oxygen, argon, carbon dioxide, water vapour, ozone, neon, helium, krypton, methane, hydrogen and nitrous oxide."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/625> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Suspended pollutants -- solid particles, liquid aerosols, etc. -- or toxic gases released into the atmosphere from a polluting source, or type of source."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6270> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A line of pipe connected to valves and other control devices, for conducting fluids, gases, or finely divided solids."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6285> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any physical extension of, or changes to, the uses of land in metropolitan areas following certain preparations or designs."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6290> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A binding rule or body of rules prescribed by a government to organize, designate and regulate land use within its domain through zoning laws, subdivision regulations, rent and sign controls, growth management and other measures designed to protect human health and ecological integrity."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6291> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A procedure or course of action taken to design, organize or prepare for the future."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6298> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Raising a certain type of plant by crossing one variety with another to produce a new variety where the desired characteristics are strongest."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6310> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any substance or mixture of substances which through physiological action protects the plants against parasites, fungi, virus, or other damaging factors."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6316> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The study of the function and chemical reactions within the various organs of plants."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6323> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any living organism that typically synthesizes its food from inorganic substances, possesses cellulose cell walls, responds slowly and often permanently to a stimulus, lacks specialized sense organs and nervous system, and has no powers of locomotion."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6327> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "1) Common name for a number of industrial applications of plasma, such as: etching of semiconductor chips, deposition of silicon for solar cell production, deposition of silicon dioxide for passivation of surfaces, activation of surfaces, melting and welding with plasma arcs as well as plasma chemistry. \n2) Plasma technology consists of minute gas-filled cells, which emit light when an electric current is channelled through them."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6329> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A polymeric material (usually organic) of large molecular weight which can be shaped by flow; usually refers to the final product with fillers, plasticizers, pigments, and stabilizers included (versus the resin, the homogeneous polymeric starting material); examples are polyvinyl chloride, polyethylene, and urea-formaldehyde."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6339> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A piece of land used for recreation, especially by children, often including equipment such as swings and slides."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6355> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "To catch game, fish, etc. illegally by trespassing on private property."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6357> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Pollution from a discrete source, such as a septic tank, a sewer, a discharge type, a landfill, a factory or waste water treatment works discharging to a watercourse; stack emission from an industrial process; or spillage from an underground storage tank leaching into groundwater."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6362> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The interacting systems of the biological communities and their nonliving environmental surroundings located in the regions where the air temperature is perennially below 10° Celsius, usually at and near the North and South Poles."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6364> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Area relating to the earth's poles or the area inside the Arctic or Antarctic Circles."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6383> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The study of the effects of political actions on human geography, involving the spatial analysis of political phenomena."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6384> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A group of persons organized to seek or exercise power in governmental or public affairs, by supporting candidates for office or by lobbying for action and mobilizing support for bills or governmental policies."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6392> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Microspores of seed-producing plants. Each pollen grain contains a much-reduced male gametophyte. Pollen grains are transferred by wind, water, birds or other animals."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6396> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The process by which a pollutant is physically incorporated into another substance or body."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6397> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The process by which concentrations of pollutants progressively increase in the tissues of living organisms in environments where these pollutants are present."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6399> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The determination of the composition of any substance that causes pollution, using classical laboratory techniques and other methods involving analytical chemistry."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/639> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Atmospheric processes are distinguished in physical and chemical processes and both types may be operating simultaneously in complicated and interdependent ways. The physical processes of transport by atmospheric winds and the formation of clouds and precipitation strongly influence the patterns and rates of acidic deposition, while chemical reactions govern the forms of the compounds deposited."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6405> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The physical, chemical or biological breakdown of a complex polluting material into simpler components."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6406> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The act or process in which polluting agents settle or accumulate naturally in ecosystems."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6407> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The spreading of pollutants from a point of release in air, soil and water. The dispersion of air pollutants is heavily influenced by how and where the pollutant is emitted, e.g., by continuous low-level versus accidental releases, multiple stacks versus a few, or the height of the stacks. The nature of the local terrain meteorology and the chemistry of the released material strongly influence the pattern of regional and, finally, global dispersion and transport."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6415> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The act or process in which polluting agents are created, produced or formed."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/641> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The gaseous area surrounding the planet is divided into several concentric spherical strata (layers, like shells) separated by narrow transition zones. The boundaries are know as \"pause\". More than 99% of the total atmospheric mass is concentrated in the first 40 km from the Earth's surface. Atmospheric layers are characterized by differences in chemical composition that produce variations in temperature."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6422> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The amount of polluting material that a transporting agent, such as a stream, a glacier, or the wind, is actually carrying at a given time."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6425> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Periodic or continuous determination of the amount of pollutants present in the environment."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6441> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A solid, liquid or gas that has been contaminated, rendered impure or made unsafe for use."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6443> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The principle that those causing pollution should meet the costs to which it gives rise."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6469> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The quantitative or qualitative measure of the presence, effect or level of any polluting substance in air, water or soil."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6481> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A chemical substance the composition of which, without regard to impurities, consists of brominated biphenyl molecules."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6485> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "PCBs are a family of chemical compounds which do not exist in nature but which are man-made. Commercial mixtures are clear, pale yellow liquids, manufactured by the replacement of hydrogen atoms on the biphenyl molecule by chlorine. Because of their physical properties, PCBs are commonly found in electrical equipment which requires dielectric fluid such as power transformers and capacitors, as well as in hydraulic machinery, vacuum pumps, compressors and heat-exchanger fluids. Other uses include: lubricants, fluorescent light ballasts, paints, glues, waxes, carbonless copy paper, inks including newspapers, dust-control agents for dirt roads, solvents for spreading insecticides, cutting oils. PCBs are stable compounds and although they are no longer manufactured they are extremely persistent and remain in huge quantities in the atmosphere and in landfill sites. They are not water-soluble and float on the surface of water where they are eaten by aquatic animals and so enter the food chain. PCBs are fat-soluble, and are therefore easy to take into the system, but difficult to excrete."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6486> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "PCDD are formed (along with variants including furans) when compounds containing chlorine are burnt at low temperature in improperly operated/designed domestic refuse and industrial waste incinerators where PCDDs can be found in both the flue gases and the fly ash."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6492> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Hydrocarbons containing two or more closed rings of atoms."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6499> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Substance made of giant molecules formed by the union of simple molecules (monomers)."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6505> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Polymer of vinyl chloride; tasteless, odourless; insoluble in most organic solvents; a member of the family of vinyl resins."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6508> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any collection of liquid effluents or wastewater drained or separated out during the processing of crops or mineral ores."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6510> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A small, natural body of standing water, usually fresh; e.g. a stagnant body of water in a marsh, or a still body of water within a cave."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6528> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The direction of change in the total number of persons inhabiting a country, city, district or area."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6552> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Company which is responsible for the supply and distribution of electric energy to a given area."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6579> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Building whose sections are manufactured in specialized factories and later transported and assembled on a building site."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6583> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any introductory action in the judicial process designed to determine the need for further court involvement or to expedite a motion that requires immediate attention."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6591> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Printed matter as a whole, especially newspapers and periodicals."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6593> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A type of stress which is exerted uniformly in all directions; its measure is the force exerted per unit area."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6614> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Consumption of energy used in the same form as in its naturally occurring state, for example crude oil, coal, natural gas, e.g. before it is converted into electricity."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6619> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "That part of a country's or region's economy that makes direct use of natural resources, including agriculture, forestry, fishing and the fuel, metal and mining industries."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/661> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "An organized assemblage of authorized persons or officials empowered to implement and enforce laws, oversee jurisdictions, settle disputes, adjudicate or make some other legal determination."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6621> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Order of mammals containing monkeys, apes, and human beings."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6622> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Forest which originally covered a region before changes in the environment brought about by people."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6623> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Principle adopted by the UN Conference on Environment and Development (1992) that in order to protect the environment, a precautionary approach should be widely applied, meaning that where there are threats of serious or irreversible damage to the environment, lack of full scientific certainty should not be used as a reason for postponing cost-effective measures to prevent environmental degradation."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6637> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The branch of law dealing with such aspects of relationships between individuals that are of no direct concern to the state."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6646> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Organisms (i.e. prokaryotes) whose genetic material (filaments of DNA) is not enclosed by a nuclear membrane, and that do not possess mitochondria or plastids. Bacteria and cyanophyta are the only prokaryotic organisms."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6658> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Obligations, responsibilities or debts imposed upon all members of an industry that manufactures or produces a product or service causing injury or harm to a consumer and apportioned according to each member's share of the market for the product."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/665> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The processing, discovery and identification of data elements by automated means."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6661> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Comparison of products or processes to identify those having reduced environmental impacts."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6676> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A standard which prescribes aspects of the physical or chemical composition of products which have potential for causing environmental damage or the handling, presentation and packaging of products, particularly those which are toxic."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/66> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A group of 15 radioactive elements some of which occur naturally while others are produced in nuclear reactions. They include plutonium, americium and neptunium. The health hazard presented by the actinides, if they are released into the environment, comes from the potency of their radioactive characteristics. They are alpha-emitters, and therefore can cause intense localized damage in tissues if absorbed into the body."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6709> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "An interdiction or forbidding of an activity or action by authority or law."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6718> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Process by which a disturbance at one point is propagated to another point more remote from the source with no net transport of the material of the medium itself; examples include the motion of electromagnetic waves, sound waves, hydrodynamic waves in liquids, and vibration waves in solids."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6720> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A gas used in aerosol preparations to expel the liquid contents through an atomizer."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6736> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Technique for causing a body to move by exerting a force against it."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6743> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Natural or man-made areas which have been reserved for conservation, scientific, educational and/or recreational purposes."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6746> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Threatened, vulnerable or endangered species which are protected from extinction by preventive measures."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6760> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A geographic area of some considerable extent, smaller than a continent but larger than a region, which is unified by some or all of its characteristics and which can therefore be studied as a whole. A faunal province, for example, has a particular assemblage of animal species, which differs from assemblages in different contemporaneous environments elsewhere."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6766> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The power of a government agency or its administrators to administer and implement laws and government policies applicable to a specific geographical area, usually falling under the jurisdiction of two or more states."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6773> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A result or consequence stemming from mental processes that create or influence human consciousness and emotions."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6776> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The science that deals with the functions of the mind and the behaviour of an organism in relation to its environment."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/678> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A fall or slide of a large mass, as of snow or rock, down a mountainside."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6790> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "That which can be accessed, used and shared by the general populace without restrictions, penalties or fees."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6793> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The theory and practice of governmental money matters, including taxation, spending, transfer and property incomes, borrowing, debt and revenue management."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6798> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The discipline in health science that, at the level of the community or the public, aims at promoting prevention of disease, sanitary living, laws, practices and a healthier environment."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6799> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Right to appear and give evidence and also right to hear and examine witnesses whose testimony is presented by opposing parties."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6802> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A general classification of law, consisting generally of constitutional, administrative, criminal and international law, concerned with the organization of the state, the relations between the state and the people who compose it, the responsibilities of public officers to the state, to each other, and to private persons, and the relations of states to one other. The branch or department of law which is concerned with the state in its political or sovereign capacity, including constitutional and administrative law, and with the definition, regulation, and enforcement of rights in cases where the state is regarded as the subject of the right or object of the duty, - including criminal law and criminal procedure, - and the law of the state, considered in its quasi private personality, i.e., as capable of holding or exercising rights, or acquiring and dealing with property, in the character of an individual."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6804> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The purported, collective view of the public on some issue or problem, typically formulated by selective polling or sampling, and frequently used as a guide to action or decision."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6805> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The canvassing of a representative sample of a large group of people on some question in order to determine the general opinion of a group."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6809> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A joint venture between corporations and government or between community members and government or business beyond the course of normal interaction."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6812> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A government agency for which an elected or appointed attorney or staff of attorneys is vested with the authority by a constitution or statute to try cases on the government's behalf, to represent public interest or to take legal action against persons violating federal, state or local laws."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6818> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The act or the means of conveying people in mass as opposed to conveyance in private vehicles."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6828> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The cellulosic material produced by reducing wood mechanically or chemically and used in making paper and cellulose products. Also known as wood pulp."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6842> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Installation where impurities are removed from waste water."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6860> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The inspection, analysis, and other relevant actions taken to provide control over what is being done, manufactured, or fabricated, so that a desirable level of quality is achieved and maintained."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6870> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The surface exploitation and removal of stone or mineral deposits from the earth's crust."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6883> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A system using beamed and reflected radiofrequency energy for detecting and locating objects, measuring distance or altitude, navigating, homing, bombing and other purposes."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6884> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Emission of any rays from either natural or man-made origins, such as radio waves, the sun's rays, medical X-rays and the fall-out and nuclear wastes produced by nuclear weapons and nuclear energy production. Radiation is usually divided between non-ionizing radiation, such as thermal radiation (heat) and light, and nuclear radiation. Non-ionizing radiation includes ultraviolet radiation from the sun which, although it can damage cells and tissues, does not involve the ionization events of nuclear radiation."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6888> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The total amount of radiation absorbed by material or tissues, in the sense of absorbed dose, exposure dose, or dose equivalent."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6897> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A binding rule or body of rules prescribed by  government to establish measures to keep humans and natural resources safe from harmful exposure to energy waves released by nuclear materials, electromagnetic current and other sources."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6899> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The complex of symptoms characterizing the disease known as radiation injury, resulting from excessive exposure of the whole body (or large part) to ionizing radiation. The earliest of these symptoms are nausea, fatigue, vomiting, and diarrhea, which may be followed by loss of hair (epilation), hemorrhage, inflammation of the mouth and throat, and general loss of energy."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6901> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The process, equipment or programming involved in transmitting and receiving sound signals by electromagnetic waves."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6904> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Contamination of a substance, living organism or site caused by radioactive material."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6909> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Waste generated by the emission of particulate or electromagnetic radiation resulting from the decay of the nuclei of unstable elements."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6912> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The material that descends to the earth or water well beyond the site of a surface or subsurface nuclear explosion."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6921> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any waste that emit radiation in excess of normal background level, including the toxic by-products of the nuclear energy industry."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6937> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Discarded textile waste, either post-consumer waste or pre-consumer waste, such as manufacturing process scraps."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6950> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Process by which particles in the atmosphere act as centres round which water can form drops which then falls as rain."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6953> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The building up of land by the deposition of allochthonous material, such as rocks, gravel, etc."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6962> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A Eurasian cruciferous plant, Brassica napus, that is cultivated for its seeds, which yield a useful oil, and as a fodder plant."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6965> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Species which have a restricted world range."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6967> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A crude, unprocessed or partially processed material used as feedstock for a processing operation."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6977> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A device that introduces either inductive or capacitive reactance into a circuit, such as a coil or capacitor."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6978> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Those studies and activities that seek to minimise the risk of a nuclear reactor accident."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/6979> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The planting of trees in forest areas which have been cleared. Reforestation has become increasingly important for preventing or reversing environmental degradation and for helping to maximize economic returns on commercially forested lands."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/698> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Group of single-cell micro-organisms, the smallest of the living organisms. Some are vital to sustain life, while others are responsible for causing highly dangerous human diseases, such as anthrax, tetanus and tuberculosis. Bacteria are found everywhere, in the soil, water and air."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/699> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A device that removes some suspended solids from sewage. Air and bacteria decompose additional wastes filtering through the sand so that cleaner water drains from the bed."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7010> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Plastic waste that can be transformed into new products."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7012> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Waste materials that are transformed into new products in such a manner that the original products may lose their identity."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7014> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Paper that has been separated from the solid waste stream for utilization as a raw material in the manufacture of a new product. Not all paper in the waste stream is recyclable. It may be heavily contaminated or otherwise unusable."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7015> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A resource recovery method involving the collection and treatment of a waste product for use as raw material in the manufacture of the same or a similar product."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7018> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Management of all the stages involved in the life of a product such as raw materials acquisition, manufacturing, distribution and retail, use and re-use and maintenance, recycling and waste management, in order to create less environmentally harmful products."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7028> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "An administrative or legal remedy that attempts to restore a person to his or her original or expected position prior to loss or injury, including breach of contract."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7032> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any of various types of tall stiff grass-like plants growing together in groups near water."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7034> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A line of rocks in the tidal zone of a coast, submerged at high water but partly uncovered at low water."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7037> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The return of waves or particles from surfaces on which they are incident."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7038> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The study of the reflectance of light or other radiant energy."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7044> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The cooling of substances, usually food, below the environmental temperature for preservative purposes. Refrigeration is responsible for the largest and fastest-growing use of CFCs in the developing world. The industrial countries, and some developing countries, have taken exceptional steps to control and, eventually, ban the production of CFCs and other ozone-depleting materials by the year 2000. However, many developing nations have not signed the Montreal Protocol because they are afraid that the cost of changing over to alternative, ozone-friendly technology will be too high."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7046> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A restricted and isolated area in which plants and animals persisted during a period of continental climatic change that made surrounding areas uninhabitable; especially an ice-free or unglaciated area within or close to a continental ice sheet or upland ice cap, where hardy biotas eked out an existence during a glacial phase. It later served as a center of dispersal for the repopulation of surrounding areas after climatic readjustment."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7047> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A person who is outside his country of origin and who, due to well-founded fear of persecution, is unable or unwilling to avail himself of that country protection."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7058> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Making changes to old industrial plants installing new equipment's and facilities for the disposal of gas emissions in the atmosphere, of waste water and waste material in soil and water."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7059> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A designated area or an administrative division of a city, county or larger geographical territory that is formulated according to some biological, political, economic or demographic criteria."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7075> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The step by step method and process of defining, developing and outlining various possible courses of actions to meet existing or future needs, goals and objectives for a designated area or an administrative division of a city, county or larger geographical area."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7087> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A rule established by authority; a permanent rule of action; a law or statute. In its most common meaning, the term is used to designate the enactment of the legislative body."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7091> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A conservation measure involving the correction of past abuses that have impaired the productivity of the resources base."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7092> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "To provide with new or different housing."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7094> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The relating of causes to the effects that they produce."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7099> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The expression of man's belief in and reverence for a superhuman power recognized as the creator and governor of the universe."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7103> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "General term indicating the elimination of substances from a medium or from the environment."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7108> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Resources capable of being continuously renewed or replaced through such processes as organic reproduction and cultivation such as those practiced in agriculture, animal husbandry, forestry and fisheries."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7112> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any commercial activity, position or site that involves work in restoring or fixing some material thing or structure, such as by replacing parts or putting together something torn, broken or detached."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7120> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any of various processes, either sexual or asexual, by which an animal or plant produces one or more individuals similar to itself."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7135> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Proposal, plan or design containing the necessary information and data for conducting a specific survey."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7143> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Area that has only private houses, not offices and factories."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7155> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Remaining potential for harm to persons, property or the environment following all possible efforts to reduce predictable hazards."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7160> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Recycling of material or energy which is left over or wasted in industrial processes and other human activities. Examples include waste heat and gaseous pollutants from electricity generation, slag from metal-ore refining, and garbage. A residual becomes an output or input when a technological advance creates economic opportunities for the waste."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7165> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A formal expression of the opinion of an official body or a public assembly, adopted by vote, as a legislative resolution."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7167> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Absorption or, less commonly, adsorption of material by a body or system from which the material was previously released."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/716> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Transactional business between any bank, an institution for safeguarding, exchanging, receiving and lending money, and that bank's clients or customers."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7176> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The process in living organisms of taking in oxygen from the surroundings and giving out carbon dioxide."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7182> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The structures and passages involved with intake, expulsion, and exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide in the vertebrate body."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7184> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The obligation to answer for an act done, and to repair or otherwise make restitution for any injury it may have caused."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7189> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Procedure or course of action taken to reestablish or bring back to state of environmental or ecological health."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7192> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A limitation on the utilization of land or some other property, often inscribed in a deed or lease document."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7193> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The sale of goods to ultimate consumers, usually in small quantities."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7194> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A basin designed and operated to provide temporary storage and thus reduce the peak flood flows of a stream."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/719> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A soft silvery-white metallic element of the alkaline earth group. It is used in bearing alloys and compounds are used as pigments."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/71> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A collection of persons united to address specific sociopolitical or socioeconomic concerns."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7201> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any re-utilization of products or components, in original form, such as when used glass bottles are sterilized and refilled for resale."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7202> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Planting of new trees and, particularly, of native plants in disturbed sites where the vegetation cover has been destroyed, to stabilize the land surface from wind and water erosion and to reclame the land for other uses. Revegetation practices are employed in mined lands, roadsides, parks, wetlands, utility corridors, riparian areas, etc."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7217> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A legal guarantee or just claim enabling a citizen or employee to compose and submit a formal written request to an authority asking for some benefit or favor or for intervention and redress of some wrong."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7218> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The legal guarantee or just claim inhering in a citizen's relation to some physical thing, but especially a plot of land, including the right to possess, use and dispose of it."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7223> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "To attach a numbered ring to the leg of a bird so that its movements can be recorded. Ringing is a very common method of tracing bird movement and providing information about bird's ages. It can also cause stress to the birds."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7232> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Sea level rises are a possible consequence of global warming. As the amount of free water in the ocean increases, and as the water becomes warmer, global warming will increase. In addition, according to theory, the heating at the poles may reduce the amount of water trapped in glaciers and ice caps. By the year 3000, the seas could rise between one and two metres. Such an event would clearly threaten low-lying areas, particularly in Asia, where million of people live and farm on river deltas and flood plains."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7235> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Technique used to determine the likelihood or chance of hazardous events occurring (such as release of a certain quantity of a toxic gas) and the likely consequences. Originally developed for use in nuclear and chemical industry where certain possible events, of low probability, could have extremely serious results. Attempts are being made to use concepts from probabilistic risk analysis to characterise environmental impacts, whose occurrence and nature are not easy to predict with any degree of accuracy."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7237> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A systematic process of evaluating and assessing the hazards of loss versus the possibility of financial gain or profit."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7238> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The exchange of information about health or environmental risks among risk assessors and managers, the general public, news media, interest groups, etc."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7240> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A subjective appreciation by individuals which will more often than not bear little relation to the statistical probability of damage or injury."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/726> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Monitoring of long-term changes in atmospheric compositions of particular significance to the weather and the climate."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7293> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Circulation of motor vehicles and people on the road network."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7295> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Discipline which includes the design of highways and pedestrian ways, the study and application of traffic statistics, and the environmental aspects of the transportation of goods and people."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/72> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A powdered, granular or pelleted form of amorphous carbon characterized by a very large surface area per unit volume because of an enormous number of fine pores."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7302> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A generic term for felted or matted fibers manufactured by blowing or spinning threads of molten rock, slag, or glass. The material is used for thermal insulation."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/730> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The minimum nutriments deemed necessary for a person of a particular age, gender, physiological condition and activity level to sustain life, health and growth."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7314> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A heat-treating furnace of circular construction which rotates the workpiece around the axis of the furnace during heat treatment; workpieces are transported through the furnace along a circular path."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7319> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any established or selected course for passage or travel."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7320> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The activity of designing, organizing or preparing for the construction of boulevards, turnpikes, highways and other roads."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7327> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A sector of the economy in which an aggregate of commercial enterprises is engaged in the manufacture and marketing of natural or synthetic rubber products."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7352> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The total number of persons inhabiting an agricultural or pastoral region."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/736> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A process that is not in continuous or mass production; operations are carried out with discrete quantities of material or a limited number of items."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7370> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Research, detailed examination and usually a written report on the need for or efficacy of actions, procedures or devices intended to lower the occurrence or risk of injury, loss and danger to persons, property or the environment."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7376> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The accumulation of soluble salts by evaporation of the waters that bore them to the soil zone, in a soil of an arid, poorly drained region."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7390> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Amount of salt contained in a solution."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7397> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A meadow subject to overflow by salt water."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7400> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A mass of salt which is injected as a diapir (a dome in which the overlying rocks have been ruptured by the squeezing-out of plastic core material) into overlying sedimentary rocks, thereby piercing and deforming them. The mechanism is similar to that of an intrusive magma, with the salt deforming and behaving plastically under pressure. It is of great economic importance because it assists in the formation of a \"trap\" structure for oil accumulation, in addition to its associated deposits of anhydrite, gypsum and sulphur."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7401> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The reaction product when a metal displaces the hydrogen of an acid."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7410> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Method of selecting items at random from a set in such a manner that the sample will be representative of the whole."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7420> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "An accumulation of loose sand heaped up by the wind, commonly found along low-lying seashores above high-tide level, more rarely on the border of large lakes or river valleys, as well as in various desert regions, where there is abundant dry surface sand during some part of the year."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7423> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The extraction of sand by mining for building purposes and for the extraction of heavy minerals such as rutile and zircon."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7425> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A place where sand is extracted from the ground."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7436> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The set of furnishings designed for personal hygiene and the disposal of organic waste."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7438> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "An engineered method of disposing of solid waste on land in a manner that protects the environment, by spreading the waste in thin layers, compacting it to the smallest practical volume and covering it with compacted soil by the end of each working day or at more frequent intervals if necessary."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7444> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Plans for the control of the physical factors in the human environment that can harm development, health, or survival."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7452> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "An object that orbits around a larger one. Artificial satellites orbiting the Earth are used for communications, the gathering of military intelligence, the monitoring of weather and other environmental phenomena, etc."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7458> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Wood fragments made by a saw in cutting."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/745> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A series of cells, each containing the essentials for producing voltaic electricity, connected together."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7464> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A disease in which humans are parasitized by any of three species of blood flukes: Schistosoma mansoni, S. haematobium, and S. japonicum; adult worms inhabit the blood vessels."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7465> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "An institution or building at which children and young people receive education."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
