<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7472> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The study of the physical universe and its contents by means of reproducible observations, measurements, and experiments to establish, verify, or modify general laws to explain its nature and behaviour."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7482> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The prescribed step or manner of proceeding in an environmental impact assessment, by which a public discussion is held to discuss the information that needs to be developed, the alternatives that need to be considered and other important environmental issues."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7484> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The trade or traffic in discarded or leftover materials that can be reused in some way."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/749> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "An open, curving indentation made by the sea or a lake into a coastline."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7500> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The activity or processes involving the extraction of mineral deposits from the surface, or below the surface, of the ocean floor."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7502> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Large-scale horizontal water motion within an ocean. The way energy from the sun, stored in the sea, is transported around the world. The currents explain, for example, why the UK has ice-free ports in winter, while St. Petersburg, at the same latitude as the Shetland Islands, needs ice breakers. Evidence is growing that the world's ocean circulation was very different during the last ice age and has changed several times in the distant past, with dramatic effects on climate. The oceans are vital as storehouses, as they absorb more than half the sun's heat reaching the earth. This heat, which is primarily absorbed near the equator is carried around the world and released elsewhere, creating currents which last up to 1.000 years. As the Earth rotates and the wind acts upon the surface, currents carry warm tropical water to the cooler parts of the world. The strength and direction of the currents are affected by landmasses, bottlenecks through narrow straits, and even the shape of the sea-bed. When the warm water reaches polar regions its heat evaporates into the atmosphere, reducing its temperature and increasing its density. When sea-water freezes it leaves salt behind in the unfrozen water and this cold water sinks into the ocean and begins to flow back to the tropics. Eventually it is heated and begins the cycle all over again."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7514> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Sea-level rises are a possible consequence of global warming. As the amount of free water in the oceans increases, and as the water becomes warmer, global warming will increase. In addition, according to theory, the heating at the poles may reduce the amount of water trapped in glaciers and ice caps."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7520> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The point, location or structure where effluent discharges into a body of marine waters such as a sea, ocean, etc."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7525> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Marine resources include food, energy and minerals."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7548> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The part of a country or region's economy that produces commodities without much direct use of natural resources."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7557> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Measures, techniques or designs implemented to protect from harm or restrict access to any apparatus, machinery or construction put in place or connected for use."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7566> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The movement and carrying- away of sediment by natural agents; especially the conveyance of a stream load by suspension, saltation, solution or traction."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7571> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The slow movement of water through small openings and spaces in the surface of unsaturated soil into or out of a body of surface or subsurface water."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7578> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The gathering of seismic data from an area."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7579> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A large seismically generated sea wave which is capable of considerable destruction in certain coastal areas, especially where submarine earthquakes occur. Although in the open ocean the wave height may be less than one meter it steepens to hights of 15 metres or more on entering shallow coastal water. The wavelength in the open ocean is of the order of 100 to 150 km and the rate of travel of a seismic sea wave is between 640 and 960 km/h."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7581> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The official or legally authorized act of taking away possessions or property, often for a violation of law or to enforce a judgment imposed by a court of law."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7595> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The interacting system of a biological community and its non-living environmental surroundings in regions that have between 10 to 20 inches of rainfall and are capable of sustaining some grasses and shrubs but not woodland."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7604> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A formalized procedure to identify the impact of changes in various model components on model output. Sensitivity analysis is an integral part of simulation experimentation and may influence model formulations. It is commonly used to examine model behaviour. The general procedure is to define a model output variable that represents an important aspect of model behaviour. The values of various inputs of the model are then varied and the resultant change in the output variable is monitored. Large changes in the output variable imply that the particular input varied is important in controlling model behaviour. Within this general definition, sensitivity analysis has been applied to a variety of model inputs including state variables, environmental variables and initial conditions."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7609> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The collection of individual components of solid waste from any source, usually separated into different collection containers, in order to recover, reuse or recycle the material or to facilitate its collection and disposal."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/760> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The care, preservation and husbandry of hymenopterous insects valued for their ability to pollinate crops and other flora or for their production of honey."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7612> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A machine for separating materials of different specific gravity by means of water or air."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7618> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The area served by a particular public facility such as school, library, police station, park, etc."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7621> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The carrying out of work for which there is a constant public demand by the provision of labor and the utilization of tools."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7628> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any liquid-born waste that contains animal or plant matter in suspension or solution, soils and storm water, or chemicals in solution."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/762> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any of the membranous-winged insects which compose the superfamily Apoidea in the order Hymenoptera characterized by a hairy body and by sucking and chewing mouthparts."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7630> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Area of land on which sewage or any other type of waste water is distributed in order to purify it; it is a kind of waste water treatment."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7636> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Sewage treatment comes in two stages - primary and secondary treatment. The primary stage involves a process of screening solids from sewage, leaving a sludge and relatively clear water for further treatment or for disposal into rivers, the sea or on to the land. In the secondary stage the sludge is stirred constantly in vast tanks to get more oxygen into the mixture, allowing bacteria to break down the organic matter and leave a harmless residue that falls as a sediment to the bottom of the tank. After processing, the clear water on top of the tank is discharged into rivers and the sediment is used as landfill or discharged at sea."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/764> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any insect of the order Coleoptera, having biting mouthparts and forewings modified to form shell-like protective elytra."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7651> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Barriers devised for keeping away from people harmful substances."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7663> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Discharging of ship waste into the sea."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7669> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A place, especially a small building, for the retail sale of goods and services."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7688> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any secondary effect, especially an undesirable one."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7699> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A very ductile malleable brilliant greyish-white element having the highest electrical and thermal conductivity of any metal. It occurs free and in argentite and other ores: used in jewellery, tableware, coinage, electrical contacts, and in electroplating. Its compounds are used in photography."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7709> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The process of choosing or picking a location or area for some designated purpose."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7715> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Gliding over snow on skis, especially as a sport."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7733> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "1) A soft, soupy, or muddy bottom deposit, such as found on tideland or in a stream bed. \n2) A semifluid, slushy, murky mass of sediment resulting from treatment of water, sewage, or industrial and mining wastes, and often appearing as local bottom deposits in polluted bodies of water."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7737> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A treatment to stabilize raw sludge. The treatment can be either anaerobic process or aerobic process."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7738> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A method used for drying and reducing sludge volume and weight. Since incineration requires auxiliary fuel to obtain and maintain high temperature and to evaporate the water contained in the incoming sludge, concentration techniques should be applied before incineration. Sludge incineration is a two-step process involving drying and combustion after a preceding dewatering process, such as filters, drying beds, or centrifuges."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7739> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Pond for the removal of settleable solids through which wastewater is passed in a treatment works."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/773> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The interacting system of the biological communities located at the bottom of bodies of freshwater and saltwater and their non-living environmental surroundings."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7740> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The processing of wastewater sludges to render them innocuous. This may be done by aerobic or anaerobic digestion followed by drying in sand beds, filtering, and incineration, filtering, and drying, or wet air oxidation."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7742> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Vertical sliding gate or valve to regulate the flow of water in a channel or lock."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7755> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Small enclosed structures containing a heat source, typically used for the purpose of intense heating. Most are lined with refractory material, the heat source is typically provided by electrical elements or the burning of gas, coke or coal."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7756> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A domestic source introducing small quantities of pollutants into a publicly owned waste-treatment system."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/775> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Those organisms attached to, living on, in or near the sea bed, river bed or lake floor."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7760> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Action, device or announcement that serves to give caution or notice to the level of air pollutants typically associated with oxidants in a given area."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7761> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "An aerosol, consisting of visible particles and gases, produced by the incomplete burning of carbon-based materials, such as wood and fossil fuels."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7765> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The inhalation and exhalation of carcinogenic fumes from burning plant material, usually tobacco."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7769> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The most common form of frozen precipitation, usually flakes or starlike crystals, matted ice needles, or combinations, and often rime-coated."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7771> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "An avalanche of relatively pure snow; some rock and earth material may also be carried downward."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7774> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Absorption of liquid by a solid or a semisolid material."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7791> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A concept associated with evolutionary theories of history and with structural functionalism. Societies are seen as moving from the simple to the complex via a process of social change based on structural differentiation."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7796> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A collection of people who interact with one another and share a certain feeling of unity."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7798> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Easily identified features of a society which can be measured, which vary over time, and are taken as revealing some underlying aspect of social reality. In general, the most commonly used indicators are derived from official statistics, and include unemployment figures, health and mortality data, and crime rates."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7805> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A organized effort by a significant number of people to change (or resist change in) some major aspect or aspects of society."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7807> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Collective, civic action shared and performed by a significant number of the community or general population."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7809> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A course of action adopted and pursued by government, business or some other organization, which seeks to ensure that all people have acceptable working or living conditions by providing social security, welfare, health care, insurance, fair employment practices, low cost housing or educational opportunities."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7818> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Data collections that employ both interviewing and sampling to produce quantitative data-sets, amenable to computer-based analysis."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7823> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Human group of people, more or less large and complex, associated for some common interest and characterized by distinctive hierarchical relationships."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7827> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Biotechnology is the application of biological and technical solutions to problems, and often refers to the industrial use of microorganisms (perhaps genetically altered) to perform chemical processing, for example of waste or water, or to manufacture hormones or enzymes for medicinal and commercial purposes. Biotechnology offers great potential to increase farm production and food processing efficiency, to lower food costs, to enhance food quality and safety and to increase international competitiveness."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7831> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The study of the development, organization, functioning and classification of human societies."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7844> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A naturally occurring process in humid climates that has long been the subject of research, whose findings suggest acid precipitation effects. The generally accepted impact of soil acidification on the productivity of terrestrial plants is summarised as follows: as soil becomes more acidic the basic cations (Ca, Mg) on the soil exchange are replaced by hydrogen ions or solubilized metals. The basic cation, now in solution, can be leached through the soil. As time progresses the soil becomes less fertile and more acidic. Resultant decreases in soil pH cause reduced, less-active population of soil microorganisms, which in turn slow decomposition of plant residues and cycling of essential plant nutrients."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7847> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The study of the living organisms, mainly microorganisms and microinvertebrates which live within the soil, and which are largely responsible for the decomposition processes vital to soil fertility."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7850> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "An increase in bulk density (mass per unit volume) and a decrease in soil porosity resulting from applied loads, vibration, or pressure. More compacted soils (or other materials) can support greater loads (load-bearing capacity). Bulk density can be increased by controlling the moisture content, compaction forces and treatment procedures, as well as by manipulating the type of material being compacted."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7852> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Management of soil to prevent or reduce soil erosion and depletion by wind and water. Preservation of soil against deterioration and loss by using it within its capabilities; application of conservation practices needed for its protection and improvement."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7853> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A binding rule or body of rules prescribed by a government to protect and prevent the loss of an area's surface layer of decomposed rock and organic material, valued for its nutrients and ability to support life."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7857> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Soil may deteriorate either by physical movement of soil particles from a given site or by depletion of the water-soluble elements in the soil which contribute to the nourishment of crop, plants, grasses, trees, and other economically usable vegetation. The physical movement generally is referred to as erosion. Wind, water, glacial ice, animals and tools in use may be agents of erosion."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7858> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Detachment and movement of topsoil or soil material from the upper part of the profile, by the action of wind or running water, especially as a result of changes brought about by human activity, such as unsuitable or mismanaged agriculture."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7863> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Process of protecting the soil from excessive erosion and making soil more fertile and productive."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7868> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A two-dimensional representation that shows the areal extent or the distribution of soils in relation to other features of the land surface."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/786> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A complete or selective listing of documents by a given subject, author or publisher, often including the description and identification of the editions, dates of issue, titles, authorship, publishers or other written materials."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7874> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "1) Water stored in soils.\n2) One of the most important elements involved in pedological processes and plant growth. There are three basic forms: a) water adhering in thin films by molecular attraction to the surface of soil particles and not available for plants is termed hygroscopic water. b) Water forming thicker films and occupying the smaller pore spaces is termed capillary water. Since it is held against the force of gravity it is permanently available for plant growth and it is this type of soil water which contains plant nutrients in solution. c) Water in excess of hygroscopic and capillary water is termed gravitational water, which is of a transitory nature because it flows away under the influence of gravity. When the excess has drained away the amount of water retained in the soil is termed its field capacity, when some of its pore spaces are still free of water."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7875> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The water regime of the soil is determined by the physical properties and arrangement of the soil particles. The pores in a soil determine its water-retention characteristics. When all the pores are full of water, the soil is said to be saturated."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7881> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The major processes in soils are gains, losses, transfers, and transformations of organic matter, soluble salts, carbonates, silicate clay minerals, sesquioxides, and silica. Gains consist normally of additions of organic matter, and of oxygen and water through oxidation and hydration, but in some sites slow continuous additions of new mineral materials take place at the surface or soluble materials are deposited from groundwater. Losses are chiefly of materials dissolved or suspended in water percolating through the profile or running off the surface."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7890> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The study of the properties, occurrence, and management of soil as a natural resource. Generally it includes the chemistry, microbiology, physics, morphology, and mineralogy of soils, as well as their genesis and classification."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7892> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Compaction involves the close-packing of the individual grains mainly by the elimination of pore-space and expulsion of entrapped water; this is normally brought about by the weight of the overlying sediments."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7895> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The combination or aggregation of primary soil particles into aggregates or clusters, which are separated from adjoining peds by surfaces of weakness. Soil structure is classified on the basis of size, shape, and distinctness into classes, types, and grades."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7896> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A sinking down of a part of the earth's crust, generally due to underground excavations."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7899> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A phase or subdivision of a soil series based primarily on texture of the surface soil to a depth at least equal to plow depth (about 15 cm)."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7904> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A device for converting sunlight into electrical power using a semiconductor sensitive to the photovoltaic effect. Solar cells are used on space satellites to power electronic equipment, and as their price falls they may come to be used to provide energy on the Earth."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7905> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Device which converts the energy from light into electricity. The collector system contains a concentrator and a receiver. The concentrator redirects and focuses sunlight on the receiver by using mirrors or lenses, and the receiver absorbs solar radiation and converts it to heat."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7908> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A domestic or industrial heating system that makes direct use of solar energy. The simplest form consists of a collector through which a fluid is pumped. The circuit also contains some form of heat storage tank and an alternative energy source to provide energy when the sun is not shining. The collector usually consists of a black surface through which water is piped, the black surface being enclosed behind glass sheets to make use of the greenhouse effect."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7912> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The electromagnetic radiation and particles emitted by the sun."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7918> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A crystalline material, that is, one in which the constituent atoms are arranged in a three-dimensional lattice, periodic in three independent directions."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7919> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The physical state of matter in which the constituent molecules, atoms, or ions have no translatory motion although they vibrate about the fixed positions that they occupy in a crystal lattice."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7926> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Solvent recovery is a widely practised form of recycling where spent solvents are distilled and reused. However, the cheaper solvents are often incinerated or dumped in hazardous waste landfill sites."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7936> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Diffusion into the environment of a sound emitted from a given source."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7938> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The sound pressure level (in decibels) at a point in a sound field, averaged over the audible frequency range and over a time interval."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7941> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Reducing or eliminating reverberation in a room by placing sound-absorbing materials on the walls and ceiling."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7948> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "An ocean south of the equator between the eastern coast of South America and the western coast of Africa that extends southward to the Antarctic continent, including the Drake Passage, South Sandwich Islands and Falkand Islands."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/794> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Waste oil that accumulates, usually in small quantities, inside the lower spaces of a ship, just inside the shell plating, and usually mixed with larger quantities of water."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7951> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A geographic region of the Asian continent bordered in the north by the countries of Central Asia and in the south by the Arabian Sea and the Bay of Bengal, extending  westward into Iran and eastward into China, including Afghanistan, Pakistan, India, Nepal, Bangladesh, Burma, Bhutan and Sri Lanka."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/795> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Water that builds up in the bottom of a ship's bilge."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7962> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Space extending between the sun and the planets of the solar system. Interplanetary space is not empty, but contains dust, particles with an electric charge, and the magnetic field of the sun (also called the IMF, or Interplanetary Magnetic Field)."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7972> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Nonfunctional debris of human origin left in a multitude of orbits about the earth as the result of the exploration and use of the environment lying outside the earth's atmosphere."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7974> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The rate of moves or migrations made by a given population within a given time frame."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7978> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "One relating to particular persons or things; one made for individual cases or for particular places or districts; one operating upon a selected class, rather than upon the public generally. A law is special when it is different from others of the same general kind or designed for a particular purpose, or limited in range or confined to a prescribed field of action or operation."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7983> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Controlled utilization, protection or development of selected classes of plants or animals for their richness, biodiversity and benefits to humanity."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7985> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Loss of species due to factors such as climate change or random events such as persistent drought, natural catastrophe, the emergence of a new predator, or genetic mutation."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/798> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "1) The accumulation of pollutants in living organisms by direct adsorption or through food chains. \n2) Accumulation by an organism of materials that are not an essential component or nutrient of that organism. Usually it refers to the accumulation of metals, but it can apply to bioaccumulation of persistent synthetic substances such as organochlorine compounds. Many organisms, such as plants, fungi and bacteria, will accumulate metals when grown in solutions containing them. The process can be employed usefully as a purification process to remove toxic heavy metals from waste water and contaminated land."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7994> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A scalar measure of the rate of movement of a body expressed either as the distance travelled divided by the time taken (average speed) or the rate of change of position with respect to time at a particular point (instantaneous speed). It is measured in metres per second, miles per hour, etc."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/7996> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The maximum permitted speed at which a vehicle may travel on certain roads."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/79> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "1) Something done voluntarily by a person, and of such a nature that certain legal consequences attach to it.\n2) Documents, decrees, edicts, laws, judgments, etc."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8000> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The uncontrolled discharge, leakage, dripping or running over of fluids or liquid substances."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8004> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Place where rubbish and waste minerals dug out of a mine are deposited."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/800> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Pollutants that become concentrated in living organisms through the consumption of food or water."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8019> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "An aerosol can for applying paint, deodorant, etc., as a fine spray."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8029> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Supplying water or pesticides to crops with a spray."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8032> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Settlement on land or property to which there is no legal title."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8036> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Ponds in which wastes are allowed to decompose over long periods of time and aeration is provided only by wind action. Sunlight is allowed to fall on sewage to purify it."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8037> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A building or structure usually with stalls that is used to house and feed horses, cattle or other animals."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8039> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The portion of a chimney rising above the roof."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8047> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "1) Something considered by an authority or by general consent as a basis of comparison.
2) An object regarded as the most common size or form of its kind.
3) A rule or principle that is used as a basis for judgment.
4) An average or normal quality, quantity, or level."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8048> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The act of conforming to a rule."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8056> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The most commonly or regularly eaten food in a country or community and which forms the mainstay of the total calorie supply, especially in the poorer populations and at times of food shortage."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8069> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A written account on the level of integrity and conditions of the ecosystem and natural resources in a given region, usually presented by an official person or body mandated to protect human health and the environment in that region."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8073> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A place along a route or line at which a bus, train, etc. stops for fuel or to pick up or let off passengers or goods, especially with ancillary buildings and services."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8074> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The body of techniques used in statistical inference concerning a population."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8076> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A branch of mathematics dealing with the collection, analysis, interpretation, and presentation of masses of numerical data."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8078> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The extent to which a society promotes human well-being in all dimensions of existence by forming people's capabilities, expanding choices and increasing opportunities."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8095> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "An act or process of destroying all forms of microbial life on and in an object."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8098> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Money or financial resources set aside to stimulate, encourage, or incite action towards greater productivity."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8099> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A group of individuals of one species within a specified area."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8102> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The counting over of materials or goods on hand, as in a stockroom or store."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8110> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A barrier of concrete, earth, etc., built across a river to create a body of water."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8117> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Storms may cause flooding and damage to crops; uproot trees; damage roofs and chimneys; break windows, leading to rain damage; overturn trucks; affect transportation, communication and energy supplies; delay building construction and destroy traditional landmarks. In their more violent form, storms may cause severe damage and loss of life."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8122> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A chamber within which a fuel-air mixture is burned to provide heat, the heat itself being radiated outward from the chamber; used for space heating, process-fluid heating, and steel blast furnaces."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8128> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The layer of the atmosphere which is sandwiched between the troposphere and mesosphere. Of the energy that reaches the Earth from the sun, only 3% is absorbed in the stratosphere, but that includes the vitally important process of absorption of ultraviolet radiation by the stratospheric ozone layer. The stratosphere is cloudless and dust free, and almost unaffected by the turbulent conditions of the underlying level of the atmosphere."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8133> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The quantitative determination of the rate and amount of flow or discharge from a natural body of running water, such as a small river or brook."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8141> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A stimulus or succession of stimuli of such magnitude as to tend to disrupt the homeostasis of the organism."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8144> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A soft silvery-white element of the alkaline earth group of metals, occurring chiefly as celestite and as strontianite. Its compounds burn with a crimson flame and are used in fire works."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8149> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Sound that travels over at least part of its path by means of the vibration of a solid structure."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8158> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "That aspect of geological oceanography which deals with the relief features of the ocean floor and with the forces that modify them."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8163> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "1) A sinking down of a part of the earth's crust, generally due to underground excavations.\n2) The sudden sinking or gradual downward settling of the Earth's surface with little or no horizontal motion. The movement is not restricted in rate, magnitude, or area involved. Subsidence may be caused by natural geologic processes, such as solution, thawing, compaction, slow crustal warping, or withdrawal of fluid lava from beneath a solid crust; or by man's activity, such as subsurface mining or the pumping of oil or ground water."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8168> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The removal of surplus water from within the soil by natural or artificial means, such as by drains placed below the surface to lower the water table below the root zone."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8173> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Halogenated compounds, because of their toxical and persistent character, should be substituted by environmental friendly compounds, like water-based fat solvents in metal processing industry or water-based coating agents."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8192> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any compound that includes one or more sulfur atoms with a more electropositive element, either carbon, metal or some other nonoxygen atom."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/819> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A community or natural assemblage of organisms; often used as an alternative to ecosystem but strictly is the fauna/flora association excluding physical aspects of the environment."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8204> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "An oxide of sulphur, such as sulphur dioxide and sulphur trioxide; they are formed primarily from the combustion of fossil fuels; major air pollutants and cause of damage to the respiratory tract as well as vegetation."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/820> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The quotient of the concentration of a chemical in aquatic organisms at a specific time or during a discrete time period of exposure, divided by the concentration in the surrounding water at the same time or during the same period."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8214> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "An appointed or official group given the responsibility of overseeing or managing normal work operations, special projects or other functions of an organization or agency."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8219> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The willingness and ability to sell a range of quantities of a good at a range of prices, during a given time period. Supply is one half of the market exchange process; the other is demand."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8225> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Water that travels over the soil surface to the nearest surface stream; runoff of a drainage basin that has not passed beneath the surface since precipitation."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8227> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any method of treating a material (metal, polymer, or wood) so as to alter the surface, rendering it receptive to inks, paints, lacquers, adhesives, and various other treatments, or resistant to weather or chemical attack."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8229> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "All waters on the surface of the Earth found in streams, rivers, ponds, lakes, marshes or wetlands, and as ice and snow."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/823> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A pollutant which can be converted by biological processes into simple inorganic molecules."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8255> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A sweetening agent, especially one that does not contain sugar."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8259> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A close and mutually beneficial association of organisms of different species."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8262> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Study of the ecology of organisms, populations, communities or systems."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8279> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Analysis or estimate noting similarities and differences in the operations of businesses and organizations."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8280> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The science concerned with the general study of structures and behaviours of systems which may be applicable in different branches of learning."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8283> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "In criminal law and torts, the act of laying hold upon an evidence, with or without removing the same."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8284> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A truck designed for bulk shipment of liquids or gases."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8285> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A ship designed for bulk shipment of liquids or gases."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8286> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Storage space for containers of liquids or gases."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8289> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "One of a group of complex organic chemicals commonly found in leaves, unripe fruits, and the bark of trees. Their function is uncertain though the unpleasant taste may discourage grazing animals. Some tannins have commercial uses, notably in the production of leather and ink; used in tanning, as a mordant in dyeing, and in ink manufacture."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/830> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The study of ethical problems arising from biological research and its applications in such fields as organ transplantation, genetic engineering, or artificial insemination."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8321> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A procedure, technique or system with definite plans for instruction or imparting knowledge."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8326> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Technical Guideline for Dangerous Substances: technical rules for handling dangerous materials."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8330> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Changing of industrial methods by introducing new technology."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8334> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any application of practical or mechanical sciences to industry or commerce capable of harming persons, property or the environment."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8340> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The approval, favorable reception and ongoing use of newly introduced devices and systems, usually developed from recent advances in the engineering sciences or industrial arts."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8342> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The transfer of development and design work: a) from a parent company to a subsidiary, perhaps in another nation where it will be paid for in repatriated profits or royalties; b) from one country to another as a form of aid to help promote development and sustainable growth. Many nations have made great progress on the strength of technology transfer."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8350> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The convergence of computing and communications technologies, thus the use of telephone or radio to link computers and the use of computers to send messages via telephone or radio links."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8361> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Mixed forest of conifers and broad-leaf deciduous trees, or mixed conifer and broad-leaf evergreen trees, or entirely broad-leaf deciduous, or entirely broad-leaf evergreen trees, found in temperate regions across the world; characterized by high rainfall, warm summers, cold winters occasionally subzero, seasonality; typically with dense canopies, understorey saplings and tall shrubs, large animals, carnivores dominant, very rich in bird species."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8362> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Forest dominated by broad-leaved hardwoods, which occurs over large tracts in the mid-latitudes of Europe, N. America, and eastern Asia, but which is restricted in the southern hemisphere to Chilean Patagonia."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8369> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Simple facilities for asylum or provisional lodgings to individuals or groups in emergencies."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/836> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The science concerned with the geographical distribution of animal and plant life."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8376> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The process whereby abnormalities of the offspring are generated, usually as the result of damage to the embryonal structure during the first trimester of pregnancy, producing deformity of the fetus."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8378> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The ability or tendency to produce anomalies of formation."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8401> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "An area that an animal or group of animals defends, mainly against members of the same species."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8403> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The part of a country or region's economy that produces services or assets lacking a tangible and storable form."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8405> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "To carry out an examination on (a substance, material, or system) by applying some chemical or physical procedure designed to indicate the presence of a substance or the possession of a property."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8422> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A material made of natural or man-made fibers and used for the manufacture of items such as clothing and furniture fittings."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8428> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Bluish-white metal with tinlike malleability, but a little softer; used in alloys."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/842> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Properties or features belonging to living organisms."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8434> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A political conception of government in a capitalist economy where the state is responsible for insuring that all members of society attain a minimum standard of living through redistribution of resources, progressive taxation and universal social programs, including health care and education."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8435> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The treatment of physical, mental or social disorders or disease."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8442> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The excessive raising or lowering of water temperature above or below normal seasonal ranges in streams, lakes, or estuaries or oceans as the result of discharge of hot or cold effluents into such water."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8446> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The concept of utilizing the temperature differences of 20°C or more that occur between the surface of an ocean and its depths to achieve a continuous supply of power; this temperature difference may be found in the tropical regions of the world. Various small plants have been constructed to demonstrate the principle."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8447> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "1) Heating and cooling a metal or alloy to obtain desired properties or conditions. \n2) Treatment of hazardous waste in a device which uses elevated temperatures as the primary means to change the chemical, physical, or biological character or composition of the hazardous waste. Examples of thermal treatment processes are incineration, molten salt, pyrolysis, calcination, wet air oxidation, and microwave discharge."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8450> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The branch of physics which seeks to derive, from a few basic postulates, relationships between properties of matter, especially those connected with temperature, and a description of the conversion of energy from one form to another."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8452> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Trade-Mark-Name for a thermic waste processing technology. Gasification is emerging as an alternative to combustion in the treatment and energy recovery from Municipal Solid Waste. Several innovative processes and demonstration plants are trying to achieve higher electrical efficiencies and lower emissions using this technology."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8454> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A compilation of terms showing synonyms, related terms and other relationships and dependencies, often used in a book format or as a standardized, controlled vocabulary for an information storage and retrieval system."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/846> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The action of growing of living organisms."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8475> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Mechanical power, which may be converted to electrical power, generated by the rise and fall of ocean tides. The possibilities of utilizing tidal power have been studied for many generations, but the only feasible schemes devised so far are based on the use of one or more tidal basins, separated from the sea by dams (known as barrages), and of hydraulic turbines through which water passes on its way between the basins and the sea."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8486> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Industry related with timber harvesting and processing."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8487> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "1) The dimension of the physical universe which, at a given place, orders the sequence of events. \n2) A designated instant in this sequence, as the time of day. Also known as epoch."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8490> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A metallic element, occurring in cassiterite, that has several allotropes; the ordinary malleable silvery-white metal slowly changes below 13.2°C to a grey powder. It is used extensively in alloys, especially bronze and pewter, and as a noncorroding coating for steel."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8494> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A part of an organism consisting of a large number of cells having a similar structure and function."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8496> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A white, water-insoluble powder that melts at 1560°C, and which is produced commercially from the titanium dioxide minerals ilmenite and rutile; used in paints and cosmetics."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8499> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any anuran amphibian of the class Bufonidae, such as Bufo bufo of Europe. They are similar to frogs but are more terrestrial, having a drier warty skin."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/84> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Chemical reaction in which one or more of the double bonds or triple bonds in an unsaturated compound is converted to a single bond by the addition of other atoms or groups."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8503> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The grey, brown, or blackish mixture of gases and suspended carbon particles resulting from the combustion of tobacco. Tobacco smoke is inhaled and distributes toxins widely throughout the body and causes an enormous variety of illness among users and among non-smokers exposed to tobacco smoke."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8521> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The sum of parameters that must be taken into account when assessing water quality (organoleptic factors, physico-chemical factors, toxic substances, microbiological parameters."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8522> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The temporary movement of people to destinations outside their normal places or work and residence, the activities undertaken during their stay in those destinations and the facilities created to cater for their needs."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8525> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "All the services connected with tourism, especially when regarded as an industry."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8540> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Metals (usually heavy metals) which interfere with the respiration, metabolism or growth of organisms."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8542> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Test for the determination of the inherent toxicity of a chemical."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8545> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any product which can cause acute or chronic injury to the human body or which is suspected of being able to cause disease or injury under some conditions."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8559> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A large group of plants characterized by the presence of specialized conducting tissues (xylem and phloem) in the roots, stems, and leaves."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8563> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The act or process of buying, selling or exchanging goods and services at either wholesale or retail, within a country or between countries."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8564> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Tradable emissions permits are used in an environmental regulatory scheme where the sources of the pollutant to be regulated (most often an air pollutant) are given permits to release a specified number of tons of the pollutant. The government issues only a limited number of permits consistent with the desired level of emissions. The owners of the permits may keep them and release the pollutants, or reduce their emissions and sell the permits. The fact that the permits have value as an item to be sold gives the owner an incentive to reduce their emissions."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8566> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The act or process of buying, selling, or exchanging commodities and the use of goods and services."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8569> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The act or the business of buying and selling for money. Mercantile or commercial business in general or the buying and selling, or exchanging, of commodities, either by wholesale or retail within a country or between countries."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/856> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A species or organism that is used to grade environmental quality or change."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8570> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Trade impacts on the environment can be direct, such as trade of endangered species, of natural resources, of natural products such as tropical timber, etc., or indirect, such as deforestation, loss of habitats, pollution from mining, from energy production, oil spills, global warming, etc., increases in transport infrastructures."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8571> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A course of action adopted and pursued by government, business or some other organization, which promotes or determines the direction for the act or process of buying, selling or exchanging goods and services within a country or between countries."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8574> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Commercial discrimination that apply to the exports of certain countries but not to similar goods from other countries."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8579> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Learned, nonrandom, systematic behavior and knowledge transmitted over several generations, especially customs and beliefs originating before the advent of modern science and technology."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8582> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "1) The movement of vehicles, ships, aircraft, persons, etc., in an area or over a route.\n2) The vehicles, persons, etc., moving in an area or over a route."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8586> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Means of controlling the number and speed of motorvehicles using a road."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8590> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The fundamental facilities and systems used for the movement of vehicles, often provided through public funding."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8592> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A number of vehicles so obstructed that they can scarcely move."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8596> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Noise emitted by vehicles (heavy vehicles, cars and motorcycles, tyre/road interaction)."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8606> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A connected group of railroad cars, usu. pushed or pulled by a locomotive."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8607> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The process of bringing a person or a group of persons to an agreed standard of proficiency, by practice and instruction."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8608> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Place where people are prepared for a specific purpose."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/861> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The direct measurement of changes in the biological status of a habitat, based on evaluations of the number and distribution of individuals or species before and after a change."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8633> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any commercial venture involved in the processes of conveying things or people from one place to another."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8641> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The act or means of moving tangible objects (persons or goods) from place to place. Often involves the use of some type of vehicle."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/865> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Viruses, bacteria, fungi, and mammal and bird antigens that may be present in the environment and cause many health effects."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8667> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "An area where trees, shrubs, or plants are grown for transplanting, for use as stocks for budding and grafting."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/866> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Disturbance of the ecological balance by the accidental or deliberate introduction of a foreign organism, animal or plant species into an environment."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8671> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The general drift, tendency, or bent of a set of statistical data as related to time or another related set of statistical data."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8683> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any of the feeding levels through which the passage of energy through an ecosystem proceeds; examples are photosynthetic plants, herbivorous animals, and microorganisms of decay."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8686> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The interacting system of a biological community and its non-living environmental surroundings in forests found in tropical regions near the equator, which are characterized by warm to hot weather and abundant rainfall."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8693> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The region of the earth's surface lying between two parallels of latitude on the earth, one 23°27' north of the equator and the other 23°27' south of the equator, representing the points farthest north and south at which the sun can shine directly overhead and constituting the boundaries of the Torrid Zone."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8696> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Tropospheric ozone is a secondary pollutant formed from emissions of nitrogen oxides, non-methane volatile organic compounds and carbon monoxide. Ozone scars lung tissue, makes eyes sting and throats itch. It has been implicated as a contributor to forest dieback, damage to agricultural crops, etc."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/86> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Additional packaging around the normal sales packaging. For example as protection against theft or for the purpose of advertising; the customer may leave the additional packaging in the shop for waste collection."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8721> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "An internal combustion engine whose cycle is completed in two strokes of the piston."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8722> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The class or category of an enterprise or organization involved in an economy."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8723> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A class or category of interests or remedies recognized in law or equity that create in the holder a right to the interest or its proceeds, typically taking the form of money, property or privilege."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8731> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A rubber ring placed over the rim of a wheel of a road vehicle to provide traction and reduce road shocks."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8736> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Separation of colloidal or very fine solid materials by filtration through microporous or semipermeable mediums."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/873> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Wild organisms harvested for subsistence, commerce, or recreation (such as fish, game, timber or furbearers); domesticated organisms raised by agriculture, aquaculture, and silviculture; and ecosystems cropped by livestock."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8758> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Storage located underground designed to hold gasoline or other petroleum products or chemical solutions."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/878> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Processes for removing impurities from waste gas based on the employing of microorganisms."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8791> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A metallic element highly toxic and radioactive; used as nuclear fuel."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8794> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A planned, coordinated group of activities or services intended for improving urban centers in order to provide healthy and safe living conditions, efficient transport and communication, adequate public facilities and aesthetic surroundings."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/879> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A generic term applied to processes that use microorganisms to decompose organic wastes either into water, carbon dioxide, and simple inorganic substances, such as aldehydes and acids. The purpose of biological waste treatment is to control either the environment for microorganisms so that their growth and activity are enhanced, and to provide a means for maintaining high concentrations of the microorganisms in contact with the wastes."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/87> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A polymer formed by the chain addition of unsaturated monomer molecules, such as olefins, with one another without the formation of a by-product, as water; examples are polyethylene, polypropylene and polystyrene."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8801> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Condition where part of a city or town becomes old or dirty or ruined, because businesses and wealthy families have moved away from it."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8805> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A binding rule or body of rules prescribed by government to regulate public services and the competing claims of residential, commercial and industrial interests in municipal areas generally characterized by moderate to high population density."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8815> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The complex of private and public gardens in an urban area."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8824> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The traits, patterns and structure of a city's specific geographic area, including its biological composition, its physical environment and its social patterns."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8826> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The administration, organization and planning performed for cities or towns, particularly the process of converting farmland or undeveloped land into offices, businesses, housing and other forms of development."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
