<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/882> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The production of light of various colors by living organisms (e.g. some bacteria and fungi, glow-worms and many marine animals). Luminescence is produced by a biochemical reaction, which is catalyzed by an enzyme. In some animals the light is used as a mating signal; in others it may be a protective device. In deep-sea forms luminous organs may serve as lanterns."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8833> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Pollution of highly populated areas mainly deriving from motor vehicles, industrial plants, combustion and heating plants, etc."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8839> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A continuing process of remodelling urban areas by means of rehabilitation and conservation as well as redevelopment. Urban renewal programmes are generally undertaken by public authorities and concern those parts of the city which have fallen below current standards of public acceptability."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/883> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Biomass refers strictly speaking to the total weight of all the living things in an ecosystem. However, it has come to refer to the amount of plant and crop material that could be produced in an ecosystem for making biofuels and other raw materials used in industry, for example."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8841> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A collection of dwellings located in an urban area."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8844> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The built-up components, the street system and the facilities which make up an urban unit."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8847> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Movements of vehicles and people within a city."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/885> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A renewable energy source that makes use of such biofuels as methane (biogas) generated by sewage, farm, industrial, or household organic waste materials. Other biofuels include trees grown in so-called \"energy forests\" or other plants, such as sugar cane, grown for their energy potential. Biomass energy relies on combustion and therefore produces carbon dioxide; its use would not, therefore, alleviate the greenhouse effect."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8866> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Recyclable material from discarded motor vehicle tyres."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8876> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The use of a source of supply from a municipal or regional area, which can be readily drawn upon when needed."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8887> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any low-lying land bordered by higher ground; especially an elongate, relatively large, gently sloping depression of the Earth's surface, commonly situated between two mountains or between ranges of hills or mountains, and often containing a stream with an outlet. It is usually developed by stream erosion, but may be formed by faulting."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/888> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The hybrid science involving the application of physical principles and methods to study and explain the structures of living organisms and the mechanics of life processes."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8892> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "An appraised, evaluated or estimated element or ingredient of a biological community and its non-living environmental surroundings."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8899> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A transparent surface coating which is applied as a liquid and then changes to a hard solid; all varnishes are solutions of resinous materials in a solvent."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8908> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Number of plants growing on a certain area of land."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/890> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A cyclically recurring pattern of physiological states in an organism or organ, such as alpha rhythm or circadian rhythm; believed by some to affect physical and mental states and behaviour."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8910> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Study of the relationships between plants and their environment."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8913> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "An edible, mixed glyceride oil derived from plants (fruit, leaves, and seeds), including cottonseed, linseed, tung, and peanut; used in food oils, shortenings, soaps, and medicine, and as a paint drying oil."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8920> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any of various herbaceous plants having parts that are used as food."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8922> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "1) The plants of an area considered in general or as communities, but not taxonomically; the total plant cover in a particular area or on the Earth as a whole. 2) The total mass of plant life that occupies a given area."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8925> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A community of plants or plant life that share distinguishable characteristics."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8931> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "An official periodical examination of an automobile, truck, boat, airplane or other means of conveyance to determine compliance in design or operation with legal standards for safety or pollution emissions."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8940> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The process of supplying or removing air, by natural or mechanical means, to or from any space; such air may or may not have been conditioned."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8946> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any chordate animal of the subphylum Vertebrata, characterized by a bony or cartilaginous skeleton and a well-developed brain: the group contains fishes, amphibians, reptiles, birds, and mammals."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/894> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Protected land and coastal areas that are approved under the Man and Biosphere programme (MAB) in conjunction with the Convention on International Trade in Endangered Species (CITES). Each reserve has to have an ecosystem that is recognized for its diversity and usefulness as a conservation unit. The reserves have at least one core area where there can be no interference with the natural ecosystem. A transition zone surrounds this and within it scientific research is allowed. Beyond this is a buffer zone which protects the whole reserve from agricultural, industrial and urban development. Biosphere reserves and buffer zones were regarded as examples of a new generation of conservation techniques."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8951> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The branch of medical practice which treats of the diseases and injuries of animals."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8955> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A long high bridge, usually held up by many arches, which carries a railway or a road over a valley or other similar area at a lower level."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/895> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Production, by synthesis or degradation, of a chemical compound by a living organism."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8967> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A group of houses and other buildings, such as a church, a school and some shops, which is smaller than a town, usually in the countryside."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8974> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The study of submicroscopic organisms known as viruses."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8976> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Submicroscopic agents that infect plants, animals and bacteria, and are unable to reproduce outside the tissues of the host. A fully formed virus consists of nucleic acid (DNA or RNA) surrounded by a protein and lipid (fat) coat. The nucleic acid of the virus interferes with nucleic acid-synthesizing mechanism of the host cell, organizing it to produce more viral nucleic acid. Viruses cause many diseases (e.g., mosaic diseases of many cultivated plants, myxomatosis, foot and mouth disease, the common cold, influenza, measles, poliomyelitis). Many plant viruses are transmitted by insects, some by eelworms. Animal viruses are spread by contact, droplet infection or by insect vectors and some are spread by the exchange of body fluids."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8977> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Energy dissipation and generation of stresses in a fluid by the distortion of fluid elements; quantitatively, when otherwise qualified, the absolute viscosity. Also known as flow resistance."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/898> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A combination of biology and technology. It is used to describe developments in the application of biological organisms for commercial and scientific purposes. So \"bio\" stands for biology and the science of life, and \"tech\" stands for technology, or the tools and techniques that the biotechnologists have in their workbox. Those tools and techniques include microorganisms and a range of methods for manipulating them, such as genetic engineering."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8992> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A special training for a regular occupation or profession, especially, one for which one is specially suited or qualified."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8995> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The property of a substance or substances to convert into vapor or gas without chemical change."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8999> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The ejection of solid, liquid, or gaseous material from a volcano."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/899> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The influence upon the environment of organisms owing to the presence and activities of other organisms, as distinct from a physical, abiotic, environmental factor."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/8> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A vehicle that has been discarded in the environment, urban or otherwise, often found wrecked, destroyed, damaged or with a major component part stolen or missing."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9008> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The total amount of refuse or unusable material that enters a process or system."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9019> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The Wadden sea is a shallow sea extending along the North Sea coasts of The Netherlands, Germany and Denmark. It is a highly dynamic ecosystem with tidal channels, sands, mud flats, salt marshes, beaches, dunes, river mouths and a transition zone to the North Sea, the offshore zone. Most parts of the Wadden Sea, in particular in The Netherlands and Lower Saxony, are sheltered by barrier islands and contain smaller or wider areas of intertidal flats. The present form of the Wadden Sea is the result of both natural forces and action by man. Twice a day, on average, 15 km3 of sea water enter the Wadden sea. With the water from the North Sea, large amount of sand and silt are imported which settle in places with little water movement. During low tides large parts of the Wadden Sea emerge. These so-called tidal flats cover about 2/3 of the tidal area and are one of its most characteristic features. Nowhere in the world can such a large unbroken stretch of tidal flats be found. They account for 60% of all tidal areas in Europe and North Africa."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/901> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A region of relatively uniform environmental conditions, occupied by a given plant community and its associated animal community."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9023> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A vertical construction made of stone, brick, wood, etc., with a length and height much greater than its thickness, used to enclose, divide or support."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9028> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A conflict or a state of hostility between two or more parties, nations or states, in which armed forces or military operations are used."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/902> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Intersection of corridors connecting patchy ecological communities. Species survival tends to be higher in patches that have higher connectivity."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9032> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Animal which has a body temperature that stays the same and does not change with the temperature of its surroundings."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9035> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any series of procedures and devices designed to detect sudden or potential threats to persons, property or the environment, often utilizing radar technology."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/903> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Measures taken to ensure that the biological and physical components of a biotope are in equilibrium by maintaining constant their relative numbers and features."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9042> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Exhaust or gaseous air given off by any industrial, manufacturing or chemical process."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9044> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "An investigation carried out to decide what arrangements are appropriate for dealing with different kinds of wastes."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9048> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The inventory of all waste produced or recovered during a certain time period, classified by type and quantity."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9051> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A grouping by type of unusable material left over from any process."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9054> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The periodic or on-demand removal of solid waste from primary source locations using a collection vehicle and followed by the depositing of this waste at some central facility or disposal site."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9058> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any specialized procedure or method used to transform refuse from one state, form or chemical composition into another."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9063> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Law that settles the rules concerning the disposal, recycling and treatment of wastes."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9065> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The amount of money incurred for the action of removing or getting rid of refuse or unwanted materials left over from a manufacturing process."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9074> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Heating and power production plant where fuel is provided from refuse."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9076> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Power station that functions with refuse-derived fuel."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9078> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The direct or indirect discharge of exhaust gas into the atmosphere."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9079> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Qualitative and quantitative analysis of exhaust gases emitted from vehicles, industrial plants, etc. in order to asses their composition."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9086> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The release of heat generated as a byproduct from industrial or power generation processes."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9087> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Waste heat applications include space heating and refrigeration in urban areas, thawing of ice-bound seaways, agricultural use to stimulate growth and to extend the growing season and in aquaculture to stimulate the growth of algae, shellfish, and other potential marine food sources."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9095> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Measures or techniques, including plans and directives, that reduce the amount of wastes generated. Examples of waste minimisation are environmentally-sound recycling and source reduction practices."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9106> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The process of obtaining materials or energy resources from waste."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9107> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A method of recovering wastes as resources which includes the collection, and often involving the treatment, of waste products for use as a replacement of all or part of the raw material in a manufacturing process."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9108> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Practices that reduce the amount of waste generated by a specific source through the redesigning of products or patterns of production or consumption."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9116> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Separating waste into different materials, such as glass, metal, paper, plastic, etc."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9119> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Transportation of wastes by means of special vehicles."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9125> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The incorporation of wastes into natural or artificial cycles, mainly in order to recover secondary raw materials or energy."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9127> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Used water, or water that is not needed, which is permitted to escape, or unavoidably escapes from canals, ditches, reservoirs or other bodies of water, for which the owners of these structures are legally responsible."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/912> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any of the warm-blooded vertebrates which make up the class Aves."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9133> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A binding rule or body of rules prescribed by a government to regulate the outflow and disposal of spent or used water from a home, community, farm or industry that contains dissolved or suspended matter."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9135> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The amount of spent or used water, often containing dissolved and suspended matter, that is found in a stream or some other body of water."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9138> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The state or condition of spent or used water that contains dissolved or suspended matter from a home, community farm or industry."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9139> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The act or process of lessening the volume of used or spent water that is discharged from homes, businesses or industries."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9140> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The removed materials resulting from physical, biological and chemical treatment of waste water."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9144> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Plant where, through physical-chemical and biological processes, organic matter, bacteria, viruses and solids are removed from residential, commercial and industrial wastewaters before they are discharged in rivers, lakes and seas."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9151> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any mass of water having definite hydrological, physical, chemical and biological characteristics and which can be employed for one or several purposes."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9159> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The protection, development and efficient management of water resources for beneficial purposes."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9160> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The utilization patterns and quantities entailed in a community or human group's use of water for survival, comfort and enjoyment."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9161> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A natural stream arising in a given drainage basin but not wholly dependent for its flow on surface drainage in its immediate area, flowing in a channel with a well-defined bed between visible banks or through a definite depression in the land, having a definite and permanent or periodic supply of water, and usually, but not necessarily, having a perceptible current in a particular direction and discharging at a fixed point into another body of water."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9165> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The system of pipes supplying water to communities and industries."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9169> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Pumping of water for different purposes (i.e. agriculture, land reclamation, domestic and industrial use, etc.)."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9178> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Consumptive water use starts with withdrawal, but in this case without any return, e.g. irrigation, steam escaping into the atmosphere, water contained in final products, i.e. it is no longer available directly for subsequent use."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9183> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Aquatic birds which constitute the order Anseriformes, including the swans, ducks, geese, and screamers."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9186> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Floating aquatic plant, Eichornia crassipes of tropical America, having showy bluish-purple flowers and swollen leafstalks: family Pontederiaceae. It forms dense masses in rivers, ponds, etc., and is a serious pest in the southern U.S., Java, Australia, New Zealand, and parts of Africa."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9190> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The level reached by the surface of a body of water."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9195> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Measures taken to ensure an adequate supply of water and a responsible utilization of water resources."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/91> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The measurement of the amount of any chemical substance that can be safely consumed by a human being in a day. Calculations are usually based on the maximum level of a substance that can be fed to animals without producing any harmful effects. This is divided by a \"safety factor\" to allow for the differences between animals and humans and to take account of the variation in human diets."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9202> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The manmade or man-induced alteration of the chemical, physical, biological and radiological integrity of water."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9203> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Precautionary measures, actions or installations implemented to avert or hinder human-made or human-induced alteration of the physical, biological, chemical and radiological integrity of water."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9206> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Measures to conserve surface and groundwater; to ensure the continued availability of water for growing domestic, commercial and industrial uses and to ensure sufficient water for natural ecosystems."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9210> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any of several processes in which undesirable impurities in water are removed or neutralized."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9214> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A graded value of the components (organic and inorganic, chemical or physical) which comprise the nature of water."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9217> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The administration or handling of the amount of available potable water."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/921> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A generic term applied to natural inflammable substances of variable colour, hardness, and volatility, composed principally of a mixture of hydrocarbons substantially free from oxygenated bodies. Bitumens are sometimes associated with mineral matter, the nonmineral constituents being fusible and largely soluble in carbon disulfide, yielding water-insoluble sulfonation products. Petroleum, asphalts, natural mineral waxes, and asphaltites are all considered bitumens."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9220> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The power of a government agency or its administrators to administer and implement regulations, laws and government policies relating to the preservation and protection of water resources."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9223> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Controlled utilization or protection of any supply of water so that it is potentially useful for some purpose, such as for an economic, recreational or life-sustaining purpose."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9227> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Use of process wastewater or treatment facility effluent in a different manufacturing process."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9230> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Management of water resources aiming at ensuring the continued availability of water for human uses and natural ecosystems."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9235> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The dividing line between two adjacent river systems, such as a ridge."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9236> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any physical extension of, or changes to, the uses of land in waterfront areas."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9242> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Common liquid (H2O) which forms rain, rivers, the sea, etc., and which makes up a large part of the bodies of organisms."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9254> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A river, canal, or other navigable channel used as a means of travel or transport."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9255> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A well sunk to extract water from a zone of saturation."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9257> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Plant for treating and purifying water before it is pumped into pipes for distribution to houses, factories, schools, etc."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9259> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Power extracted from the motion of sea waves at the coast."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9267> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "An instrument of attack or defense in combat, as a gun, missile, or sword."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9274> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The changing of natural weather phenomena by technical means."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9276> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The periodic or continuous surveillance or analysis of the state of the atmosphere and climate, including variables such as temperature, moisture, wind velocity and barometric pressure."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9278> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The act or process of predicting and highlighting meteorological conditions that are expected for a specific time period and for a specific area or portion of air space, by using objective models based on certain atmospheric parameters, along with the skill and experience of a meteorologist."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9298> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Ecosystems of areas largely inundated with water but offering elevated lands as a habitat for wildlife. This areas include swamps, both seasonal and permanent, marsh, open fresh water, shallow saline lagoons, the estuaries of rivers, floodplains and coastal sand dunes. They provide food, breeding grounds, water and sanctuary for many forms of fish, birds and other animal and plant life. They are among the most productive ecosystems producing timber, peat moss and crops such as rice and a variety of berries."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9299> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Process used to remove particulate matter and/or gaseous pollutants by means of an aqueous stream or slurry."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9300> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "1) An air cleaning device that literally washes out the dust. Exhaust air is forced into a spray chamber, where fine water particles cause the dust to drop from the air stream. The dust-ladden water is then treated to remove the solid material and is often recirculated.\n2) Equipment through which a gas is passed to remove impurities (solid, liquid, or gaseous particles) by intimate contact with a suitable liquid, usually an aqueous medium."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9301> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Organic refuse or material left over from a manufacturing process, which is characterized by the presence of moisture."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9302> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Large marine mammals of the order Cetacea; the body is streamlined, the broad flat tail is used for propulsion, and the limbs are balancing structures."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9323> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Plants growing in a natural state (not cultivated)."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9327> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The motion of air relative to the earth's surface; usually means horizontal air motion, as distinguished from vertical motion."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/934> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "1) Removing colored components from a textile. Common bleaches are hydrogen peroxide, sodium hypochloride, and sodium chlorite. \n2) The brightening and delignification of pulp by the addition of oxidizing chemicals such as chlorine or reducing chemicals such as sodium hypochloride."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9352> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The permanent clear-felling of an area of forest or woodland. On steep slopes this can lead to severe soil erosion, especially where heavy seasonal rains or the melting of snow at higher levels cause sudden heavy flows of water. In the humid tropics it may also lead to a release of carbon dioxide from the soil."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9353> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "The interacting system of a biological community and its non-living environmental surroundings in wooded areas or land areas covered with trees and shrubs."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9362> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Waste which is left over after the processing of raw timber."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9363> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A textile fiber made from raw wool characterized by absorbency, resiliency and insulation."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9367> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A mine where all the mineral that could be profitably exploited has been removed."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9375> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Any or all locations or environments where people are employed."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9389> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Accounting procedure that is used when an asset is uncollectible and is therefore charged-off as a loss."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9395> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "A substance which would not normally be found in a given environment, and usually means a toxic chemical which is entirely artificial, such as a chlorinated aromatic compound or an organomercury compound."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9404> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Profit or income created through an investment or a business transaction."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .

<http://www.eionet.europa.eu/gemet/concept/9417> <http://www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#definition> "Designation and reservation under a master plan of land use for light and heavy industry, dwellings, offices, and other buildings; use is enforced by restrictions on types of buildings in each zone."@en <urn:graph-verity:gemet:4.2.3> .
